ISO27-001.title: ISMS Project Charter
ISO27-001.content:
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | [ISMS-PLAN-001] |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | [Chief Information Security Officer / ISMS Manager] |
| Effective Date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Framework | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 |
| Control Reference | Clause 5.1 — Leadership and Commitment |
| Classification | Internal |

## Purpose & Objectives

This ISMS Project Charter formally authorises the implementation of an Information Security Management System (ISMS) aligned to ISO/IEC 27001:2022. It establishes the leadership mandate, project sponsorship, implementation scope, governance approach, resourcing, budget authority, timeline, and expected outcomes for the organisation’s ISO/IEC 27001:2022 implementation.

This Charter supports ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Clause 5.1 by demonstrating that top management provides leadership and commitment to the ISMS by:

- Ensuring the information security policy and information security objectives are established and compatible with the strategic direction of the organisation.
- Ensuring integration of ISMS requirements into organisational processes.
- Ensuring that resources needed for the ISMS are available.
- Communicating the importance of effective information security management and conformity with ISMS requirements.
- Ensuring the ISMS achieves its intended outcomes.
- Directing and supporting personnel to contribute to ISMS effectiveness.
- Promoting continual improvement.
- Supporting management roles relevant to information security.

The objectives of this project are to:

1. Establish, implement, maintain, and prepare for certification of an ISMS conforming to ISO/IEC 27001:2022.
2. Define and approve the ISMS scope, including organisational units, locations, technologies, information assets, business processes, and interfaces with interested parties.
3. Conduct a formal information security risk assessment and risk treatment process aligned to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.
4. Develop and approve the Statement of Applicability, including control applicability decisions for ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A controls.
5. Implement required governance, risk management, operational, technical, and assurance activities necessary to meet ISO/IEC 27001:2022 requirements.
6. Establish measurable information security objectives and performance monitoring mechanisms.
7. Conduct internal audit and management review prior to external certification assessment.
8. Demonstrate visible executive sponsorship and sustained leadership commitment throughout ISMS implementation and operation.

The authorised sponsor for this initiative is [Executive Sponsor Role], acting on behalf of top management. The designated ISMS implementation owner is [ISMS Manager Role].

## Scope

The scope of this Charter covers the project to implement an ISMS in accordance with ISO/IEC 27001:2022. The intended ISMS scope will be formally documented in the ISMS Scope Statement and approved by top management during the initiation phase.

The provisional implementation scope includes:

| Scope Area | Included |
|---|---|
| Organisation | [Organisation Name] |
| Business units | [Business Units / Departments] |
| Locations | [Physical Locations / Remote Workforce / Data Centres] |
| Services / products | [In-Scope Services, Products, Platforms] |
| Core processes | Governance, risk management, asset management, access management, supplier management, incident management, business continuity coordination, security monitoring, compliance management |
| Information types | Customer information, employee information, corporate records, financial information, operational data, intellectual property, credentials, logs, security records |
| Technology environment | [Cloud Platforms], [SaaS Applications], [Identity Provider], [Endpoint Fleet], [Network Infrastructure], [Business Applications] |
| Interested parties | Customers, employees, regulators, suppliers, service providers, shareholders/owners, auditors, certification body |
| External dependencies | Managed service providers, cloud service providers, software vendors, professional services, legal/regulatory advisers |

The project includes the following ISO/IEC 27001:2022 management system requirements:

- Context of the organisation and interested party requirements.
- ISMS scope definition.
- Leadership commitment and governance.
- Information security policy and supporting policies.
- Organisational roles, responsibilities, and authorities.
- Risk assessment and risk treatment methodology.
- Information security objectives and planning.
- Competence, awareness, and communication.
- Documented information management.
- Operational planning and control.
- Performance evaluation, monitoring, measurement, analysis, and evaluation.
- Internal audit.
- Management review.
- Nonconformity management and continual improvement.

The project also includes evaluation and implementation planning for ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A controls, including organisational, people, physical, and technological controls, as determined by the risk treatment process and Statement of Applicability.

Out of scope for this Charter unless formally approved by the sponsor:

- Certification or attestation against frameworks other than ISO/IEC 27001:2022.
- Full remediation of legacy systems not included in the approved ISMS scope.
- Replacement of major business platforms unless required by approved risk treatment plans.
- Expansion of the ISMS to additional legal entities, subsidiaries, or international locations not listed in the approved ISMS Scope Statement.
- Implementation of customer-specific security requirements not mapped to the approved ISMS scope, unless separately authorised.

## Assumptions & Dependencies

The implementation plan is based on the following assumptions:

| Assumption | Impact if Invalid | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Top management will provide visible sponsorship and timely decisions. | Delayed approvals, reduced organisational adoption, weak evidence for Clause 5.1. | Executive Sponsor |
| Required personnel will be available to participate in workshops, risk assessments, control design, remediation, and audits. | Delays in ISMS implementation and incomplete evidence. | Department Heads |
| Existing business processes can be adapted to include ISMS requirements rather than replaced wholesale. | Increased cost and project complexity. | ISMS Manager |
| Key technology and process owners can provide accurate asset, system, process, and supplier information. | Incomplete scope, risk assessment, or Statement of Applicability. | Asset and Process Owners |
| Budget will be approved for tooling, advisory support, training, audit, and remediation activities. | Inability to implement or evidence required controls. | Executive Sponsor / Finance |
| External certification audit dates will be available within the target timeline. | Certification target date may move. | ISMS Manager |
| Existing security controls and documentation can be reused where appropriate. | Increased documentation and implementation effort. | Control Owners |

The following dependencies are critical to successful delivery:

| Dependency | Description | Required By | Responsible Party |
|---|---|---|---|
| Executive mandate | Formal approval of this Charter and project authority. | Project initiation | Top Management |
| ISMS scope decision | Agreement on organisational, technical, physical, and service boundaries. | Risk assessment and certification planning | Executive Sponsor / ISMS Manager |
| Risk assessment methodology | Approved method for evaluating information security risks and risk acceptance criteria. | Risk assessment phase | ISMS Manager / Risk Owner |
| Asset and process inventory | Current list of in-scope assets, systems, processes, information types, and owners. | Risk assessment and control mapping | IT, Operations, Business Owners |
| Legal and regulatory input | Identification of applicable legal, statutory, regulatory, and contractual obligations. | Context analysis and control selection | Legal / Compliance |
| Budget approval | Funding for implementation activities, tooling, consultants, training, internal audit, and certification. | Project execution | Executive Sponsor / Finance |
| Internal audit capability | Qualified internal auditor or independent audit provider. | Pre-certification assurance | ISMS Manager |
| Certification body engagement | Selection and scheduling of accredited certification body. | Stage 1 and Stage 2 audit | ISMS Manager / Procurement |
| Remediation capacity | Availability of control owners to address gaps and nonconformities. | Implementation and audit readiness | Department Heads |

## Approach / Phases

The ISMS implementation will follow a structured project lifecycle designed to establish effective governance, implement ISO/IEC 27001:2022 requirements, generate objective evidence, and prepare the organisation for certification.

### Phase 1 — Initiation and Leadership Mandate

This phase establishes formal authority, sponsorship, governance, and project controls.

Key activities:

- Approve this ISMS Project Charter.
- Appoint the Executive Sponsor, ISMS Manager, risk owners, control owners, and project working group.
- Confirm top management expectations for the ISMS, including certification intent.
- Define project governance, escalation paths, reporting cadence, and decision forums.
- Confirm budget parameters and procurement requirements.
- Communicate project launch and leadership commitment to relevant personnel.

Expected outputs:

- Approved ISMS Project Charter.
- Project governance structure.
- Initial stakeholder register.
- Project communication plan.
- Confirmed sponsor and ISMS leadership roles.

### Phase 2 — Context, Scope, and Planning

This phase determines the organisational context and defines the boundaries of the ISMS.

Key activities:

- Identify internal and external issues relevant to information security.
- Identify interested parties and their information security requirements.
- Define and approve the ISMS scope.
- Identify applicable legal, regulatory, contractual, and business requirements.
- Establish information security policy principles.
- Establish information security objectives aligned with strategic direction.
- Define documented information requirements.
- Confirm project plan, budget, and resource allocation.

Expected outputs:

- Context and interested parties analysis.
- Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements register.
- Approved ISMS Scope Statement.
- Draft or approved Information Security Policy.
- Information security objectives.
- Document register and evidence plan.

### Phase 3 — Risk Assessment and Statement of Applicability

This phase establishes the risk-based foundation for the ISMS and determines applicable controls.

Key activities:

- Approve the information security risk assessment and risk treatment methodology.
- Identify in-scope assets, information types, processes, systems, and owners.
- Conduct risk assessments with business and technology stakeholders.
- Define risk acceptance criteria and assign risk ownership.
- Select risk treatment options.
- Map risk treatments to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A controls and other relevant controls.
- Develop the Statement of Applicability.
- Obtain management approval for residual risks and risk treatment plans.

Expected outputs:

- Risk assessment methodology.
- Asset and process inventory.
- Risk register.
- Risk treatment plan.
- Statement of Applicability.
- Approved risk acceptance records.

### Phase 4 — ISMS Design and Control Implementation

This phase implements required management system processes and selected controls.

Key activities:

- Develop or update ISMS policies, standards, procedures, plans, and records.
- Implement organisational controls, including access governance, asset ownership, supplier security, incident management, and change management alignment.
- Implement people controls, including screening, terms and conditions, security awareness, disciplinary process alignment, and role-based competence.
- Implement physical controls applicable to in-scope facilities and assets.
- Implement technological controls, including identity and access management, logging, vulnerability management, secure configuration, backup, endpoint protection, network security, encryption, and secure development where applicable.
- Establish operational monitoring and evidence collection.
- Conduct training and awareness activities.
- Track and report implementation progress and risks.

Expected outputs:

- Approved ISMS documentation set.
- Control implementation evidence.
- Training and awareness records.
- Supplier security records.
- Access review evidence.
- Vulnerability and remediation records.
- Incident response and business continuity integration records.
- Updated risk treatment plan.

### Phase 5 — Performance Evaluation and Internal Assurance

This phase evaluates ISMS effectiveness and readiness for external certification.

Key activities:

- Monitor and measure information security objectives and control performance.
- Conduct ISMS internal audit covering ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clauses and applicable Annex A controls.
- Record audit findings, nonconformities, observations, and improvement opportunities.
- Conduct management review with top management.
- Evaluate progress against intended ISMS outcomes.
- Confirm adequacy of resources and ongoing leadership commitment.
- Approve corrective action plans.

Expected outputs:

- Monitoring and measurement results.
- Internal audit plan and report.
- Corrective action register.
- Management review minutes and decisions.
- Updated risk register and treatment plan.
- Audit readiness assessment.

### Phase 6 — Certification Readiness and External Audit Support

This phase prepares the organisation for certification assessment and supports audit activities.

Key activities:

- Select and contract an accredited certification body.
- Prepare evidence repository and audit logistics.
- Conduct Stage 1 readiness review.
- Address Stage 1 findings or concerns.
- Conduct Stage 2 certification audit.
- Respond to audit findings and nonconformities.
- Submit corrective action evidence as required.
- Transition project governance into ongoing ISMS operational governance.

Expected outputs:

- Certification audit schedule.
- Stage 1 audit evidence and findings response.
- Stage 2 audit evidence and findings response.
- Certification decision or corrective action plan.
- ISMS operational governance handover.
- Continual improvement backlog.

## Milestones & Timeline

The target implementation timeline is [6–12 months], subject to scope complexity, resource availability, remediation effort, and certification body scheduling.

| Milestone | Key Deliverables | Target Date | Approval / Acceptance Authority | Status |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Charter approved and project launched | Approved ISMS Project Charter, sponsor appointment, project governance confirmed | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Executive Sponsor | Planned |
| ISMS scope approved | ISMS Scope Statement, context analysis, interested parties register | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Top Management | Planned |
| Information security policy approved | Information Security Policy and communication plan | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Top Management | Planned |
| Risk methodology approved | Risk assessment methodology and risk acceptance criteria | [YYYY-MM-DD] | ISMS Steering Committee | Planned |
| Risk assessment completed | Risk register, asset/process inventory, risk owner assignments | [YYYY-MM-DD] | ISMS Manager / Risk Owners | Planned |
| Statement of Applicability approved | Statement of Applicability with control inclusion/exclusion rationale | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Executive Sponsor / ISMS Manager | Planned |
| Risk treatment plan approved | Risk treatment plan, residual risk approvals, budgeted remediation actions | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Risk Owners / Top Management | Planned |
| Core ISMS documentation approved | Policies, procedures, records, document control framework | [YYYY-MM-DD] | ISMS Manager | Planned |
| Control implementation substantially complete | Evidence for selected Annex A controls and operational processes | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Control Owners | Planned |
| Awareness and role-based training completed | Training records, competence evidence, communications | [YYYY-MM-DD] | HR / ISMS Manager | Planned |
| Internal audit completed | Internal audit report, nonconformity records, corrective action plans | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Internal Auditor / ISMS Manager | Planned |
| Management review completed | Management review minutes, decisions, improvement actions, resource decisions | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Top Management | Planned |
| Stage 1 certification audit completed | Stage 1 audit report and response to findings | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Certification Body / ISMS Manager | Planned |
| Stage 2 certification audit completed | Stage 2 audit report, nonconformity responses if applicable | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Certification Body / Executive Sponsor | Planned |
| Project closure and ISMS operational handover | Closure report, operational governance schedule, continual improvement backlog | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Executive Sponsor | Planned |

## Roles & Responsibilities

Top management retains ultimate accountability for ensuring the ISMS is established, implemented, maintained, resourced, and continually improved. Responsibilities must be assigned to competent individuals and communicated to relevant personnel.

| Role | Responsibilities | Authority |
|---|---|---|
| Top Management | Demonstrate leadership and commitment to the ISMS; approve ISMS strategic direction, policy, objectives, scope, resource allocation, major risk acceptance, and management review outcomes; ensure ISMS integration into business processes. | Approve ISMS direction, resources, risk acceptance thresholds, and major decisions. |
| Executive Sponsor | Provide executive mandate for the ISO/IEC 27001:2022 implementation; remove organisational barriers; approve project funding; chair or sponsor steering meetings; escalate decisions to top management. | Authorise budget, prioritisation, escalations, and project changes within delegated authority. |
| ISMS Manager | Lead ISMS implementation; coordinate ISO/IEC 27001:2022 requirements; maintain project plan; manage documentation; coordinate risk assessment, Statement of Applicability, internal audit, management review, and certification readiness. | Direct project activities, request evidence, coordinate control owners, and escalate risks/issues. |
| ISMS Steering Committee | Provide cross-functional oversight; review progress, risks, issues, budget, and resourcing; make implementation decisions; support adoption across departments. | Approve project-level decisions and recommend executive decisions. |
| Risk Owners | Own assigned information security risks; participate in assessment; approve treatment plans; accept residual risks within authority; ensure risk responses are implemented. | Accept or escalate risk decisions according to risk acceptance criteria. |
| Control Owners | Design, implement, operate, and evidence assigned controls; report control performance; remediate control gaps and audit findings. | Implement control activities and require supporting actions from process participants. |
| Process Owners | Ensure ISMS requirements are embedded into business processes; provide process documentation and evidence; support impact assessment and change adoption. | Approve process changes within business area. |
| IT / Security Team | Implement technical and operational security controls; provide security monitoring, access management, vulnerability management, backup, logging, incident response, and configuration evidence. | Execute approved technical controls and security operations. |
| Legal / Compliance | Identify legal, statutory, regulatory, and contractual information security requirements; support compliance obligations register; review policy and contractual implications. | Advise on obligations and approve compliance interpretations. |
| Human Resources | Support competence, awareness, disciplinary process alignment, onboarding/offboarding controls, role changes, and personnel-related records. | Implement HR-related ISMS controls and maintain personnel evidence. |
| Procurement / Vendor Management | Support supplier risk management, contractual security requirements, vendor due diligence, and third-party assurance evidence. | Enforce supplier onboarding and contractual security requirements. |
| Internal Auditor | Conduct independent internal audit of the ISMS; report conformity, nonconformities, and improvement opportunities; verify corrective actions where assigned. | Access relevant records and personnel; issue audit findings. |
| Employees and Contractors | Follow approved information security policies and procedures; complete required training; report incidents, weaknesses, and nonconformities. | Raise security concerns and improvement suggestions. |
| Certification Body | Conduct independent Stage 1 and Stage 2 certification audits against ISO/IEC 27001:2022. | Issue audit conclusions and certification recommendation in accordance with accreditation rules. |

The following governance forums will be used:

| Forum | Frequency | Chair | Purpose | Required Outputs |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| ISMS Steering Committee | Monthly during implementation | Executive Sponsor or delegate | Review project status, risks, decisions, budget, and resourcing. | Meeting minutes, action log, decisions. |
| ISMS Working Group | Weekly or biweekly during active implementation | ISMS Manager | Coordinate workstreams, control implementation, evidence collection, and issue resolution. | Action tracker, evidence status, issue log. |
| Risk Review Workshops | As scheduled during risk assessment and treatment | ISMS Manager | Assess risks, validate risk owners, agree treatment plans. | Risk register updates, treatment actions. |
| Management Review | At least before certification and thereafter at planned intervals | Top Management | Evaluate ISMS suitability, adequacy, effectiveness, resources, changes, risks, opportunities, and improvement needs. | Management review minutes and decisions. |

## Resources

Top management will ensure that sufficient resources are available for the establishment, implementation, maintenance, and continual improvement of the ISMS.

### Human Resources

| Resource Type | Expected Requirement | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| Executive Sponsor | [2–4 hours/month] | Decision-making, sponsorship, escalation, resource approval. |
| ISMS Manager | [0.5–1.0 FTE during implementation] | Day-to-day programme leadership and ISMS coordination. |
| Security / IT Control Owners | [4–12 hours/week during implementation] | Technical control design, implementation, and evidence. |
| Business Process Owners | [2–6 hours/month] | Scope validation, process mapping, risk assessment, control embedding. |
| Legal / Compliance | [2–6 hours/month] | Obligations mapping, policy review, supplier and regulatory input. |
| HR | [2–6 hours/month] | Awareness, competence, onboarding/offboarding control support. |
| Procurement / Vendor Management | [2–6 hours/month] | Supplier control implementation and evidence collection. |
| Internal Auditor | [5–15 audit days] | Internal audit planning, execution, reporting, and follow-up. |
| External Consultant, if used | [Variable] | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 advisory, gap assessment, documentation support, readiness review. |

### Budget

The project budget will be approved and tracked by the Executive Sponsor in coordination with Finance. Budget allocations should cover the following categories:

| Budget Category | Description | Estimated Amount |
|---|---|---:|
| ISMS advisory support | Gap assessment, implementation advisory, documentation support, certification readiness support | [Amount / Currency] |
| Certification body fees | Stage 1 audit, Stage 2 audit, auditor travel if applicable, annual surveillance audits | [Amount / Currency] |
| Internal audit | Independent internal audit provider or internal auditor training and time allocation | [Amount / Currency] |
| Security tooling | GRC tooling, vulnerability management, logging/SIEM, endpoint security, IAM, awareness training platform, evidence repository, as required | [Amount / Currency] |
| Training and awareness | ISO/IEC 27001 training, role-based security training, internal auditor training, employee awareness | [Amount / Currency] |
| Control remediation | Technical remediation, process improvements, supplier assurance, documentation updates, physical security enhancements | [Amount / Currency] |
| Legal and compliance support | Contract review, regulatory mapping, privacy/security advisory as required | [Amount / Currency] |
| Contingency | Reserved for unplanned remediation, audit follow-up, or scope changes | [Amount / Currency] |

### Tools and Infrastructure

The following tools or repositories will be used or established to support ISMS implementation:

| Tool / Repository | Purpose | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| ISMS document repository | Controlled storage of ISMS policies, procedures, plans, records, and audit evidence. | ISMS Manager |
| Risk register | Record of assessed risks, risk owners, treatment decisions, residual risk, and review dates. | ISMS Manager / Risk Owners |
| Statement of Applicability repository | Record of Annex A control applicability, implementation status, and justification. | ISMS Manager |
| Corrective action register | Tracking nonconformities, corrective actions, owners, due dates, and closure evidence. | ISMS Manager |
| Ticketing / work management system | Track implementation actions, remediation tasks, and evidence collection. | ISMS Manager / IT |
| Training platform | Deliver and evidence security awareness and role-based training. | HR / ISMS Manager |
| Security operations tools | Support logging, monitoring, access control, vulnerability management, backup, endpoint security, and incident management. | IT / Security Team |

### Authority and Funding Controls

- The Executive Sponsor is authorised to approve expenditures within the approved ISMS project budget.
- Budget changes exceeding [Threshold Amount / Percentage] require approval from [Approval Authority].
- Scope changes that materially affect certification boundaries, timeline, budget, or risk posture require approval by the ISMS Steering Committee and, where significant, top management.
- Risk treatment actions requiring capital expenditure must be supported by risk justification and approved through normal financial governance.

## Success Metrics

The project will be considered successful when the ISMS is established, implemented, operating, and ready for certification against ISO/IEC 27001:2022, with evidence of leadership commitment and effective governance.

Success metrics include:

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Charter approval | Approved by top management before project launch | Signed or recorded approval | Executive Sponsor |
| ISMS scope approval | Approved scope documented by target milestone | Approved ISMS Scope Statement | ISMS Manager |
| Information security policy approval and communication | Policy approved and communicated to relevant personnel | Approval record, communication evidence | Top Management / ISMS Manager |
| Information security objectives established | Objectives defined, measurable, and aligned to business direction | Objectives register and management approval | ISMS Manager |
| Leadership participation | Steering committee and management review conducted as scheduled | Meeting minutes and attendance | Executive Sponsor |
| Risk assessment completion | 100% of in-scope critical processes and systems assessed | Risk register completeness review | ISMS Manager |
| Risk ownership assigned | 100% of identified risks assigned to owners | Risk register | ISMS Manager |
| Risk treatment plan approval | Treatment plan approved for risks above acceptance criteria | Approved risk treatment plan | Risk Owners |
| Statement of Applicability completion | 100% of Annex A controls assessed for applicability with justification | Approved Statement of Applicability | ISMS Manager |
| Control implementation progress | 100% of required controls implemented or covered by approved treatment plan before Stage 2 | Control evidence review | Control Owners |
| Mandatory awareness training | At least [95%] completion by in-scope personnel before certification audit | Training reports | HR / ISMS Manager |
| Internal audit completion | Full ISMS internal audit completed before management review | Internal audit report | Internal Auditor |
| Management review completion | Management review completed before Stage 1 or Stage 2 as planned | Management review minutes | Top Management |
| Corrective action closure | High-priority audit findings closed before Stage 2; remaining actions accepted with plan | Corrective action register | ISMS Manager |
| Certification readiness | Stage 1 completed with no unresolved major readiness blockers | Stage 1 audit report and action log | ISMS Manager |
| Certification outcome | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification achieved or certification body recommendation received | Certification body report | Executive Sponsor |

Additional indicators of effective Clause 5.1 leadership and commitment include:

- Evidence that ISMS decisions are integrated into business planning and operational priorities.
- Allocation of sufficient personnel, funding, and tooling to meet ISMS objectives.
- Timely management decisions on risks, exceptions, nonconformities, and resource constraints.
- Documented communication from top management regarding the importance of information security and ISMS conformity.
- Management review outputs that include decisions on improvement, resourcing, and changes affecting the ISMS.

## Review & Update Triggers

This Charter will be reviewed at least at major project phase gates and whenever material changes occur that may affect the ISMS implementation mandate, scope, budget, timeline, resources, or leadership commitment.

Review triggers include:

| Trigger | Required Action | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Approval of ISMS scope | Confirm Charter remains aligned to approved scope and certification boundary. | ISMS Manager |
| Material change to organisational structure | Assess impact on governance, roles, responsibilities, and scope. | Executive Sponsor / ISMS Manager |
| Addition or removal of major systems, services, locations, or business units | Assess impact on scope, risk assessment, resources, budget, and audit plan. | ISMS Manager |
| Change in executive sponsor, ISMS Manager, or key control owners | Update role assignments and authority records. | Executive Sponsor |
| Budget variance exceeding [Threshold Amount / Percentage] | Reforecast budget and obtain required approval. | Executive Sponsor / Finance |
| Timeline slippage exceeding [Threshold Duration] | Rebaseline milestone plan and communicate impacts. | ISMS Manager |
| Significant risk assessment results | Update resource requirements, treatment priorities, and leadership decisions. | Risk Owners / ISMS Manager |
| Major incident or material control failure | Reassess project priorities, controls, risk treatment, and certification readiness. | ISMS Manager / Incident Owner |
| Internal audit identifies major nonconformity | Update corrective action plan, timeline, and readiness assumptions. | ISMS Manager |
| Certification body identifies Stage 1 or Stage 2 major nonconformity | Update remediation plan, resources, and certification timeline. | Executive Sponsor / ISMS Manager |
| Significant legal, regulatory, contractual, or customer requirement change | Assess impact on ISMS objectives, scope, controls, and evidence requirements. | Legal / Compliance |
| Management review decision requiring change | Update Charter, project plan, resources, or governance as directed. | ISMS Manager |

Updates to this Charter require approval by the Executive Sponsor. Material changes affecting ISMS scope, certification intent, budget, or strategic direction require top management approval.

At project closure, this Charter will be archived as implementation evidence and superseded by ongoing ISMS governance documentation, including the ISMS operating model, management review schedule, internal audit programme, risk management process, and continual improvement plan.

ISO27-002.title: ISMS Scope Statement
ISO27-002.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Control Reference | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| [ISMS-POL-004.3] | 1.0 | [ISMS Manager / CISO] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 | Clause 4.3 — Determining the Scope of the Information Security Management System | Internal |

## Purpose

This policy defines the mandatory requirements for establishing, documenting, maintaining, and reviewing the scope of the organisation’s Information Security Management System (ISMS) in accordance with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Clause 4.3.

The ISMS scope statement shall clearly define the boundaries and applicability of the ISMS, including the organisational units, locations, services, processes, information assets, technology environments, networks, third-party dependencies, and interfaces that are included or excluded. The scope shall provide a clear basis for information security risk assessment, treatment planning, Statement of Applicability development, internal audit, management review, and certification activities.

## Scope

This policy applies to all activities required to determine, approve, communicate, and maintain the ISMS scope for the organisation.

The ISMS scope shall cover the organisational boundaries, business activities, locations, services, assets, networks, systems, processes, personnel, and external interfaces that are relevant to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information within the ISMS.

The approved ISMS scope for the organisation is defined as follows:

| Scope Element | Included in ISMS Scope |
|---|---|
| Organisation / Legal Entity | [Organisation legal name] |
| Business Units / Functions | [e.g., Information Technology, Security Operations, Product Engineering, Customer Support, Human Resources, Finance, Compliance] |
| Services / Products | [e.g., SaaS platform operations, managed services, customer support services, internal corporate IT services] |
| Physical Locations | [Head office address], [data centre location if applicable], [regional offices], remote working locations used by in-scope personnel |
| Cloud / Hosting Environments | [e.g., AWS production account, Azure tenant, Microsoft 365 tenant, Google Workspace, managed hosting provider] |
| Information Assets | Information used, processed, stored, or transmitted by in-scope business processes, including customer data, employee data, security logs, operational records, source code, credentials, business records, and configuration data |
| Technology Assets | Servers, endpoints, network devices, cloud resources, databases, applications, identity platforms, monitoring tools, backup platforms, and security tooling supporting in-scope services |
| Networks | Corporate network, production network, cloud virtual networks, VPN, wireless networks, remote access services, and trusted administrative access paths supporting in-scope services |
| Personnel | Employees, contractors, temporary staff, privileged users, system administrators, developers, support personnel, and other personnel performing in-scope activities |
| Third Parties / External Providers | Suppliers, cloud providers, managed service providers, software vendors, professional service providers, and other external parties that support in-scope services or information processing |
| Interfaces and Dependencies | Interfaces between in-scope and out-of-scope environments, customer integrations, supplier connections, APIs, identity federation, data transfer mechanisms, and administrative access channels |

Any exclusions from the ISMS scope shall be explicitly documented, justified, approved, and verified to ensure that the exclusion does not affect the organisation’s ability or responsibility to provide information security for in-scope information and services.

| Exclusion | Justification | Residual Interface / Dependency | Approval |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Excluded business unit, location, system, service, or process] | [Business or technical justification] | [Any remaining connection, data flow, dependency, or shared control] | [Approver and date] |

## Policy Statements

1. The organisation shall establish, document, approve, and maintain a formal ISMS scope statement that defines the boundaries and applicability of the ISMS in accordance with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Clause 4.3.

2. The ISMS scope statement shall consider the internal and external issues relevant to the organisation’s purpose and information security objectives, including business context, regulatory obligations, operating model, technology environment, threat landscape, and stakeholder expectations.

3. The ISMS scope statement shall consider the requirements of interested parties relevant to information security, including customers, regulators, employees, suppliers, shareholders, certification bodies, contractual counterparties, and internal governance bodies.

4. The ISMS scope statement shall define the organisation’s in-scope business units, departments, teams, functions, and governance structures that are responsible for or materially involved in managing, processing, storing, transmitting, or protecting information.

5. The ISMS scope statement shall define the in-scope products, platforms, services, business processes, and supporting operational activities to which the ISMS applies.

6. The ISMS scope statement shall identify all in-scope physical locations, including offices, data centres, facilities, secure areas, remote working locations, and any other locations where in-scope information is accessed, processed, stored, transmitted, or administered.

7. The ISMS scope statement shall identify all in-scope information assets and asset classes, including customer information, employee information, business records, intellectual property, source code, credentials, system configurations, security logs, and other information requiring protection.

8. The ISMS scope statement shall identify all in-scope technology assets and environments, including applications, databases, servers, endpoints, cloud services, infrastructure platforms, storage repositories, identity systems, security tools, backup systems, and administrative systems.

9. The ISMS scope statement shall identify all in-scope networks and connectivity arrangements, including corporate networks, production networks, cloud networks, wireless networks, remote access solutions, VPNs, administrative access pathways, and connections to third parties.

10. The ISMS scope statement shall identify interfaces and dependencies between in-scope and out-of-scope areas, including data flows, shared infrastructure, shared personnel, integrated applications, identity federation, monitoring dependencies, administrative access, supplier services, and customer connections.

11. The ISMS scope statement shall define the relationship between the ISMS and external organisations, including cloud service providers, managed service providers, outsourced business processes, suppliers, contractors, consultants, and other third parties that support or affect in-scope information security.

12. The ISMS scope shall be sufficiently clear and detailed to enable effective information security risk assessment, risk treatment, control selection, Statement of Applicability development, internal audit planning, management review, and certification assessment.

13. The ISMS scope shall not be defined in a manner that omits material information security risks, avoids applicable legal, regulatory, or contractual obligations, or misrepresents the organisation’s responsibility for information security.

14. Any proposed exclusion from the ISMS scope shall be documented with a clear business justification, risk rationale, description of residual interfaces or dependencies, and evidence that the exclusion does not compromise the ISMS or mislead interested parties.

15. Exclusions shall be reviewed and approved by the ISMS Owner and senior management before being incorporated into the ISMS scope statement.

16. The organisation shall maintain documented information describing the ISMS scope and shall make it available to relevant personnel, auditors, certification bodies, regulators, customers, and other authorised interested parties as appropriate.

17. The ISMS scope statement shall be aligned with other ISMS documentation, including the information security policy, risk assessment methodology, asset inventory, risk treatment plan, Statement of Applicability, supplier register, network architecture records, data flow records, business continuity arrangements, and internal audit programme.

18. The ISMS scope statement shall be reviewed whenever significant organisational, technical, regulatory, contractual, operational, or risk-related changes occur.

19. Significant changes that may affect the ISMS scope shall include, at minimum, new business units, mergers or acquisitions, divestments, new products or services, material changes to customer commitments, new cloud environments, changes in hosting architecture, outsourcing of in-scope processes, new office locations, closure of sites, major network changes, and introduction or retirement of critical systems.

20. Changes to the ISMS scope shall be assessed through the organisation’s governance, risk, and change management processes before implementation where practicable.

21. The ISMS scope shall be approved by senior management to demonstrate leadership commitment and to confirm organisational accountability for the defined ISMS boundaries.

22. The ISMS scope statement shall be reviewed at least annually and as part of ISMS management review to confirm continued suitability, adequacy, and alignment with the organisation’s context and information security objectives.

23. The ISMS scope shall be used as the authoritative boundary for ISMS certification, internal audits, external audits, risk assessments, control applicability decisions, performance monitoring, and continual improvement activities.

24. Personnel responsible for in-scope processes, assets, systems, and services shall comply with ISMS requirements applicable to their role and area of responsibility.

25. Where shared services or shared infrastructure support both in-scope and out-of-scope activities, the organisation shall define and implement appropriate controls to protect in-scope information and prevent unmanaged risk transfer across boundaries.

26. The organisation shall ensure that out-of-scope systems, locations, services, or entities do not adversely affect the security of in-scope information assets through unmanaged connectivity, shared access, unsupported dependencies, or uncontrolled data flows.

27. The ISMS scope shall be communicated in a manner that enables stakeholders to understand what is included, what is excluded, and how interfaces with excluded areas are controlled.

28. Evidence supporting the determination and maintenance of the ISMS scope shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s documented information and record retention requirements.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Senior Management | Approves the ISMS scope statement; ensures the scope aligns with organisational strategy and risk appetite; provides resources to establish, operate, maintain, and continually improve the ISMS within the defined scope. |
| ISMS Owner / CISO | Accountable for defining, maintaining, and governing the ISMS scope; ensures scope decisions meet ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Clause 4.3 requirements; escalates unresolved scope issues to senior management. |
| ISMS Manager | Coordinates scope documentation, review, change assessment, and evidence collection; maintains the approved ISMS scope statement; ensures alignment with risk assessment, Statement of Applicability, internal audit, and management review processes. |
| Risk Owner(s) | Confirm that in-scope processes, services, and assets are represented accurately in risk assessments; accept or escalate risks arising from scope boundaries, interfaces, or exclusions. |
| Business Unit Leaders | Identify business processes, locations, personnel, suppliers, and services that should be included in the ISMS scope; notify the ISMS Manager of material changes affecting scope. |
| Asset Owners | Identify and maintain information and technology assets within their ownership; confirm whether assets are in scope; support risk assessment and control implementation for in-scope assets. |
| IT / Technology Owners | Maintain accurate information about in-scope systems, networks, cloud environments, applications, infrastructure, integrations, and technical dependencies; notify the ISMS Manager of technical changes affecting scope. |
| Legal / Compliance | Identify legal, regulatory, contractual, and customer obligations that affect the ISMS scope; review exclusions for potential compliance impact. |
| Supplier / Vendor Management | Identify suppliers and outsourced services that support in-scope activities; ensure supplier relationships and dependencies are reflected in the ISMS scope and supporting documentation. |
| Internal Audit | Uses the approved ISMS scope to plan and perform ISMS internal audits; verifies that scope boundaries, exclusions, and dependencies are documented, justified, and controlled. |
| All Personnel | Comply with ISMS requirements applicable to in-scope activities; report changes, gaps, or uncertainty regarding ISMS applicability to their manager or the ISMS Manager. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this policy is mandatory for all personnel and organisational areas included within or materially affecting the ISMS scope.

The organisation shall monitor compliance with this policy through governance activities, internal audits, management review, risk assessments, control reviews, asset inventory validation, supplier reviews, architecture reviews, and change management activities.

Minimum monitoring requirements are defined below:

| Monitoring Activity | Frequency | Responsible Role | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Review of ISMS scope statement for continued accuracy | At least annually | ISMS Manager | Approved ISMS scope statement, review record |
| Review of scope during management review | At least annually | Senior Management / ISMS Owner | Management review minutes, action log |
| Validation of in-scope business units, services, and processes | At least annually and upon major change | ISMS Manager / Business Unit Leaders | Scope validation record, organisational mapping |
| Validation of in-scope assets and systems against asset inventory | At least annually and upon major change | Asset Owners / IT Owners | Asset inventory extract, reconciliation evidence |
| Review of networks, cloud environments, and technical boundaries | At least annually and after significant architecture change | IT / Technology Owners | Network diagrams, cloud architecture records, change records |
| Review of suppliers supporting in-scope services | At least annually and upon onboarding or termination | Supplier Management | Supplier register, due diligence records, contract records |
| Review of exclusions and boundary interfaces | At least annually and upon change | ISMS Owner / Risk Owners | Exclusion register, risk assessment, approval records |
| Internal audit of ISMS scope determination and maintenance | Per internal audit programme | Internal Audit | Internal audit report, corrective actions |
| Certification audit support and evidence provision | Per certification cycle | ISMS Manager | Auditor evidence pack, scope statement, supporting records |

Non-compliance with this policy shall be documented, assessed for information security risk, and addressed through corrective action, risk treatment, disciplinary action, supplier remediation, or management escalation as appropriate.

Failure to maintain an accurate ISMS scope may result in invalid risk assessments, inappropriate control applicability decisions, incomplete audit coverage, certification nonconformities, breach of legal or contractual obligations, or unmanaged information security risk.

The ISMS Manager shall track findings related to ISMS scope definition, exclusions, boundaries, or dependencies until closure. Significant or repeated non-compliance shall be reported to senior management.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented and approved business justification and where the exception does not compromise the integrity, effectiveness, or accurate representation of the ISMS scope.

Requests for exceptions shall include, at minimum:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Exception Description | The specific requirement, boundary, service, location, asset, network, or dependency for which an exception is requested. |
| Business Justification | The reason the exception is required, including operational, contractual, legal, technical, or strategic considerations. |
| Risk Assessment | The information security risks created by the exception, including impact on confidentiality, integrity, availability, compliance, and ISMS effectiveness. |
| Compensating Controls | Controls or safeguards that will reduce the risk associated with the exception. |
| Duration | The proposed start date, end date, and review date for the exception. |
| Owner | The accountable business or risk owner responsible for managing the exception. |
| Approval | Formal approval by the ISMS Owner and, where material, senior management. |

Exceptions shall be time-bound, risk-assessed, and reviewed at least quarterly or at an approved frequency proportionate to risk.

Permanent exclusions from the ISMS scope shall not be managed as policy exceptions. Permanent exclusions shall be documented directly in the ISMS scope statement, justified, approved, and reviewed in accordance with this policy.

The ISMS Manager shall maintain an exception register for approved exceptions related to the ISMS scope.

| Exception ID | Requirement Affected | Risk Rating | Owner | Approval Date | Expiry Date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [EXC-001] | [Policy statement or scope element] | [Low/Medium/High/Critical] | [Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/Closed/Expired] |

## Review & Maintenance

This policy and the ISMS scope statement shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur that may affect the boundaries or applicability of the ISMS.

The review shall confirm that:

- the ISMS scope remains aligned with the organisation’s internal and external context;
- requirements of interested parties remain accurately reflected;
- in-scope business units, services, processes, locations, assets, networks, and systems remain accurate;
- interfaces and dependencies with out-of-scope areas are understood and controlled;
- exclusions remain justified and do not undermine the ISMS;
- the scope supports effective risk assessment, risk treatment, control selection, Statement of Applicability, internal audit, management review, and certification activities;
- changes since the previous review have been assessed and incorporated where required; and
- supporting documentation remains consistent with the approved scope.

The following events shall trigger an out-of-cycle review of the ISMS scope:

| Trigger Event | Required Action | Responsible Role |
|---|---|---|
| New or discontinued business unit, function, or legal entity | Assess impact on ISMS scope and update scope documentation if required | ISMS Owner / Business Unit Leader |
| New product, service, platform, or customer-facing process | Assess whether the activity falls within the ISMS scope | ISMS Manager / Product or Service Owner |
| New office, facility, data centre, or significant remote working model change | Assess location and physical security scope impact | ISMS Manager / Facilities / IT |
| Major cloud, network, hosting, or architecture change | Assess technical boundary, data flow, and control impact | IT / Technology Owner |
| Merger, acquisition, divestment, or outsourcing arrangement | Assess organisational and supplier scope impact | Senior Management / Legal / ISMS Owner |
| New legal, regulatory, or contractual obligation | Assess interested party requirements and scope implications | Legal / Compliance |
| Significant security incident or audit finding | Assess whether scope boundaries or exclusions contributed to the issue | ISMS Manager / Risk Owner |
| Supplier onboarding, termination, or material service change | Assess third-party dependency and scope impact | Supplier Management |
| Certification audit preparation or surveillance audit | Confirm scope accuracy and certification boundary | ISMS Manager |

Changes to this policy or the ISMS scope statement shall be version-controlled, approved by the designated owner, and communicated to affected stakeholders.

Records of scope reviews, approvals, exclusions, exception decisions, and related corrective actions shall be retained as documented information in accordance with the organisation’s record retention requirements.

The owner of this policy is responsible for ensuring that it remains current, accurate, and aligned with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 requirements and the organisation’s ISMS objectives.

## Interested Parties Register (XLSX template)

_Editable template — add your own rows. The example row(s) below are placeholders to replace._

| Interested Party ID | Interested Party Name | Interested Party Type | Internal or External | Relationship to Organisation | Business Area or ISMS Scope Relevance | Information Security Interest or Concern | Security Requirement or Expectation | Requirement Type | Source of Requirement | Legal Regulatory Contractual or Other Reference | Confidentiality Requirement | Integrity Requirement | Availability Requirement | Privacy or Personal Data Requirement | Requirement Addressed by ISMS | How Requirement Is Addressed | Linked ISMS Control or Process | Responsible Owner | Engagement or Communication Method | Review Frequency | Last Reviewed Date | Next Review Date | Status | Notes or Change History |

| [EXAMPLE: IP-002] | [EXAMPLE: Data Protection Regulator] | [EXAMPLE: Regulator] | [EXAMPLE: External] | [EXAMPLE: Supervises compliance with applicable personal data protection law] | [EXAMPLE: All processing of personal data within the ISMS scope] | [EXAMPLE: Requires appropriate security of personal data and breach notification where legally required] | [EXAMPLE: Personal data must be processed securely using appropriate technical and organisational measures] | [EXAMPLE: Regulatory] | [EXAMPLE: Applicable data protection legislation and regulatory guidance] | [EXAMPLE: GDPR Article 32 and Article 33] | [EXAMPLE: High] | [EXAMPLE: High] | [EXAMPLE: Medium] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: Addressed through privacy governance, access controls, encryption, incident response, risk assessment, and records of processing] | [EXAMPLE: Annex A 5.34, 5.31, 8.24; Privacy Procedure; Incident Response Plan] | [EXAMPLE: Data Protection Officer] | [EXAMPLE: Regulatory monitoring and compliance review] | [EXAMPLE: On Regulatory Change] | [EXAMPLE: 2025-01-15] | [EXAMPLE: 2025-07-15] | [EXAMPLE: Active] | [EXAMPLE: 2025-01-15 CD - updated following annual privacy compliance review] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Interested Party ID | Enter a unique identifier for the interested party record, using a consistent format such as IP-001, IP-002. |
| Interested Party Name | Enter the name of the stakeholder or stakeholder group, such as a regulator, customer segment, supplier, employee group, shareholder, or certification body. |
| Interested Party Type | Enter the category of interested party. Allowed values: Customer, Employee, Supplier, Regulator, Certification Body, Shareholder, Board, Partner, Outsourcer, Public Authority, Data Subject, Community, Other. |
| Internal or External | Enter whether the interested party is Internal or External to the organisation. |
| Relationship to Organisation | Briefly describe the relationship, such as receives services, provides hosting, audits the ISMS, regulates operations, works within scope, or owns business risk. |
| Business Area or ISMS Scope Relevance | Identify the business unit, service, location, system, process, or ISMS scope boundary to which this interested party is relevant. |
| Information Security Interest or Concern | Describe why this party is relevant to information security, such as protection of confidential data, service availability, regulatory compliance, secure supplier access, incident notification, or access control. |
| Security Requirement or Expectation | Record the specific information security requirement, need, or expectation this party has of the organisation. Write one clear requirement per row where possible. |
| Requirement Type | Classify the requirement. Allowed values: Legal, Regulatory, Contractual, Customer, Internal Governance, Risk Based, Standard or Certification, Supplier, Privacy, Operational, Other. |
| Source of Requirement | Enter where the requirement was identified from, such as contract, law, regulation, policy, SLA, DPIA, risk assessment, customer security schedule, supplier agreement, audit report, or management review. |
| Legal Regulatory Contractual or Other Reference | Enter the exact reference where applicable, such as contract clause, regulation name and article, policy ID, SLA section, purchase order condition, or N/A if not applicable. |
| Confidentiality Requirement | Enter the confidentiality relevance. Allowed values: High, Medium, Low, Not Applicable. Base this on the sensitivity of information expected to be protected for this interested party. |
| Integrity Requirement | Enter the integrity relevance. Allowed values: High, Medium, Low, Not Applicable. Base this on the need for information or processing to remain accurate, complete, and protected from unauthorised change. |
| Availability Requirement | Enter the availability relevance. Allowed values: High, Medium, Low, Not Applicable. Base this on uptime, continuity, recovery, or service access expectations. |
| Privacy or Personal Data Requirement | State whether the requirement involves personal data or privacy obligations. Allowed values: Yes, No, Not Known. If Yes, include the relevant privacy expectation in the requirement fields. |
| Requirement Addressed by ISMS | State whether the organisation has determined this requirement will be addressed through the ISMS. Allowed values: Yes, Partially, No, To Be Assessed. |
| How Requirement Is Addressed | Briefly describe the ISMS mechanism used to address the requirement, such as risk treatment, policy, procedure, control, supplier management, incident process, audit programme, awareness training, or business continuity arrangements. |
| Linked ISMS Control or Process | Enter the relevant ISO/IEC 27001 clause, Annex A control, internal control ID, policy, procedure, risk ID, SoA reference, or process name that addresses the requirement. |
| Responsible Owner | Enter the role accountable for maintaining understanding of this party and its requirements, such as CISO, Compliance Manager, DPO, Procurement Lead, Service Owner, HR Manager, or Legal Counsel. |
| Engagement or Communication Method | Record how the organisation monitors or engages with this party, such as contract review, supplier review meeting, regulatory monitoring, customer QBR, employee forum, audit, ticketing system, or management review. |
| Review Frequency | Enter how often this party and its requirements are reviewed. Allowed values: Monthly, Quarterly, Semi-Annually, Annually, On Contract Change, On Regulatory Change, On Major Business Change, Event Driven. |
| Last Reviewed Date | Enter the date this record was last reviewed in YYYY-MM-DD format. Leave blank only for new records not yet reviewed. |
| Next Review Date | Enter the planned next review date in YYYY-MM-DD format, based on the review frequency or triggering event. |
| Status | Enter the current status of the record. Allowed values: Draft, Active, Under Review, Retired. |
| Notes or Change History | Record brief notes about changes, assumptions, review outcomes, or decisions, including date and initials where useful. |

### Maintenance

The template is owned by the ISMS Manager or Compliance Manager, with input from Legal, Risk, Procurement, HR, Service Owners, and the Data Protection Officer where applicable. It should be reviewed at least annually and whenever contracts, regulations, services, suppliers, organisational context, or ISMS scope change, drawing from contract repositories, legal/regulatory trackers, risk assessments, supplier records, customer requirements, management review outputs, and policy/process repositories.
