ISO27-012.title: Information Security Policy
ISO27-012.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Control Reference | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| [ISMS-POL-001] | 1.0 | [Chief Information Security Officer / ISMS Manager] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 | Clause 5.2 / Annex A.5.1 | Internal |

## Purpose

This Information Security Policy establishes the organisation’s top-level commitment to the protection of information assets and the implementation, operation, maintenance, and continual improvement of an Information Security Management System (ISMS) aligned with ISO/IEC 27001:2022.

This Policy sets mandatory requirements for information security governance, including leadership commitment, information security objectives, risk-based controls, compliance obligations, communication, accountability, and continual improvement. It provides direction for the establishment of supporting information security policies, standards, procedures, processes, and controls.

## Scope

This Policy applies to:

- All employees, officers, directors, contractors, consultants, temporary workers, interns, third-party users, and other personnel who access, process, store, transmit, manage, or support information assets on behalf of [Organisation Name].
- All information assets owned, leased, administered, processed, or entrusted to [Organisation Name], regardless of format, medium, location, system, or lifecycle stage.
- All business processes, information systems, applications, networks, cloud services, end-user devices, operational technology where applicable, facilities, and third-party services within the defined ISMS scope.
- All locations and operating environments included in the ISMS scope, including offices, remote working locations, data centres, cloud environments, and third-party-hosted environments.
- All information classified as public, internal, confidential, restricted, personal data, regulated data, customer data, intellectual property, or any other classification defined by [Organisation Name].

The formal boundaries and applicability of the ISMS shall be defined and maintained in the ISMS Scope Statement, considering organisational context, internal and external issues, interested parties, legal, regulatory, contractual, and business requirements.

## Policy Statements

1. [Organisation Name] shall establish, implement, maintain, and continually improve an Information Security Management System aligned with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and appropriate to the organisation’s purpose, strategic direction, business objectives, operating context, and information security risk profile.

2. Senior management shall approve, sponsor, and support this Information Security Policy and shall ensure that information security is integrated into organisational governance, business planning, risk management, procurement, project delivery, technology management, supplier management, and operational decision-making.

3. [Organisation Name] shall define and maintain information security objectives that are measurable where practicable, aligned with business objectives, consistent with this Policy, and supported by plans identifying responsible owners, resources, timelines, and evaluation criteria.

4. Information security objectives shall include, at a minimum, objectives related to:
   - Protecting the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information assets.
   - Managing information security risks within approved risk acceptance criteria.
   - Meeting applicable legal, regulatory, contractual, and privacy obligations.
   - Supporting secure and resilient business operations.
   - Promoting security awareness and responsible user behaviour.
   - Ensuring timely detection, reporting, response, and recovery from information security incidents.
   - Continually improving the effectiveness of the ISMS.

5. [Organisation Name] shall apply a risk-based approach to information security, including the identification, assessment, treatment, monitoring, and review of information security risks in accordance with the organisation’s approved information security risk management methodology.

6. Information security controls shall be selected, implemented, operated, monitored, and reviewed based on risk assessment results, business requirements, legal and regulatory obligations, contractual commitments, and the ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Statement of Applicability.

7. [Organisation Name] shall maintain a documented Statement of Applicability that identifies applicable ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A controls, justification for inclusion or exclusion, and implementation status.

8. This Policy shall provide the governing authority for supporting information security policies, standards, procedures, guidelines, baselines, and control documentation. Supporting documents shall be consistent with this Policy and shall provide additional mandatory or advisory requirements where appropriate.

9. Information shall be classified, handled, stored, transmitted, retained, and disposed of in accordance with its sensitivity, value, criticality, legal requirements, and business impact.

10. Access to information assets shall be granted based on authorised business need, least privilege, segregation of duties, and approved identity and access management processes.

11. Users shall be accountable for safeguarding credentials, devices, information, and systems assigned to them and shall comply with applicable security requirements, acceptable use rules, and confidentiality obligations.

12. [Organisation Name] shall protect information assets throughout their lifecycle, including creation, collection, receipt, processing, storage, transmission, sharing, archival, and secure disposal.

13. [Organisation Name] shall identify and comply with applicable statutory, regulatory, contractual, privacy, intellectual property, and industry requirements relating to information security.

14. Information security requirements shall be incorporated into supplier selection, contracting, onboarding, service delivery, monitoring, and offboarding processes where suppliers access, process, store, transmit, or support organisational information assets.

15. Information security shall be considered during the design, acquisition, development, implementation, maintenance, and decommissioning of information systems, services, applications, infrastructure, and business processes.

16. [Organisation Name] shall establish and maintain processes for reporting, assessing, responding to, managing, and learning from information security events and incidents.

17. Business continuity, disaster recovery, backup, and resilience arrangements shall consider information security requirements and shall be tested at planned intervals according to risk and business criticality.

18. [Organisation Name] shall maintain appropriate technical, organisational, physical, and procedural controls to reduce information security risks to acceptable levels.

19. Personnel shall receive information security awareness, education, and training appropriate to their roles, responsibilities, access privileges, and exposure to information security risks.

20. This Policy and applicable supporting information security policies shall be communicated to relevant personnel and interested parties in a form that is understandable, accessible, and appropriate to their role and relationship with [Organisation Name].

21. Personnel and relevant third parties shall acknowledge their understanding of and agreement to comply with this Policy and applicable supporting information security requirements where required by role, contract, or risk.

22. This Policy shall be retained as documented information and made available to authorised interested parties, including employees, contractors, auditors, regulators, customers, and suppliers, where appropriate and subject to confidentiality and disclosure requirements.

23. [Organisation Name] shall monitor, measure, analyse, and evaluate the effectiveness of the ISMS, information security objectives, and applicable controls through defined metrics, control testing, risk reviews, audits, management reviews, incident analysis, and compliance monitoring.

24. Internal audits of the ISMS shall be performed at planned intervals to determine whether the ISMS conforms to ISO/IEC 27001:2022, organisational requirements, and this Policy.

25. Senior management shall review the ISMS at planned intervals to ensure its continuing suitability, adequacy, effectiveness, and alignment with the strategic direction of [Organisation Name].

26. Nonconformities, control failures, incidents, audit findings, and identified weaknesses shall be investigated, recorded, prioritised, remediated, and reviewed for corrective action and continual improvement.

27. [Organisation Name] shall maintain evidence demonstrating implementation and operation of this Policy and the ISMS, including approvals, risk assessments, treatment plans, control records, training records, audit results, management review outputs, exceptions, and corrective actions.

28. All personnel and relevant third parties shall comply with this Policy, supporting information security policies, contractual security obligations, and applicable laws and regulations.

29. Any suspected or actual breach of this Policy shall be reported promptly through the defined incident reporting or management escalation channels.

30. [Organisation Name] shall continually improve the ISMS and information security controls based on risk changes, business changes, technology changes, audit results, monitoring outcomes, incidents, lessons learned, stakeholder requirements, and management review decisions.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board of Directors / Governing Body | Provides governance oversight for information security; ensures information security risks are considered in enterprise risk management; approves risk appetite where applicable; holds senior management accountable for ISMS effectiveness. |
| Chief Executive Officer / Executive Management | Demonstrates leadership and commitment to the ISMS; ensures this Policy is aligned with organisational strategy; provides resources; supports enforcement; ensures information security objectives are established and reviewed. |
| Information Security Steering Committee / Risk Committee | Reviews ISMS performance, significant risks, treatment plans, major incidents, compliance status, exceptions, and improvement initiatives; supports prioritisation and cross-functional decision-making. |
| Chief Information Security Officer / ISMS Manager | Owns this Policy; coordinates ISMS implementation and maintenance; manages the information security risk management process; maintains the Statement of Applicability; reports ISMS performance; coordinates audits and management reviews. |
| Risk Owners | Own assigned information security risks; approve risk treatment decisions within delegated authority; monitor risk status; ensure treatment actions are completed and remain effective. |
| Asset Owners / Information Owners | Classify and protect assigned information assets; define access requirements; approve access where required; ensure controls are implemented according to risk and business requirements. |
| Control Owners | Implement, operate, monitor, and evidence assigned information security controls; remediate control weaknesses; report control performance and exceptions. |
| IT / Technology Management | Implements and operates technical security controls; maintains secure infrastructure, systems, applications, and networks; supports vulnerability management, logging, backup, access management, and incident response activities. |
| Human Resources | Ensures personnel security requirements are embedded in onboarding, role changes, training, disciplinary processes, and offboarding; supports awareness and acknowledgement processes. |
| Legal / Compliance / Privacy Function | Advises on legal, regulatory, privacy, contractual, and compliance obligations; supports management of external requirements and regulatory engagement where applicable. |
| Procurement / Supplier Management | Ensures supplier security requirements are assessed, included in contracts, monitored during service delivery, and addressed at termination or transition. |
| Managers | Ensure personnel under their supervision understand and comply with this Policy; support training, access reviews, incident reporting, and remediation activities. |
| Employees, Contractors, and Authorised Users | Comply with this Policy and supporting requirements; protect information assets; complete required training; report security events, incidents, weaknesses, and suspected violations promptly. |
| Internal Audit / Independent Assurance Function | Provides independent assessment of ISMS conformity, control design, control effectiveness, and compliance with this Policy and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 requirements. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory. [Organisation Name] shall monitor adherence to this Policy and supporting information security requirements through governance, assurance, and operational control activities.

| Monitoring Activity | Minimum Frequency | Responsible Role | Evidence / Output |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Review of information security objectives and progress | Quarterly | CISO / ISMS Manager | Objective dashboard, KPI/KRI report, action tracker |
| Information security risk assessment review | At least annually and upon significant change | ISMS Manager / Risk Owners | Risk register, risk treatment plan, approval records |
| Statement of Applicability review | At least annually and upon significant change | ISMS Manager | Approved Statement of Applicability |
| ISMS internal audit | At planned intervals, at least annually | Internal Audit / Independent Assessor | Audit plan, audit report, findings, corrective actions |
| Management review of the ISMS | At least annually | Executive Management | Management review minutes, decisions, action items |
| Policy acknowledgement tracking | Upon onboarding and at defined intervals | HR / ISMS Manager | Acknowledgement records |
| Security awareness completion monitoring | At least annually | HR / ISMS Manager | Training completion report |
| Access review monitoring | Based on risk and system criticality | Asset Owners / IT | Access review records, remediation evidence |
| Supplier security review | Based on supplier risk tier | Procurement / Supplier Management | Assessment results, contract clauses, review records |
| Incident trend and lessons learned review | Quarterly or after major incidents | CISO / Incident Response Lead | Incident reports, lessons learned, corrective actions |
| Corrective action status review | Monthly or as defined by severity | ISMS Manager / Control Owners | Corrective action register |

Noncompliance may result in corrective action, suspension or removal of access privileges, contractual remedies, disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment or contract, civil or criminal referral, or other actions permitted by law and organisational policy.

Enforcement actions shall be proportionate to the severity, intent, recurrence, business impact, legal implications, and risk created by the violation. Policy violations involving suspected misconduct, fraud, unauthorised disclosure, data breach, or unlawful activity shall be escalated to appropriate management, Legal, Human Resources, Privacy, Compliance, or law enforcement authorities as required.

The organisation shall maintain records of compliance monitoring, violations, investigations, disciplinary outcomes where appropriate, remediation actions, and management decisions in accordance with retention, confidentiality, privacy, and legal requirements.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be formally requested, reviewed, approved, documented, time-bound, and risk-assessed before implementation, unless emergency action is required to protect life, safety, legal interests, or critical business operations.

Exception requests shall include, at a minimum:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Requestor | Individual, team, or business unit requesting the exception |
| Policy requirement | Specific Policy statement or supporting requirement for which exception is sought |
| Business justification | Reason the requirement cannot be met and business impact if not approved |
| Risk assessment | Identified risks, likelihood, impact, affected assets, affected data, and potential consequences |
| Compensating controls | Alternative safeguards to reduce risk during the exception period |
| Duration | Requested start date, end date, and review date |
| Owner | Individual accountable for managing the exception and ensuring closure |
| Approval | Required approval based on risk level and delegated authority |
| Closure plan | Actions and timeline to return to compliance or implement a permanent approved solution |

Exception approvals shall follow the organisation’s risk acceptance authority model.

| Exception Risk Level | Approval Authority | Maximum Initial Duration | Review Requirement |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Low | Control Owner and ISMS Manager | 90 days | At expiry or upon material change |
| Medium | Risk Owner and ISMS Manager | 180 days | At least every 90 days |
| High | Executive Management / Risk Committee | 180 days | At least every 60 days |
| Critical | Executive Management and Board / Governing Body delegate | 90 days | At least monthly |

Exceptions shall not be approved where they would knowingly violate applicable law, regulation, binding contractual obligation, or unacceptable risk appetite limits unless explicitly authorised through approved legal and executive governance channels.

Expired exceptions shall be treated as noncompliance unless renewed through formal review and approval. All exceptions shall be recorded in an exception register and reviewed periodically by the ISMS Manager and relevant governance forum.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur that may affect the ISMS or information security requirements, including changes to:

- Organisational strategy, structure, or operating model.
- ISMS scope, business processes, or critical services.
- Legal, regulatory, contractual, privacy, or industry requirements.
- Information security risk profile or risk appetite.
- Technology architecture, cloud services, systems, or infrastructure.
- Threat landscape, vulnerabilities, incidents, or lessons learned.
- Audit findings, nonconformities, corrective actions, or management review decisions.
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022 requirements or related control guidance.

The Policy Owner shall coordinate review and maintenance activities, obtain input from relevant stakeholders, ensure continued alignment with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Clause 5.2 and Annex A.5.1, and submit material changes for approval by authorised senior management.

| Review Trigger | Required Action | Responsible Role |
|---|---|---|
| Scheduled annual review | Confirm suitability, adequacy, effectiveness, and alignment with ISMS objectives | Policy Owner |
| Significant organisational or technology change | Assess whether Policy updates or supporting control changes are required | ISMS Manager / Control Owners |
| Significant incident or breach | Review relevant Policy requirements and identify improvements | CISO / Incident Response Lead |
| Audit finding or nonconformity | Update Policy or supporting documentation where corrective action requires change | Policy Owner / Internal Audit |
| Regulatory or contractual change | Assess compliance impact and update requirements as needed | Legal / Compliance / Policy Owner |
| Management review decision | Implement approved changes and record actions | ISMS Manager |

Approval and version control shall be maintained as documented information.

| Version | Date | Description of Change | Author | Approved By |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Initial issue | [Name / Role] | [Name / Role] |

This Policy shall remain in effect until superseded, withdrawn, or replaced by an approved version. Updated versions shall be communicated to relevant interested parties and made available through approved document repositories or communication channels.

ISO27-013.title: Information Security Objectives
ISO27-013.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Control Reference | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| [ISMS-POL-006.2] | 1.0 | [Information Security Manager] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 | Clause 6.2 — Information Security Objectives and Planning to Achieve Them | Internal |

## Purpose

This Policy establishes the mandatory requirements for defining, approving, communicating, monitoring, reviewing and maintaining measurable information security objectives in accordance with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Clause 6.2.

The purpose of these objectives is to ensure the organisation’s Information Security Management System (ISMS) delivers intended outcomes, supports the information security policy, addresses applicable risks and opportunities, and provides measurable evidence of continual improvement.

## Scope

This Policy applies to:

- The organisation’s ISMS and all processes, functions, locations, assets, technologies and services within the defined ISMS scope.
- All business units, departments and functions that own, operate, support or depend on information assets within the ISMS scope.
- All employees, contractors, third-party users and service providers with responsibilities that affect achievement of information security objectives.
- Strategic, tactical and operational information security objectives established at organisational, functional, process, project and service levels.

This Policy applies to the full lifecycle of information security objectives, including establishment, approval, planning, communication, measurement, reporting, evaluation, revision and retirement.

## Policy Statements

1. The organisation shall establish information security objectives at relevant functions, levels and processes required for the effective operation and continual improvement of the ISMS.

2. Information security objectives shall be consistent with the approved Information Security Policy and shall support the organisation’s strategic direction, risk appetite and business objectives.

3. Information security objectives shall take into account:
   - Applicable information security requirements.
   - Results of information security risk assessments.
   - Results of risk treatment planning.
   - Legal, regulatory and contractual obligations.
   - Interested party requirements relevant to the ISMS.
   - Internal and external issues affecting the ISMS context.
   - Findings from audits, management reviews, incidents, nonconformities and performance monitoring.

4. Each information security objective shall be measurable or capable of objective evaluation using defined metrics, thresholds, milestones or qualitative evidence where quantitative measurement is not practicable.

5. Information security objectives shall be documented in an approved objectives register or equivalent controlled ISMS record.

6. Each information security objective shall include, at minimum:
   - Objective statement.
   - Business or security rationale.
   - Relevant ISMS risk, requirement, control, process or improvement driver.
   - Metric or evaluation method.
   - Target or success criterion.
   - Baseline, where applicable.
   - Owner.
   - Required resources.
   - Planned actions to achieve the objective.
   - Responsible parties.
   - Target completion date or review frequency.
   - Monitoring and reporting method.
   - Current status.
   - Evidence location.

7. The organisation shall define information security objectives using a structured format that supports accountability and measurement, such as the following:

| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Objective ID | Unique identifier for traceability |
| Objective Statement | Clear statement of the intended information security outcome |
| Linked Requirement or Risk | Related risk, legal requirement, control, audit finding, incident trend or business requirement |
| Metric / Evaluation Method | Quantitative KPI, qualitative assessment method or milestone evidence |
| Target / Success Criterion | Measurable threshold or defined completion criterion |
| Owner | Individual role accountable for achievement |
| Supporting Roles | Roles responsible for delivery or evidence provision |
| Resources Required | People, tools, budget, training, processes or external support required |
| Planned Actions | Actions required to achieve the objective |
| Due Date / Frequency | Target completion date or recurring measurement frequency |
| Reporting Route | Forum, report or dashboard used for monitoring |
| Evidence | Records demonstrating progress and achievement |
| Status | Not Started, In Progress, At Risk, Achieved, Not Achieved, Deferred or Retired |

8. Information security objectives shall be established for relevant ISMS areas, which may include, where applicable:
   - Risk treatment effectiveness.
   - Security awareness and training.
   - Access control effectiveness.
   - Vulnerability management.
   - Incident management and response.
   - Supplier and third-party security.
   - Business continuity and resilience.
   - Compliance with legal, regulatory and contractual obligations.
   - Audit and corrective action performance.
   - Security monitoring and detection capability.
   - Data protection and information classification.
   - Secure change, development and configuration management.
   - Continual improvement of the ISMS.

9. The organisation shall maintain a current set of information security objectives appropriate to the size, complexity, risk profile and business context of the organisation.

10. Information security objectives shall be approved by ISMS leadership or other authorised governance body prior to implementation.

11. Where objectives require investment, technology changes, staffing, training or cross-functional support, the required resources shall be identified and approved through appropriate management channels.

12. The organisation shall plan how to achieve each information security objective by defining:
    - What will be done.
    - What resources will be required.
    - Who will be responsible.
    - When the objective will be completed or reviewed.
    - How results will be evaluated.

13. The required planning information for each objective shall be documented before the objective is considered active.

14. Information security objectives shall be communicated to relevant personnel and interested parties as appropriate to their roles and responsibilities.

15. Personnel assigned ownership or delivery responsibilities for information security objectives shall be informed of their responsibilities, target dates, expected evidence and reporting obligations.

16. Information security objectives shall be integrated into relevant ISMS processes, including risk treatment planning, internal audits, corrective action management, management review, operational planning and performance evaluation.

17. Information security objectives shall be monitored at planned intervals using defined metrics, evidence and status updates.

18. Progress against information security objectives shall be reported to appropriate governance forums, including management review, at intervals sufficient to support timely decision-making and corrective action.

19. The following minimum monitoring schedule shall apply unless a more frequent schedule is required due to risk, regulatory obligation or management direction:

| Objective Type | Minimum Monitoring Frequency | Minimum Reporting Forum |
|---|---:|---|
| Strategic ISMS objectives | Quarterly | ISMS Steering Committee or Management Review |
| Risk treatment objectives | Monthly or aligned to treatment plan milestones | Risk Review or ISMS Governance Forum |
| Compliance-related objectives | Quarterly | Compliance Review or Management Review |
| Incident or vulnerability remediation objectives | Monthly, or more frequently for high-risk items | Security Operations or Risk Review |
| Audit finding and corrective action objectives | Monthly until closure | Corrective Action Review or Management Review |
| Awareness and training objectives | Quarterly | ISMS Governance Forum |
| Supplier security objectives | Quarterly or per contract review cycle | Supplier Governance Review |

20. The organisation shall retain documented evidence of monitoring and evaluation of information security objectives.

21. Where an information security objective is not achieved, is at risk of not being achieved, or is no longer suitable, the owner shall identify the reason and initiate appropriate action.

22. Actions for objectives that are not achieved or at risk shall include one or more of the following, as appropriate:
    - Corrective action.
    - Risk reassessment.
    - Resource escalation.
    - Target revision with approval.
    - Change to planned actions.
    - Acceptance of residual risk by authorised management.
    - Retirement or replacement of the objective where no longer applicable.

23. Changes to information security objectives shall be controlled, documented and approved by authorised management.

24. The organisation shall ensure that objective targets are realistic, risk-based and aligned with available resources, while maintaining sufficient ambition to drive continual improvement of the ISMS.

25. Information security objectives shall not be limited to compliance activity alone and shall include objectives that improve the effectiveness, resilience and maturity of information security controls and processes.

26. Information security objectives shall be traceable to relevant ISMS records where applicable, including:
    - Information security risks and risk treatment plans.
    - Statement of Applicability.
    - Internal and external audit results.
    - Management review outputs.
    - Incident and problem records.
    - Corrective action records.
    - Compliance obligations.
    - Security performance metrics.
    - Business and operational requirements.

27. Information security objectives shall be reviewed following significant changes, including:
    - Major organisational change.
    - Material changes to the ISMS scope.
    - Significant security incidents.
    - New or changed legal, regulatory or contractual requirements.
    - Material changes to risk exposure or threat landscape.
    - Major technology, supplier or process changes.
    - Internal or external audit findings indicating objective misalignment.
    - Management review decisions.

28. The organisation shall define and maintain objective examples or templates to promote consistency in how information security objectives are written, measured and reported.

29. Information security objective records shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s records retention requirements and shall remain available as evidence of ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Clause 6.2 conformity.

30. Information security objectives shall be protected from unauthorised alteration, deletion or disclosure in accordance with their classification and the organisation’s document control requirements.

31. Objectives that contain sensitive information, such as risk exposure, control weaknesses, incident trends or security capability gaps, shall be classified and handled appropriately.

32. Information security objectives shall be included as an input to ISMS management review and continual improvement activities.

33. The achievement, non-achievement and continuing suitability of information security objectives shall be considered when evaluating ISMS performance and effectiveness.

34. The organisation shall not treat information security objectives as static annual statements only; objectives shall be maintained as active management instruments that guide security planning, performance evaluation and continual improvement.

35. At least the following objective categories shall be considered during each formal objective-setting cycle:

| Category | Example Objective Focus | Typical Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Risk Treatment | Reduce unacceptable information security risks to approved residual risk levels | Risk treatment plan updates, risk acceptance records |
| Awareness | Improve staff completion and effectiveness of security training | Training completion reports, phishing simulation results |
| Access Control | Improve timely access reviews and removal of inappropriate access | Access review records, joiner-mover-leaver metrics |
| Vulnerability Management | Reduce exposure to critical and high vulnerabilities within defined remediation targets | Vulnerability reports, remediation tickets |
| Incident Management | Improve incident detection, response and lessons learned | Incident reports, post-incident reviews |
| Supplier Security | Increase assurance over suppliers handling sensitive information | Supplier assessments, contract security clauses |
| Compliance | Maintain compliance with applicable information security obligations | Compliance assessments, audit evidence |
| ISMS Improvement | Improve closure of audit findings and corrective actions | Corrective action logs, verification records |

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Top Management | Shall ensure information security objectives are established, aligned with strategic direction, supported by appropriate resources and reviewed through management review. |
| ISMS Steering Committee / Governance Forum | Shall approve objectives, monitor progress, review escalations, make resource decisions and ensure objectives remain suitable and risk-aligned. |
| Information Security Manager | Shall coordinate the objective-setting process, maintain the objectives register, define measurement methods, facilitate reporting and ensure Clause 6.2 requirements are met. |
| Risk Owner | Shall ensure objectives linked to information security risks and risk treatment plans are appropriate, measurable and progressed within approved timeframes. |
| Objective Owner | Shall be accountable for achieving assigned objectives, maintaining progress updates, providing evidence, identifying risks to delivery and escalating issues. |
| Control Owner | Shall support objectives related to the operation, performance or improvement of assigned information security controls. |
| Process Owner | Shall establish and support objectives relevant to business or operational processes within the ISMS scope. |
| Compliance / Legal Function | Shall advise on objectives required to address legal, regulatory and contractual information security obligations. |
| Internal Audit | Shall assess, as appropriate, whether information security objectives are established, measurable, monitored, evidenced and aligned with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 requirements. |
| Human Resources | Shall support objectives related to personnel security, awareness, training and disciplinary processes. |
| IT / Technology Teams | Shall support objectives related to technical controls, vulnerability management, access management, monitoring, resilience and secure operations. |
| Procurement / Supplier Management | Shall support objectives related to supplier security assurance and third-party risk management. |
| Employees and Contractors | Shall comply with assigned responsibilities and contribute to achievement of relevant information security objectives. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory for all personnel and organisational units within scope.

The organisation shall monitor compliance with this Policy through one or more of the following mechanisms:

- Review of the information security objectives register.
- ISMS performance reporting.
- Management review.
- Internal audits.
- External audits.
- Risk treatment plan reviews.
- Corrective action reviews.
- Security governance meetings.
- Evidence sampling and verification.
- Review of metric definitions, reporting quality and target achievement.

The Information Security Manager shall ensure that evidence is available to demonstrate:

- Objectives have been established at relevant functions and levels.
- Objectives are consistent with the Information Security Policy.
- Objectives are measurable or capable of evaluation.
- Objectives consider applicable information security requirements and risk treatment outcomes.
- Plans exist for achieving objectives.
- Owners, resources, timelines and evaluation methods are defined.
- Objectives are communicated where relevant.
- Progress is monitored and reported.
- Results are evaluated and acted upon.
- Objectives are updated when required.

Non-compliance with this Policy may result in:

- Corrective action.
- Management escalation.
- Reassessment of associated risks.
- Withdrawal or revision of objective approval.
- Mandatory remediation planning.
- Contractual remedies for suppliers or third parties.
- Disciplinary action in accordance with organisational policy.
- Reporting to governance, audit, legal or regulatory bodies where required.

Failure to establish, monitor or maintain required information security objectives shall be treated as an ISMS nonconformity and managed through the organisation’s corrective action process.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented and approved business, operational, legal or risk-based justification.

All exception requests shall include:

| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Exception Request ID | Unique identifier |
| Requestor | Name and role of person requesting the exception |
| Policy Requirement | Specific requirement for which exception is requested |
| Rationale | Business, technical, legal or operational justification |
| Risk Assessment | Description of associated information security risks |
| Compensating Controls | Controls or measures to reduce risk during the exception period |
| Impact | Impact on ISMS objectives, risk treatment or compliance obligations |
| Duration | Start date and expiry date |
| Approval | Authorised approver based on risk and governance requirements |
| Review Frequency | Required review interval for longer-running exceptions |
| Closure Plan | Actions required to return to compliance |

Exceptions shall:

- Be approved by the Information Security Manager and relevant risk owner.
- Be time-bound and subject to review.
- Not compromise compliance with applicable legal, regulatory or contractual obligations unless formally approved by authorised legal and executive management.
- Be recorded in the ISMS exception register.
- Be reviewed at expiry or earlier if risk conditions change.
- Be reported to the appropriate governance forum where material to ISMS performance or risk.

Permanent exceptions shall not be granted. Long-term deviations shall be addressed through risk treatment, objective revision, control improvement or formal change to this Policy.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur that may affect the establishment, planning, monitoring or achievement of information security objectives.

Triggers for review shall include:

- Changes to ISO/IEC 27001 requirements or certification scope.
- Changes to the organisation’s ISMS scope.
- Significant changes to business strategy, operating model or risk appetite.
- Significant information security incidents.
- Material changes in legal, regulatory or contractual obligations.
- Internal or external audit findings.
- Management review outputs.
- Significant changes in technology, suppliers or threat landscape.
- Repeated failure to achieve information security objectives.
- Identification of ineffective or unsuitable measurement methods.

The Information Security Manager shall be responsible for coordinating review and maintenance of this Policy.

Top Management or the designated ISMS governance authority shall approve material changes to this Policy.

Documented records of Policy reviews, approvals and changes shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s document control and records retention requirements.

ISO27-014.title: Roles, Responsibilities & Authorities
ISO27-014.content:
| Metadata | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | [ISMS-POL-005] |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | [Chief Information Security Officer / ISMS Manager] |
| Effective Date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Framework | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 |
| Control Reference | Clause 5.3 — Organisational Roles, Responsibilities and Authorities; Annex A.5.2 — Information Security Roles and Responsibilities |
| Classification | Internal |

## Purpose

The purpose of this Policy is to establish mandatory requirements for defining, assigning, communicating, and maintaining information security roles, responsibilities, and authorities within the Information Security Management System (ISMS).

This Policy supports the organisation’s implementation of ISO/IEC 27001:2022 by ensuring that:

- responsibilities and authorities relevant to information security and the ISMS are clearly assigned;
- accountability for ISMS performance and conformity is established;
- information security duties are communicated to relevant personnel and interested parties;
- roles are maintained throughout organisational, technological, and operational change;
- conflicts of interest and incompatible duties are identified and managed.

## Scope

This Policy applies to:

- all personnel, including employees, contractors, temporary staff, interns, and third-party users who perform work under the organisation’s control;
- all business units, functions, departments, and locations included within the approved ISMS scope;
- all information assets, processes, systems, services, applications, infrastructure, and data within the ISMS scope;
- all individuals assigned responsibilities for establishing, operating, maintaining, monitoring, reviewing, or improving the ISMS;
- third-party suppliers and service providers where contractual or operational responsibilities affect the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of information within the ISMS scope.

This Policy applies to all information security responsibilities whether they are assigned through job descriptions, organisational charts, governance forums, RACI matrices, process documentation, supplier contracts, project documentation, or system ownership records.

## Policy Statements

1. The organisation shall define and maintain information security roles, responsibilities, and authorities necessary for the establishment, implementation, maintenance, and continual improvement of the ISMS.

2. Top management shall ensure that responsibilities and authorities for roles relevant to information security are assigned and communicated within the organisation.

3. Top management shall assign responsibility and authority for ensuring that the ISMS conforms to the requirements of ISO/IEC 27001:2022.

4. Top management shall assign responsibility and authority for reporting on the performance of the ISMS to top management and relevant governance bodies.

5. The organisation shall appoint an ISMS owner or ISMS Manager with authority to coordinate ISMS governance activities, maintain ISMS documentation, support risk management activities, and report ISMS performance.

6. Information security responsibilities shall be defined for all roles that manage, operate, administer, develop, support, access, or oversee information assets within the ISMS scope.

7. Information security responsibilities shall be documented in appropriate artefacts, including job descriptions, role profiles, policies, procedures, asset registers, risk treatment plans, contracts, committee terms of reference, and responsibility matrices.

8. The organisation shall ensure that assigned information security responsibilities are appropriate to the role holder’s authority, competence, seniority, and organisational position.

9. The organisation shall ensure that individuals are made aware of their information security responsibilities before being granted access to information assets, systems, or services.

10. Information security roles and responsibilities shall be communicated during onboarding, role changes, training, awareness activities, contract initiation, and other relevant points in the personnel or supplier lifecycle.

11. Managers shall ensure that personnel under their supervision understand and comply with assigned information security responsibilities.

12. Asset owners shall be assigned for information assets within the ISMS scope and shall be accountable for ensuring that assets are classified, protected, used, retained, and disposed of in accordance with applicable information security requirements.

13. Risk owners shall be assigned for information security risks and shall be accountable for approving risk treatment decisions, accepting residual risk within delegated authority, and monitoring risk treatment progress.

14. Control owners shall be assigned for applicable ISO/IEC 27001 controls and shall be accountable for implementation, operation, monitoring, evidence retention, and reporting of control effectiveness.

15. Process owners shall be assigned for ISMS processes and shall be accountable for ensuring that those processes are documented, followed, measured where applicable, and improved.

16. System owners shall be assigned for systems, applications, platforms, and infrastructure components within the ISMS scope and shall be accountable for ensuring that security requirements are implemented and maintained throughout the system lifecycle.

17. The organisation shall define responsibilities for identifying, reporting, assessing, responding to, and learning from information security events and incidents.

18. The organisation shall define responsibilities for information security risk assessment, risk treatment, internal audit, management review, corrective action, supplier security management, access control, asset management, change management, business continuity, and compliance obligations.

19. The organisation shall ensure segregation of duties is applied where necessary to reduce the risk of unauthorised or unintended modification, misuse, fraud, or error.

20. Where segregation of duties is not practicable due to business constraints, compensating controls shall be documented, approved, implemented, and monitored.

21. Individuals shall not approve their own access, changes, risk acceptance, control evidence, audit results, or corrective action closure where such approval would create a conflict of interest.

22. The organisation shall define delegated authorities for information security decisions, including risk acceptance, policy approval, exception approval, access approval, supplier approval, and incident escalation.

23. Delegated authorities shall be documented and aligned with the organisation’s governance, risk appetite, legal obligations, and management structure.

24. Information security responsibilities assigned to external parties shall be documented in contracts, statements of work, service level agreements, data processing agreements, or other binding arrangements.

25. Supplier and outsourced service responsibilities shall include applicable requirements for confidentiality, access control, incident notification, compliance with security policies, evidence provision, audit support, and return or deletion of information upon termination.

26. The organisation shall maintain an approved responsibility matrix or equivalent record that maps key ISMS responsibilities to accountable and responsible roles.

27. Responsibility assignments shall be reviewed when there are material changes to the organisation, ISMS scope, business processes, information assets, systems, suppliers, legal obligations, or risk environment.

28. Vacant roles, interim assignments, or temporary delegations affecting the ISMS shall be formally recorded, approved, and communicated.

29. Role conflicts, unclear accountability, or gaps in responsibility shall be escalated to the ISMS Manager and relevant management for resolution.

30. The organisation shall retain evidence of assigned and communicated information security responsibilities in accordance with document control and records management requirements.

31. Personnel shall perform assigned information security responsibilities in accordance with approved policies, procedures, standards, contractual obligations, and applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

32. Failure to fulfil assigned information security responsibilities shall be managed through appropriate performance management, supplier management, contractual, disciplinary, or corrective action processes.

33. The organisation shall ensure that personnel assigned ISMS responsibilities have appropriate competence, awareness, training, and support to fulfil those responsibilities effectively.

34. The organisation shall periodically monitor whether assigned roles, responsibilities, and authorities remain appropriate, understood, implemented, and effective.

35. The organisation shall ensure that information security roles and responsibilities are considered during organisational design, recruitment, onboarding, project initiation, system implementation, service transition, outsourcing, and offboarding.

The following minimum ISMS responsibility assignments shall be maintained:

| ISMS Area | Accountable Role | Minimum Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ISMS governance | Top Management | Provide leadership, approve ISMS direction, ensure responsibilities and authorities are assigned, and review ISMS performance. |
| ISMS coordination | ISMS Manager / Information Security Manager | Coordinate ISMS operation, maintain ISMS documentation, support risk management, monitor performance, and report to management. |
| ISO/IEC 27001 conformity | ISMS Manager / Control Owners | Ensure relevant ISMS processes and controls are implemented, evidenced, monitored, and improved. |
| ISMS performance reporting | ISMS Manager | Report ISMS performance, risks, nonconformities, audit outcomes, control status, and improvement needs. |
| Information security risk ownership | Assigned Risk Owners | Own risk treatment decisions and residual risk acceptance within delegated authority. |
| Asset protection | Asset Owners | Ensure assets are identified, classified, protected, and handled according to requirements. |
| Control operation | Control Owners | Operate assigned controls, retain evidence, report issues, and support effectiveness reviews. |
| Access authorisation | System Owners / Data Owners / Line Managers | Approve access based on business need, least privilege, and segregation of duties. |
| Security incident management | Incident Response Lead / Security Operations | Coordinate incident response, escalation, investigation, communication, and lessons learned. |
| Supplier security | Procurement / Supplier Owner / Information Security | Ensure supplier security requirements are defined, assessed, contracted, monitored, and reviewed. |
| Internal audit | Internal Audit Function / Independent Auditor | Conduct impartial audits of the ISMS and report audit results. |
| Corrective action | Action Owners | Investigate assigned nonconformities, implement corrective actions, and provide closure evidence. |
| Legal and regulatory compliance | Legal / Compliance / Data Protection Officer | Identify applicable obligations and support compliance monitoring. |
| Personnel security | Human Resources / Line Managers | Ensure information security responsibilities are included in employment lifecycle activities. |
| Technology operations | IT Operations / System Administrators | Operate technical controls securely and in accordance with approved procedures. |

The organisation shall maintain a RACI or equivalent responsibility model for core ISMS activities. At minimum, the model shall include the following activities:

| ISMS Activity | Top Management | ISMS Manager | Risk Owner | Control Owner | Asset/System Owner | Line Manager | Internal Audit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Approve ISMS policy and objectives | A | R | C | C | C | C | I |
| Maintain ISMS scope and documentation | A | R | C | C | C | I | I |
| Conduct information security risk assessment | I | R | A | C | C | C | I |
| Approve risk treatment and residual risk | C | C | A | C | C | I | I |
| Implement risk treatment actions | I | C | A | R | R | C | I |
| Operate assigned security controls | I | C | C | A/R | R | C | I |
| Monitor control effectiveness | I | R | C | A/R | C | I | I |
| Report ISMS performance | A | R | C | C | C | I | I |
| Conduct internal ISMS audit | I | C | I | C | C | I | A/R |
| Address audit findings and nonconformities | A | C | C | R | R | C | I |
| Conduct management review | A/R | R | C | C | C | C | I |
| Manage information security incidents | I | C | C | R | R | C | I |
| Review role assignments | A | R | C | C | C | R | I |

Legend:

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| R | Responsible for performing or coordinating the activity. |
| A | Accountable for the outcome and final decision. |
| C | Consulted before or during the activity. |
| I | Informed of status, results, or decisions. |

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Top Management | Demonstrate leadership and commitment to the ISMS; ensure information security responsibilities and authorities are assigned and communicated; approve relevant policies and objectives; ensure ISMS resources are available; assign authority for ISO/IEC 27001 conformity and ISMS performance reporting; review ISMS performance and improvement needs. |
| ISMS Manager / Information Security Manager | Coordinate ISMS implementation and operation; maintain the ISMS responsibility model; support risk assessments and treatment planning; monitor control ownership; report ISMS performance; coordinate management review inputs; ensure responsibilities are reflected in ISMS documentation; escalate gaps, conflicts, and unresolved accountability issues. |
| Information Security Steering Committee / Governance Forum | Provide oversight of information security priorities, risk posture, policy compliance, resource needs, and cross-functional accountability; review significant role conflicts or responsibility gaps; support escalation and decision-making within delegated authority. |
| Risk Owners | Own assigned information security risks; approve or recommend risk treatment options; accept residual risk within delegated authority; ensure treatment actions are progressed; review risks when business or threat conditions change. |
| Control Owners | Implement, operate, and monitor assigned controls; maintain control evidence; identify control failures or weaknesses; support audits and assessments; report control status to the ISMS Manager. |
| Asset Owners | Ensure assigned information assets are identified, classified, valued where applicable, protected, accessed appropriately, retained, and disposed of in accordance with policy; approve access where delegated; define handling requirements for assets. |
| System Owners / Application Owners | Ensure security requirements are implemented throughout the system lifecycle; approve system access where delegated; ensure vulnerabilities, changes, backups, logging, and operational controls are managed; support incident response and audit activities. |
| Data Owners | Define permitted use, classification, access criteria, retention, sharing, and protection requirements for assigned data; approve access to data where delegated; support privacy, legal, and compliance obligations. |
| Line Managers | Ensure personnel understand and fulfil assigned information security responsibilities; initiate access requests and removals; support onboarding, transfers, and offboarding; escalate non-compliance or responsibility conflicts; ensure job duties reflect security obligations. |
| Human Resources | Ensure information security responsibilities are included in employment lifecycle processes, including recruitment, onboarding, role changes, disciplinary processes, and termination; maintain relevant personnel records; support awareness and training coordination. |
| IT Operations | Operate infrastructure, platforms, networks, endpoints, and services securely; implement technical controls; follow approved change and incident processes; maintain operational evidence; enforce access, logging, backup, and vulnerability management requirements as assigned. |
| Security Operations / Incident Response Lead | Monitor, triage, escalate, and coordinate response to information security events and incidents; maintain incident roles and escalation paths; support post-incident reviews and improvement actions. |
| Procurement / Supplier Management | Ensure supplier security responsibilities are identified, assessed, included in contracts, monitored, and reviewed; maintain records of supplier accountability and service obligations. |
| Legal / Compliance / Data Protection Officer | Identify applicable legal, regulatory, contractual, and privacy obligations; advise on compliance responsibilities; support reviews of supplier and data protection accountability where applicable. |
| Internal Audit | Conduct independent audits of the ISMS; assess whether responsibilities and authorities are defined, communicated, implemented, and effective; report audit findings objectively; verify corrective action closure where assigned. |
| All Personnel | Understand and comply with assigned information security responsibilities; protect information assets; report information security events, incidents, weaknesses, and policy violations; complete required training; comply with applicable policies, procedures, and contractual obligations. |
| Third Parties / Suppliers | Fulfil information security responsibilities defined in contracts or agreements; protect organisational information; report incidents and weaknesses within agreed timeframes; support assurance, audit, and evidence requests where contractually required. |

The following authority levels shall be defined and maintained by the organisation:

| Decision / Authority Area | Minimum Required Authority |
|---|---|
| Approval of ISMS policy | Top Management or delegated executive authority |
| Approval of ISMS scope | Top Management |
| Approval of information security objectives | Top Management or delegated governance body |
| Acceptance of high or material residual information security risk | Top Management or approved risk governance body |
| Acceptance of medium or operational residual risk | Assigned Risk Owner within delegated authority |
| Approval of security policy exceptions | ISMS Manager and relevant Risk Owner; escalation to Top Management for high-risk exceptions |
| Approval of privileged access | System Owner and appropriate management authority, with independent review where required |
| Approval of supplier security exceptions | Supplier Owner, Information Security, and Risk Owner |
| Closure of ISMS audit nonconformities | Internal Audit or designated verification authority, independent from the action owner where practicable |
| Approval of changes to ISMS responsibility assignments | ISMS Manager and relevant management authority |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy shall be mandatory for all personnel and applicable third parties within the ISMS scope.

The organisation shall monitor compliance with this Policy through appropriate governance, assurance, and operational activities, including:

| Monitoring Activity | Responsible Role | Minimum Frequency | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Review of ISMS role and responsibility matrix | ISMS Manager | At least annually and upon significant change | Approved RACI, responsibility matrix, governance records |
| Review of control ownership assignments | ISMS Manager / Control Owners | At least annually | Control register, Statement of Applicability, evidence tracker |
| Review of risk ownership assignments | ISMS Manager / Risk Owners | At least annually and during risk review cycles | Risk register, risk treatment plan |
| Review of asset ownership assignments | Asset Owners / ISMS Manager | At least annually | Asset register, classification records |
| Management review of ISMS performance and accountability | Top Management / ISMS Manager | At planned intervals | Management review minutes and actions |
| Internal audit of ISMS governance and control ownership | Internal Audit | As defined in the internal audit programme | Audit plan, audit report, findings |
| Access approval and segregation of duties review | System Owners / IT / Information Security | At defined intervals based on risk | Access review records, SoD assessments |
| Supplier responsibility review | Supplier Owner / Procurement / Information Security | At onboarding, renewal, and periodic review | Contracts, supplier assessments, service reviews |
| Training and awareness completion review | Human Resources / ISMS Manager | At least annually | Training records, attestations |

Non-compliance with this Policy may result in one or more of the following actions:

- corrective action under the ISMS corrective action process;
- management escalation;
- removal or modification of access rights;
- additional training or supervision;
- performance management or disciplinary action;
- supplier remediation, service credit, contractual action, or termination;
- reporting to legal, regulatory, or contractual stakeholders where required.

Where non-compliance results in an information security incident, the incident shall be managed in accordance with the organisation’s incident management requirements.

Evidence demonstrating compliance with this Policy shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s document control, records retention, and legal obligations.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where there is a justified business need and where the associated information security risk has been assessed, approved, and documented.

All exceptions shall:

1. be submitted using the organisation’s approved exception process;
2. identify the specific Policy requirement for which the exception is requested;
3. include a documented business justification;
4. include an information security risk assessment;
5. identify compensating controls where applicable;
6. specify an exception owner;
7. define an expiry date or review date;
8. be approved by the ISMS Manager and relevant Risk Owner;
9. be escalated to Top Management or the designated governance body where the exception creates high or material residual risk;
10. be recorded in the ISMS exception register.

The following minimum information shall be recorded for each exception:

| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Exception ID | Unique identifier assigned by the ISMS function |
| Requestor | Person or function requesting the exception |
| Policy Requirement | Specific clause or requirement affected |
| Business Justification | Reason the requirement cannot currently be met |
| Risk Assessment | Summary of risk, impact, likelihood, and residual risk |
| Compensating Controls | Controls implemented to reduce risk |
| Exception Owner | Individual accountable for managing the exception |
| Approval Authority | Role or governance body approving the exception |
| Effective Date | Date the exception becomes active |
| Expiry / Review Date | Date by which the exception must be reviewed or closed |
| Status | Open, approved, rejected, expired, or closed |

Exceptions shall not be used to avoid assigning accountability for ISMS responsibilities. Any temporary vacancy, delegation, or responsibility gap shall have an approved interim accountable owner.

Expired exceptions shall be treated as non-compliance unless formally renewed or closed.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur that may affect information security roles, responsibilities, or authorities, including:

- changes to ISO/IEC 27001 requirements or applicable Annex A controls;
- changes to the ISMS scope;
- organisational restructuring;
- changes in business processes, technology, services, or operating locations;
- changes in legal, regulatory, or contractual obligations;
- significant information security incidents;
- internal or external audit findings;
- changes in supplier or outsourcing arrangements;
- changes in risk appetite or risk assessment outcomes;
- identified gaps, overlaps, or conflicts in accountability.

The Policy Owner shall be responsible for coordinating review and maintenance of this Policy. Updates shall be approved in accordance with the organisation’s document control and policy approval requirements.

At minimum, each review shall confirm that:

| Review Area | Required Outcome |
|---|---|
| Alignment with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Clause 5.3 | Responsibilities and authorities for ISMS conformity and performance reporting remain assigned. |
| Alignment with Annex A.5.2 | Information security roles and responsibilities remain defined, allocated, and communicated. |
| ISMS scope relevance | Roles remain appropriate for the current ISMS scope and organisational context. |
| Accountability coverage | Key ISMS processes, risks, assets, controls, and systems have assigned owners. |
| Authority levels | Delegated authorities remain appropriate and approved. |
| Segregation of duties | Incompatible responsibilities are identified and managed. |
| Communication and awareness | Personnel and third parties understand applicable responsibilities. |
| Evidence availability | Records are retained to demonstrate assignment, communication, and review. |

Version history shall be maintained for this Policy.

| Version | Date | Description of Change | Author | Approver |

| 1.0 | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Initial issue | [Name / Role] | [Name / Role] |

ISO27-015.title: Acceptable Use Policy
ISO27-015.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Control Reference | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| [AUP-POL-001] | 1.0 | [Information Security Manager] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 | Annex A.5.10 — Acceptable Use of Information and Other Associated Assets | Internal |

## Purpose

The purpose of this Acceptable Use Policy is to define mandatory rules for the appropriate, secure, and authorised use of the organisation’s information, information systems, IT assets, communications services, and information processing facilities.

This Policy supports ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A.5.10 by ensuring that personnel understand and follow the organisation’s requirements for acceptable use of information and associated assets throughout their lifecycle, including creation, access, processing, storage, transmission, sharing, retention, and disposal.

## Scope

This Policy applies to:

- All employees, contractors, consultants, temporary workers, interns, third-party users, service providers, and any other personnel who access, process, store, transmit, or manage organisational information or associated assets.
- All information owned, processed, stored, or transmitted by or on behalf of the organisation, regardless of format, classification, location, or ownership of the device used.
- All organisational information assets and associated assets, including but not limited to:
  - End-user devices, including desktops, laptops, tablets, smartphones, and removable media.
  - Servers, applications, databases, cloud platforms, collaboration tools, and software-as-a-service services.
  - Networks, internet connectivity, email, messaging systems, telephony, video conferencing, and remote access services.
  - Physical information processing facilities, including offices, data centres, server rooms, network rooms, and secure work areas.
  - Paper records, printed materials, portable storage, backups, and archived information.
- Use of organisation-provided assets and personally owned assets where they are authorised to access or process organisational information.

This Policy applies regardless of whether access occurs from organisation premises, remote locations, third-party premises, public locations, or personal residences.

## Policy Statements

1. **Authorised Use**
   1.1. Users shall use organisational information, IT assets, communication services, and information processing facilities only for authorised business purposes and in accordance with assigned duties, contractual obligations, applicable laws, and approved organisational policies.  
   1.2. Users shall access only the information, systems, services, and facilities for which they have been explicitly authorised.  
   1.3. Users shall not attempt to bypass, disable, interfere with, or circumvent security controls, access restrictions, monitoring mechanisms, logging, content filtering, endpoint protection, or other protective measures.  
   1.4. Users shall not use organisational assets for activities that are illegal, fraudulent, malicious, discriminatory, harassing, defamatory, obscene, threatening, or otherwise inconsistent with organisational values and legal obligations.

2. **Protection of Information**
   2.1. Users shall handle organisational information in accordance with its approved classification, handling requirements, retention requirements, and any applicable legal, regulatory, contractual, or privacy obligations.  
   2.2. Users shall ensure that confidential, restricted, personal, customer, regulated, or commercially sensitive information is accessed, stored, processed, transmitted, shared, and disposed of only using approved methods and systems.  
   2.3. Users shall not disclose organisational information to unauthorised individuals, groups, third parties, public forums, social media platforms, or external services without prior authorisation and an approved business need.  
   2.4. Users shall verify recipients and communication channels before sending confidential, restricted, personal, or sensitive information.  
   2.5. Users shall not discuss confidential or sensitive organisational information in public areas, shared spaces, transport, or any location where it may be overheard by unauthorised persons.  
   2.6. Users shall protect printed, written, and displayed information from unauthorised viewing, copying, removal, or destruction.

3. **Use of Organisational IT Assets**
   3.1. Users shall take reasonable care of organisational IT assets assigned to them and shall protect such assets from loss, theft, damage, unauthorised access, and misuse.  
   3.2. Users shall not lend, transfer, sell, modify, reassign, or dispose of organisational IT assets unless authorised through approved asset management processes.  
   3.3. Users shall keep organisational devices physically secure, including when working remotely, travelling, or using shared locations.  
   3.4. Users shall promptly report lost, stolen, damaged, compromised, or suspected compromised assets in accordance with incident reporting requirements.  
   3.5. Users shall return all organisational assets, information, access tokens, removable media, documents, and credentials upon termination, role change, contract completion, or request by the organisation.

4. **User Accounts, Authentication, and Credentials**
   4.1. Users shall use only their assigned user accounts and shall not share accounts, passwords, passphrases, authentication tokens, smart cards, certificates, one-time codes, or multi-factor authentication devices with any other person.  
   4.2. Users shall maintain the confidentiality of credentials and shall not write them down, store them in unapproved locations, transmit them insecurely, or reuse them where prohibited by organisational standards.  
   4.3. Users shall use approved password managers and authentication methods where provided or mandated by the organisation.  
   4.4. Users shall lock or log out of workstations, applications, and sessions when unattended or when use is complete.  
   4.5. Users shall immediately report suspected credential disclosure, unauthorised account use, phishing attempts, or authentication anomalies.

5. **Software, Applications, and Cloud Services**
   5.1. Users shall use only approved, licensed, and authorised software, applications, browser extensions, scripts, utilities, and cloud services for organisational business.  
   5.2. Users shall not install, download, execute, or use unauthorised software, freeware, shareware, cracked software, unlicensed software, peer-to-peer tools, hacking tools, malware, or tools designed to bypass security controls.  
   5.3. Users shall not upload, store, process, or share organisational information using unauthorised personal cloud storage, personal email, consumer messaging applications, file-sharing services, artificial intelligence services, or external collaboration platforms.  
   5.4. Users shall not connect third-party applications, integrations, plug-ins, or automation tools to organisational systems unless approved through appropriate security and change management processes.  
   5.5. Users shall comply with software licensing, intellectual property, copyright, and usage restrictions.

6. **Email, Messaging, Collaboration, and Internet Use**
   6.1. Users shall use organisational email, messaging, collaboration, and internet services responsibly, professionally, and in support of authorised business activities.  
   6.2. Users shall not use organisational communication services to create, transmit, store, or distribute content that is unlawful, abusive, offensive, discriminatory, harassing, sexually explicit, defamatory, threatening, knowingly false, or malicious.  
   6.3. Users shall not open suspicious links, attachments, macros, or files from untrusted sources and shall report suspected phishing or malicious communications using approved reporting channels.  
   6.4. Users shall not auto-forward organisational email or business communications to personal email accounts or unauthorised external accounts.  
   6.5. Users shall not subscribe to non-business services, mailing lists, social media accounts, or web platforms using organisational accounts unless there is an approved business purpose.  
   6.6. Users shall not use organisational internet access to visit sites or services that are illegal, malicious, high-risk, or unrelated to authorised business where such use creates security, legal, reputational, or operational risk.

7. **Remote Working and Mobile Use**
   7.1. Users shall access organisational systems remotely only through approved remote access methods, secured networks, and authentication mechanisms.  
   7.2. Users shall ensure that remote working environments protect organisational information from unauthorised access, viewing, overhearing, recording, theft, or loss.  
   7.3. Users shall not use public or untrusted devices to access organisational systems unless explicitly authorised and technically controlled.  
   7.4. Users shall not process confidential, restricted, personal, or regulated information over public networks unless an approved secure connection is used.  
   7.5. Users shall ensure that mobile devices used for organisational purposes are protected by approved security controls, including screen lock, encryption where required, supported operating systems, and remote wipe or equivalent management capability where applicable.

8. **Personally Owned Devices and Bring Your Own Device**
   8.1. Users shall not use personally owned devices to access, store, process, or transmit organisational information unless such use is explicitly authorised under approved bring-your-own-device requirements.  
   8.2. Users shall permit required security controls on personally owned devices used for organisational purposes, including device registration, access controls, encryption, endpoint protection, mobile device management, data separation, monitoring of organisational data, and remote removal of organisational information where applicable.  
   8.3. Users shall not store organisational information locally on personally owned devices unless specifically authorised and protected in accordance with organisational security requirements.  
   8.4. Users shall promptly notify the organisation if an authorised personally owned device is lost, stolen, compromised, shared with unauthorised persons, sold, transferred, repaired, or decommissioned.

9. **Removable Media and Portable Storage**
   9.1. Users shall use removable media and portable storage only where there is an approved business need and where the media is authorised, encrypted where required, and protected from loss or unauthorised access.  
   9.2. Users shall not connect unknown, found, untrusted, or personal removable media to organisational assets or networks.  
   9.3. Users shall not copy confidential, restricted, personal, regulated, or sensitive information to removable media unless authorised and protected using approved encryption and handling controls.  
   9.4. Users shall securely return, erase, destroy, or dispose of removable media in accordance with organisational media handling and disposal requirements.

10. **Physical and Environmental Use of Facilities**
   10.1. Users shall access organisation premises, restricted areas, secure workspaces, data centres, server rooms, network rooms, and information processing facilities only when authorised.  
   10.2. Users shall not allow unauthorised individuals to tailgate, piggyback, enter restricted areas, use access badges, or access information processing facilities.  
   10.3. Users shall wear and display identification badges where required and shall challenge or report unidentified or unauthorised persons in controlled areas where safe to do so.  
   10.4. Users shall comply with clean desk and clear screen requirements to protect sensitive information from unauthorised disclosure.  
   10.5. Users shall not tamper with, relocate, connect to, disconnect, or modify network equipment, cabling, servers, security devices, power systems, environmental controls, or other infrastructure unless authorised.

11. **Use of Networks and Connectivity**
   11.1. Users shall connect organisational assets only to authorised networks and approved connectivity services.  
   11.2. Users shall not connect unauthorised wireless access points, routers, switches, modems, network bridges, cellular hotspots, storage devices, or other network equipment to organisational networks.  
   11.3. Users shall not perform network scanning, vulnerability testing, interception, packet capture, traffic redirection, credential harvesting, spoofing, denial-of-service activity, or other security testing unless formally authorised.  
   11.4. Users shall not intentionally introduce malware, unauthorised code, unauthorised automation, or disruptive activity into organisational systems or networks.

12. **Data Transfer, Sharing, and External Disclosure**
   12.1. Users shall share organisational information only with authorised recipients who have a legitimate business need and are subject to appropriate confidentiality, contractual, legal, and security obligations.
