37. Critical ICT services shall be subject to recovery testing at a frequency commensurate with business impact and risk, as defined below unless stricter requirements are approved:

| Criticality Tier | Description | Minimum Test Frequency | Minimum Test Type |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Tier 1 | Mission-critical services supporting essential operations, legal obligations, safety, revenue-critical activities, or high-impact customer commitments | At least annually | Technical recovery or failover test plus tabletop exercise |
| Tier 2 | Important services required to sustain significant business operations | At least every 18 months | Technical recovery, restoration test, or structured simulation |
| Tier 3 | Supporting services with moderate disruption impact | At least every 24 months | Tabletop, restoration sample, or walkthrough |
| Tier 4 | Non-critical services with low disruption impact | As determined by risk assessment | Walkthrough or plan review |

38. Backup restoration testing for critical information and systems shall be performed at planned intervals sufficient to demonstrate that data can be restored within approved recovery objectives.

39. Test results shall be documented, reviewed, and retained as evidence of ICT readiness and continuity capability.

40. Continuity and ICT readiness tests shall include defined success criteria, observed results, issues, corrective actions, owners, and target completion dates.

41. Identified deficiencies in continuity and ICT readiness arrangements shall be tracked to resolution through an approved corrective action process.

42. The organisation shall conduct post-incident and post-exercise reviews to identify lessons learned and improvements to information security, continuity, and ICT recovery capabilities.

43. Lessons learned from actual disruptions, near misses, exercises, audits, threat intelligence, supplier incidents, and technology changes shall be incorporated into plans, controls, training, and recovery strategies.

44. Personnel with continuity, crisis, ICT recovery, security, supplier management, or communications responsibilities shall receive appropriate training and awareness relevant to their assigned roles.

45. Personnel involved in recovery activities shall be familiar with applicable plans, escalation paths, secure recovery procedures, emergency access arrangements, and information handling requirements during disruption.

46. The organisation shall maintain continuity and ICT readiness documentation in a manner that is accessible during disruption while protected from unauthorised access, disclosure, alteration, or destruction.

47. Offline or out-of-band copies of essential continuity and ICT recovery documentation shall be maintained where necessary to support recovery during loss of primary ICT services.

48. The organisation shall ensure that continuity and ICT recovery documentation remains current following significant changes to systems, business processes, suppliers, facilities, staffing, architecture, or regulatory requirements.

49. The organisation shall ensure that recovery environments, alternate sites, backup platforms, standby systems, and recovery tooling are protected by appropriate information security controls equivalent to their risk and classification.

50. Recovery of ICT services shall include security validation prior to return to production or business use, including verification of system integrity, data integrity, access controls, malware status, logging, monitoring, and configuration baseline where applicable.

51. Services shall not be declared restored until accountable owners have confirmed that minimum service levels, information security requirements, and validation criteria have been met.

52. The organisation shall prioritise safe and secure recovery over rapid restoration where restoration without adequate security validation would create unacceptable risk.

53. Where disruption involves a suspected or confirmed cyber incident, recovery activities shall be coordinated with the information security incident response process to prevent reinfection, evidence destruction, unauthorised access, or premature restoration.

54. The organisation shall maintain records demonstrating compliance with this Policy, including Business Impact Analyses, continuity plans, ICT recovery plans, test records, backup restoration evidence, supplier assurance records, training records, post-event reviews, risk assessments, approvals, and corrective action tracking.

55. The organisation shall ensure that business continuity and ICT readiness arrangements support applicable legal, regulatory, contractual, and customer obligations, including notification requirements and data protection requirements.

56. The organisation shall define minimum evidence requirements for continuity and ICT readiness activities as follows:

| Activity | Minimum Evidence Required | Minimum Retention |
|---|---|---:|
| Business Impact Analysis | Approved BIA record, recovery objectives, dependency mapping | 3 years or until superseded |
| Continuity plan approval | Approved plan, version history, owner sign-off | 3 years or until superseded |
| ICT recovery plan approval | Approved plan, recovery objectives, technical validation | 3 years or until superseded |
| Continuity exercise | Scenario, participants, results, issues, action plan | 3 years |
| ICT recovery test | Test plan, execution evidence, outcomes, defects, approvals | 3 years |
| Backup restoration test | Restore evidence, integrity validation, timing results | 3 years |
| Emergency access use | Authorisation, access log, activities performed, post-use review | 1 year minimum or per access logging standard |
| Actual disruption review | Timeline, decisions, impacts, lessons learned, corrective actions | 5 years |
| Supplier continuity assurance | Supplier evidence, contract terms, test participation where applicable | Duration of contract plus 3 years |

57. The organisation shall ensure that continuity and ICT readiness requirements are considered during the design, acquisition, development, onboarding, outsourcing, and retirement of ICT services.

58. New or materially changed ICT services supporting critical business activities shall not enter production unless continuity and recovery requirements have been assessed, documented, and accepted by the relevant service owner.

59. The organisation shall establish measurable continuity and ICT readiness performance indicators, including plan currency, test completion, recovery objective achievement, backup success, restoration test success, critical issue closure, and supplier assurance status.

60. Management shall review continuity and ICT readiness performance at planned intervals and shall ensure that significant risks, gaps, and overdue corrective actions are addressed.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board of Directors / Governing Body | Provides oversight of organisational resilience, approves risk appetite where applicable, and receives reporting on significant continuity and ICT readiness risks. |
| Executive Management | Ensures adequate resources, sponsorship, and accountability for business continuity and ICT readiness capabilities. Approves strategic continuity and recovery priorities. |
| Business Continuity Manager | Owns the business continuity management process; coordinates Business Impact Analyses, continuity strategy, plan development, exercising, training, and improvement tracking. |
| Chief Information Officer / Head of ICT | Ensures ICT readiness capabilities are designed, implemented, maintained, and tested to meet approved recovery objectives and business continuity requirements. |
| Chief Information Security Officer / Information Security Manager | Defines information security requirements during disruption; ensures security controls are maintained during continuity and recovery activities; supports secure recovery from cyber incidents. |
| Business Process Owners | Identify critical business activities, approve Business Impact Analysis outputs, define minimum service levels, approve continuity plans, participate in testing, and validate business recovery. |
| ICT Service Owners | Maintain ICT recovery requirements, recovery plans, dependency mapping, technical recovery capabilities, recovery test evidence, and service restoration validation. |
| Crisis Management Team | Coordinates organisational response during major disruption, authorises activation of crisis-level arrangements, and directs internal and external communications as applicable. |
| Incident Response Team | Coordinates security incident response activities, especially where disruption is caused by or involves a cyber incident. Advises on secure containment, eradication, recovery, and evidence preservation. |
| Risk Management Function | Supports risk assessment, risk treatment, control monitoring, and escalation of continuity and ICT readiness risks. |
| Procurement / Supplier Management | Ensures suppliers supporting critical services are subject to appropriate continuity, recovery, information security, assurance, and contractual requirements. |
| Legal / Compliance / Privacy Function | Advises on regulatory, contractual, legal, customer, data protection, and notification obligations during disruptive events. |
| Communications / Public Relations | Coordinates authorised internal and external communications during disruption, including customer, media, and stakeholder messaging. |
| Facilities / Physical Security | Supports alternate site arrangements, physical access, environmental controls, emergency response coordination, and facility recovery requirements. |
| Human Resources | Supports workforce availability planning, emergency contact processes, staff welfare, role coverage, and continuity-related awareness. |
| Employees and Contractors | Follow applicable continuity, incident, security, and communication procedures; protect organisational information during disruption; promptly report incidents, outages, and suspected continuity issues. |
| Internal Audit | Provides independent assurance over the design and operating effectiveness of continuity and ICT readiness controls where included in the audit plan. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory.

The organisation shall monitor compliance through appropriate governance, assurance, and operational monitoring activities, including:

- review of Business Impact Analyses and recovery objectives;
- review of Business Continuity Plan and ICT Disaster Recovery Plan currency;
- review of test schedules, test results, and recovery objective achievement;
- monitoring of backup success, backup protection, and restoration test results;
- monitoring of critical ICT service availability, incidents, and recovery performance;
- review of supplier continuity and ICT recovery assurance for critical dependencies;
- tracking of corrective actions arising from exercises, incidents, audits, and risk assessments;
- review of emergency access usage and emergency changes during disruption;
- review of evidence supporting ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A.5.29 and A.5.30 compliance;
- periodic management reporting on continuity and ICT readiness status.

The following minimum compliance indicators shall be maintained and reported to management at planned intervals:

| Metric | Target |
|---|---:|
| Critical business activities with current approved BIA | 100% |
| Tier 1 and Tier 2 ICT services with approved recovery requirements | 100% |
| Critical Business Continuity Plans reviewed within required cycle | 100% |
| Critical ICT Disaster Recovery Plans reviewed within required cycle | 100% |
| Scheduled continuity and ICT recovery tests completed on time | ≥ 95% |
| Tier 1 recovery tests achieving approved RTO and RPO | ≥ 95% or formally risk accepted |
| Backup restoration tests completed for critical systems | 100% as scheduled |
| Critical corrective actions closed by due date | ≥ 90% |
| Critical supplier continuity assurance completed | 100% for in-scope suppliers |
| Emergency access reviews completed after use | 100% |

Non-compliance with this Policy may result in corrective action, risk acceptance requirements, suspension of system or service approval, supplier remediation, contract review, disciplinary action, or other management action appropriate to the severity and impact of the non-compliance.

Material non-compliance, significant continuity risk, failure to meet approved recovery objectives, or failure to maintain information security during disruption shall be escalated to Executive Management and, where appropriate, the Governing Body.

Where a disruptive event results in actual or suspected compromise of information, regulatory breach, customer-impacting outage, or failure to meet contractual obligations, the relevant incident, legal, privacy, and regulatory notification processes shall be followed.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented business justification, risk assessment, approval by authorised management, and defined compensating controls.

Exception requests shall include, at a minimum:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Requestor | Individual or function requesting the exception |
| Policy requirement | Specific requirement for which exception is requested |
| Business justification | Reason the requirement cannot be met |
| Affected assets or services | Systems, processes, information, suppliers, or locations impacted |
| Risk assessment | Confidentiality, integrity, availability, legal, regulatory, contractual, and operational impacts |
| Compensating controls | Measures to reduce risk during the exception period |
| Duration | Requested start and end date |
| Owner | Person accountable for managing the exception |
| Approval | Required management, risk, ICT, information security, and business owner approvals |
| Review date | Date by which the exception must be reviewed or closed |

Exceptions shall be time-bound and shall not exceed [maximum exception period, e.g., 12 months] unless renewed through a formal review and approval process.

Exceptions affecting Tier 1 or Tier 2 critical services, legal or regulatory obligations, customer commitments, cyber recovery capability, backup protection, or emergency access controls shall require approval from the relevant Executive Management member and the Information Security Manager.

Emergency deviations during an active disruption may be approved by the Crisis Management Team, Incident Response Lead, Chief Information Officer, or other authorised executive where delay would materially increase harm. Such deviations shall be documented retrospectively, reviewed after stabilisation, and either closed or converted into a formal exception.

Approved exceptions shall be recorded in an exceptions register and reviewed periodically by the Policy Owner, Risk Management, and Information Security.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur that may affect business continuity or ICT readiness requirements.

Reviews shall consider, at a minimum:

- changes to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 requirements, applicable laws, regulations, contractual commitments, or customer obligations;
- changes to organisational strategy, products, services, operating model, locations, or critical business processes;
- changes to ICT architecture, cloud services, suppliers, systems, networks, data flows, or recovery capabilities;
- results from Business Impact Analyses, risk assessments, audits, continuity exercises, ICT recovery tests, and backup restoration tests;
- actual disruptions, cyber incidents, near misses, supplier incidents, and lessons learned;
- changes in threat landscape, including ransomware, destructive malware, cloud outages, supply chain attacks, and regional disruption scenarios;
- performance against continuity and ICT readiness metrics;
- open corrective actions, exceptions, and risk acceptances.

The Policy Owner shall ensure that this Policy remains aligned with the organisation’s Information Security Management System, business continuity arrangements, ICT disaster recovery capabilities, risk appetite, and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A.5.29 and A.5.30 requirements.

Material changes to this Policy shall be approved by Executive Management or the designated governance body.

Superseded versions of this Policy shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s document retention requirements.

ISO27-026.title: Privacy / PII Protection Policy
ISO27-026.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Control Reference | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| [POL-PRIV-001] | 1.0 | Data Protection Officer / Privacy Officer | [Effective Date] | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 | Annex A.5.34 — Privacy and Protection of PII | Internal |

## Purpose

The purpose of this Privacy / Personally Identifiable Information Protection Policy is to establish mandatory requirements for the protection of personally identifiable information (PII) processed by the organisation.

This Policy supports implementation of ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A.5.34 by ensuring that PII is identified, handled, protected, retained, transferred and disposed of in accordance with applicable privacy laws, regulatory obligations, contractual requirements and the organisation’s information security management system (ISMS).

This Policy is intended to ensure that the organisation:

- Processes PII lawfully, fairly and transparently.
- Protects the confidentiality, integrity and availability of PII.
- Applies appropriate privacy and security controls throughout the PII lifecycle.
- Minimises the risk of unauthorised access, disclosure, alteration, loss or misuse of PII.
- Demonstrates accountability for privacy and PII protection obligations.

## Scope

This Policy applies to:

- All employees, contractors, temporary workers, consultants, interns and third parties who access, process, store, transmit or manage PII on behalf of the organisation.
- All PII processed by the organisation, regardless of format, location, system, process or medium.
- All information assets, applications, databases, cloud services, endpoints, networks, physical records, backups and removable media that store or process PII.
- All processing activities involving PII, including collection, recording, use, access, sharing, transfer, retention, archival, anonymisation, pseudonymisation and destruction.
- All business units, subsidiaries and locations within the scope of the ISMS.

For the purposes of this Policy:

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| PII | Any information that identifies, relates to, describes, is reasonably capable of being associated with, or could reasonably be linked directly or indirectly to an identified or identifiable natural person. |
| Sensitive PII | PII that presents a higher privacy or security risk if compromised, including government identifiers, financial data, authentication credentials, health data, biometric data, precise location data, children’s data, and any special categories of personal data defined by applicable law. |
| Processing | Any operation performed on PII, including collection, recording, organisation, structuring, storage, adaptation, retrieval, consultation, use, disclosure, transmission, restriction, erasure or destruction. |
| Data Subject | The natural person to whom PII relates. |
| Controller | The party that determines the purposes and means of processing PII. |
| Processor | The party that processes PII on behalf of a controller. |

## Policy Statements

1. The organisation shall identify, document and maintain an inventory of processing activities involving PII, including the purpose of processing, categories of PII, data subjects, systems, storage locations, recipients, retention periods and applicable legal or contractual obligations.

2. The organisation shall process PII only where there is a documented and lawful basis, legitimate business purpose, contractual obligation, regulatory requirement or other approved justification.

3. The organisation shall collect only the minimum PII necessary to fulfil a documented and approved business purpose.

4. The organisation shall not process PII for purposes that are incompatible with the original stated purpose unless permitted by applicable law, supported by an approved lawful basis and communicated where required.

5. The organisation shall classify PII in accordance with the organisation’s information classification scheme and apply handling controls appropriate to its sensitivity, volume, context and risk.

6. The organisation shall identify and classify sensitive PII and apply enhanced protection measures, including stricter access controls, encryption, monitoring and approval requirements.

7. The organisation shall provide appropriate privacy notices or disclosures to data subjects where required by applicable law, contract or organisational policy.

8. The organisation shall maintain mechanisms to receive, assess and respond to data subject rights requests, including requests for access, correction, deletion, restriction, portability, objection or withdrawal of consent, where applicable.

9. The organisation shall maintain records of consent where consent is used as the lawful basis for processing PII.

10. The organisation shall ensure consent is freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous where required, and shall provide an effective mechanism for withdrawal of consent.

11. The organisation shall implement access controls to ensure PII is accessible only to authorised personnel and systems based on the principles of least privilege and need to know.

12. The organisation shall review access to systems and repositories containing PII at defined intervals and upon role change, transfer or termination.

13. Privileged access to PII shall be restricted, monitored and subject to enhanced authentication and authorisation controls.

14. The organisation shall use strong authentication mechanisms for access to systems that store or process PII, commensurate with the risk and sensitivity of the PII.

15. The organisation shall protect PII from unauthorised disclosure during storage, processing and transmission through appropriate technical and organisational controls.

16. The organisation shall encrypt sensitive PII at rest and in transit where technically feasible and proportionate to risk.

17. Where encryption is not feasible, the organisation shall document the rationale and implement compensating controls approved through the exception process.

18. The organisation shall apply pseudonymisation, anonymisation, tokenisation, masking or redaction where appropriate to reduce privacy risk.

19. PII used for development, testing, training or analytics shall be anonymised, pseudonymised or otherwise protected unless use of identifiable PII has been formally approved and risk assessed.

20. The organisation shall not use production PII in non-production environments unless there is a documented business requirement, approved risk assessment and equivalent security controls.

21. The organisation shall establish and maintain retention schedules for PII based on legal, regulatory, contractual and business requirements.

22. PII shall not be retained longer than necessary for the purpose for which it was collected, unless retention is required by law, litigation hold, contractual obligation or approved business need.

23. The organisation shall securely delete, destroy, anonymise or return PII at the end of its approved retention period or upon termination of processing, unless continued retention is legally required.

24. Disposal of PII shall be performed using approved secure disposal methods appropriate to the medium and sensitivity of the PII.

25. The organisation shall maintain evidence of secure destruction for PII where required by law, contract, risk assessment or internal procedure.

26. The organisation shall conduct privacy risk assessments for new or materially changed processing activities involving PII.

27. The organisation shall conduct Data Protection Impact Assessments or equivalent privacy impact assessments for processing likely to result in high risk to individuals, including large-scale processing, profiling, automated decision-making, sensitive PII processing or systematic monitoring.

28. Privacy and PII protection requirements shall be incorporated into the design, development, acquisition and change management of systems, services and business processes.

29. The organisation shall apply privacy by design and privacy by default principles when implementing systems and processes that handle PII.

30. The organisation shall ensure that default settings in systems and services minimise unnecessary collection, use, sharing, visibility and retention of PII.

31. The organisation shall ensure that third parties processing PII on behalf of the organisation are subject to documented due diligence, risk assessment and contractual privacy and security obligations.

32. Contracts with third parties that process PII shall define the subject matter, duration, nature and purpose of processing, categories of PII, categories of data subjects, confidentiality obligations, security requirements, subcontracting restrictions, breach notification requirements, audit rights, return or deletion obligations and cross-border transfer requirements.

33. The organisation shall maintain an inventory of third parties and subprocessors that process PII on behalf of the organisation.

34. Third parties shall be authorised to process PII only in accordance with documented instructions and applicable contractual terms.

35. The organisation shall assess and manage risks associated with cross-border transfers of PII and shall implement appropriate legal, contractual and technical safeguards before such transfers occur.

36. PII shall not be transferred to another jurisdiction unless the transfer is permitted under applicable privacy law and approved organisational processes.

37. The organisation shall ensure that PII shared internally is limited to authorised recipients and approved business purposes.

38. The organisation shall prohibit unauthorised copying, downloading, printing, emailing, uploading or removal of PII from approved systems or locations.

39. PII shall not be stored in unauthorised repositories, personal cloud storage, unmanaged devices, removable media or unapproved messaging platforms.

40. The organisation shall define approved channels and methods for transmitting PII, including secure file transfer, encrypted email, approved collaboration platforms or other controlled mechanisms.

41. The organisation shall log and monitor access to sensitive PII and high-risk PII processing environments, where technically feasible and proportionate to risk.

42. Monitoring activities involving PII shall be conducted in accordance with applicable laws, internal policies and documented legitimate purposes.

43. The organisation shall protect audit logs containing PII from unauthorised access, alteration and deletion.

44. The organisation shall establish and maintain procedures for identifying, reporting, investigating, managing and notifying personal data breaches or suspected compromises of PII.

45. Suspected or confirmed PII breaches shall be reported immediately through the organisation’s incident reporting channels.

46. The organisation shall assess whether a PII breach requires notification to regulators, affected individuals, customers, partners or other stakeholders within legally required timeframes.

47. The organisation shall maintain records of PII incidents and breaches, including facts, effects, decisions, notifications, remediation actions and lessons learned.

48. Personnel with access to PII shall complete privacy and information security awareness training at onboarding and periodically thereafter.

49. Personnel with roles involving high-risk PII processing shall receive role-specific privacy and PII protection training.

50. The organisation shall ensure that confidentiality obligations apply to employees, contractors and third parties with access to PII.

51. The organisation shall maintain appropriate physical security controls to protect physical records and devices containing PII from unauthorised access, loss, theft or damage.

52. Printed or physical PII shall be secured when unattended and disposed of using approved secure destruction methods.

53. The organisation shall ensure that backup copies containing PII are protected using access controls, encryption where appropriate, secure storage and defined retention periods.

54. The organisation shall ensure that PII protection requirements are included in business continuity, disaster recovery and incident response planning where PII is processed by critical services.

55. The organisation shall maintain documented privacy governance processes to oversee compliance with this Policy and applicable PII protection obligations.

56. The organisation shall maintain evidence demonstrating implementation of PII protection controls, including inventories, risk assessments, approvals, training records, access reviews, contracts, incident records and audit results.

57. The organisation shall ensure that conflicts between this Policy and applicable privacy laws or contractual requirements are escalated to the Data Protection Officer / Privacy Officer and Legal Counsel for resolution.

58. Where multiple privacy or PII protection requirements apply, the organisation shall apply the requirement that provides the greater level of protection unless legally prohibited.

59. The organisation shall ensure that automated decision-making or profiling involving PII is assessed, documented and controlled where it may produce legal, significant or material effects on individuals.

60. The organisation shall maintain appropriate governance and approval for any processing of children’s PII or other legally protected categories of PII.

61. The organisation shall establish and maintain a lawful, documented process for responding to requests from law enforcement, regulators or public authorities for disclosure of PII.

62. The organisation shall not disclose PII to public authorities or external parties unless legally required, contractually authorised or approved by Legal Counsel and the Data Protection Officer / Privacy Officer.

63. The organisation shall ensure that changes to systems, suppliers, processing purposes, data flows or legal requirements that affect PII are reviewed for privacy impact before implementation.

64. The organisation shall define and maintain privacy control requirements as part of the ISMS risk treatment process.

65. The organisation shall protect PII in accordance with applicable privacy laws and regulations in jurisdictions where the organisation operates, offers goods or services, monitors individuals, or otherwise falls within legal scope.

The following minimum control expectations shall apply to PII based on sensitivity:

| PII Category | Examples | Minimum Required Protection |
|---|---|---|
| General PII | Name, business contact details, customer identifier | Access limited by business need; approved storage location; retention applied; secure transmission where external |
| Confidential PII | Personal contact details, date of birth, employee records, customer account information | Role-based access; encryption in transit; logging where feasible; retention schedule; restricted sharing |
| Sensitive PII | Government identifiers, financial account data, health data, credentials, biometrics, precise location data | Encryption at rest and in transit; enhanced access control; monitoring; formal approval for sharing; privacy risk assessment |
| High-Risk PII Processing | Large-scale profiling, children’s data, automated decisions, cross-border transfers, sensitive PII at scale | Privacy impact assessment; DPO / Privacy Officer review; Legal review where required; senior risk acceptance if residual risk remains |

The following retention and disposal expectations shall apply unless superseded by approved legal, regulatory or contractual requirements:

| PII Record Type | Retention Requirement | Disposal Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Customer PII | Retain only for the customer relationship and approved post-relationship retention period | Secure deletion, anonymisation or return according to approved retention schedule |
| Employee PII | Retain for employment period plus statutory retention period | Secure deletion or destruction after retention expiry |
| Candidate / Applicant PII | Retain only for recruitment purpose and approved talent pool period where consent or lawful basis exists | Secure deletion after recruitment retention period |
| Marketing PII | Retain until consent withdrawal, opt-out, inactivity threshold or approved retention expiry | Suppression or deletion in accordance with legal requirements |
| Authentication / Access Logs Containing PII | Retain for security monitoring and audit period | Secure deletion after log retention period |
| Incident Records Containing PII | Retain for investigation, legal, regulatory and audit purposes | Secure archival or deletion after approved retention period |

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board / Executive Management | Provide oversight and support for privacy and PII protection; ensure adequate resources are available; approve significant risk treatment decisions where required. |
| Data Protection Officer / Privacy Officer | Own this Policy; advise on privacy obligations; oversee PII protection governance; review privacy impact assessments; advise on data subject rights, breach notification and cross-border transfers; monitor compliance with privacy requirements. |
| Chief Information Security Officer / Information Security Manager | Ensure technical and organisational security controls are implemented to protect PII; integrate PII protection into the ISMS; oversee security risk assessments, incident response and control monitoring. |
| Legal Counsel | Advise on applicable privacy laws, regulatory obligations, contractual terms, lawful bases for processing, data transfer mechanisms and disclosure requests. |
| Data Owners / Business Process Owners | Identify and document PII processing activities; define business purposes; approve access; ensure retention requirements are followed; ensure processing is consistent with approved purposes. |
| System Owners / Application Owners | Implement and maintain security controls for systems processing PII; ensure logging, access controls, encryption, retention and secure deletion capabilities are supported. |
| Information Asset Owners | Classify assets containing PII; ensure appropriate handling, storage, access and disposal controls are applied. |
| Procurement / Vendor Management | Ensure suppliers processing PII undergo due diligence, contractual review, onboarding approval and ongoing monitoring. |
| Human Resources | Ensure workforce privacy obligations, confidentiality terms, awareness training, employee records protection and disciplinary processes are maintained. |
| IT Operations | Implement access controls, encryption, backup protection, monitoring, secure configuration and secure disposal of systems and media containing PII. |
| Security Operations / Incident Response Team | Detect, triage, investigate and respond to suspected or confirmed PII incidents; support breach assessment and containment; maintain incident evidence. |
| Employees, Contractors and Third Parties | Protect PII in accordance with this Policy; complete required training; use approved systems and channels; report suspected incidents immediately; process PII only as authorised. |
| Internal Audit / Compliance Function | Conduct independent reviews of compliance with this Policy, applicable ISO/IEC 27001:2022 control requirements and related privacy obligations. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory.

The organisation shall monitor compliance with this Policy through a risk-based assurance programme that may include:

- ISMS internal audits.
- Privacy compliance reviews.
- Access reviews for systems containing PII.
- Supplier assurance and contract compliance reviews.
- Technical control testing.
- Vulnerability and configuration assessments.
- Security monitoring and log review.
- Incident and breach trend analysis.
- Training completion monitoring.
- Review of PII inventories and processing records.
- Review of privacy impact assessments and risk treatment plans.

The following minimum monitoring activities shall be performed:

| Activity | Minimum Frequency | Responsible Role | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Review PII processing inventory | At least annually and upon material change | Data Protection Officer / Privacy Officer; Data Owners | Updated processing inventory |
| Review access to sensitive PII systems | At least quarterly | System Owners; Data Owners | Access review records and remediation actions |
| Review third parties processing PII | At onboarding and at least annually for high-risk suppliers | Procurement / Vendor Management; Privacy Officer | Due diligence records, risk assessments, contracts |
| Privacy impact assessments for high-risk processing | Before implementation and upon material change | Business Process Owner; Privacy Officer | Approved assessment and risk treatment plan |
| Privacy and security awareness training | At onboarding and annually | Human Resources; Information Security | Training completion records |
| Test PII incident response process | At least annually | Incident Response Team; Privacy Officer | Exercise report and lessons learned |
| Review retention and disposal compliance | At least annually | Data Owners; Records Management | Retention review and disposal evidence |
| Internal audit of PII protection controls | According to audit plan | Internal Audit / Compliance | Audit report and corrective action plan |

Non-compliance with this Policy may result in:

- Revocation or restriction of system access.
- Mandatory retraining.
- Corrective or disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment or contract.
- Supplier remediation, suspension or termination.
- Notification to regulators, customers or affected individuals where required.
- Legal action where misconduct, negligence or unlawful processing has occurred.

Violations or suspected violations of this Policy shall be reported to the Data Protection Officer / Privacy Officer, Information Security Manager, Legal Counsel or through the organisation’s approved reporting channels.

The organisation shall maintain records of compliance activities, identified nonconformities, corrective actions and management decisions in accordance with ISMS document control and record retention requirements.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented business justification and the associated privacy and information security risks have been assessed, approved and formally accepted.

Exception requests shall include, at minimum:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Requestor | Individual or business owner requesting the exception |
| Affected process, system or supplier | The scope of the requested exception |
| Policy requirement impacted | Specific statement or control requirement for which exception is requested |
| PII involved | Categories, sensitivity and approximate volume of PII affected |
| Business justification | Reason compliance cannot be achieved within required timeframe |
| Risk assessment | Privacy, legal, regulatory, contractual and security risks |
| Compensating controls | Measures to reduce risk during the exception period |
| Duration | Requested start and end date; open-ended exceptions are not permitted |
| Approvals | Required approval from Data Owner, Privacy Officer, Information Security and Legal Counsel where applicable |
| Review date | Date by which the exception shall be reassessed or closed |

Exceptions involving sensitive PII, high-risk processing, regulatory obligations, cross-border transfers, breach notification requirements or significant residual risk shall require approval by the Data Protection Officer / Privacy Officer, Information Security Manager and Legal Counsel. Senior management approval shall be required where residual risk exceeds the organisation’s risk appetite.

Approved exceptions shall:

- Be time-bound.
- Be recorded in the organisation’s exception register.
- Include compensating controls where feasible.
- Be reviewed before expiry.
- Be closed when compliance is achieved or when the underlying business need no longer exists.

Expired exceptions shall be treated as non-compliance unless renewed through the formal exception process.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur that may affect PII protection obligations, including:

- Changes to applicable privacy laws, regulations or regulatory guidance.
- Changes to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 requirements or ISMS scope.
- New or materially changed PII processing activities.
- Significant changes to systems, suppliers, jurisdictions or data flows.
- Privacy incidents, breaches, audit findings or control failures.
- Changes to organisational structure, roles or responsibilities.
- Changes to risk appetite or approved risk treatment plans.

The Data Protection Officer / Privacy Officer shall own and coordinate review of this Policy with input from Information Security, Legal Counsel, Compliance, Data Owners, IT and other relevant stakeholders.

Policy changes shall be approved in accordance with the organisation’s document governance process. The current approved version shall be made available to all relevant personnel and communicated to stakeholders with responsibilities for PII protection.

Superseded versions shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s document retention and ISMS record control requirements.

ISO27-027.title: Document Control Procedure
ISO27-027.content:
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | [DOCUMENT-ID] |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | Information Security Manager |
| Effective Date | [EFFECTIVE-DATE] |
| Framework | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 |
| Control Reference | Clause 7.5 — Documented Information |
| Classification | Internal |

## Purpose

This procedure defines how documented information required by the Information Security Management System (ISMS) is created, reviewed, approved, distributed, controlled, retained, protected, and disposed of in accordance with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Clause 7.5.

The purpose is to ensure that ISMS documentation is:

- Available and suitable for use where and when needed.
- Adequately protected from loss of confidentiality, improper use, or loss of integrity.
- Properly identified, described, reviewed, approved, version controlled, and retained.
- Withdrawn from use when obsolete.
- Managed consistently across the document lifecycle.

This procedure supports compliance with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 requirements for documented information, including creation and updating, control, availability, preservation, distribution, access, retrieval, use, storage, change control, retention, and disposition.

## Scope

This procedure applies to all documented information required by the ISMS or determined by the organisation as necessary for the effectiveness of the ISMS, including but not limited to:

- ISMS scope statement.
- Information security policy and supporting policies.
- Risk assessment and risk treatment methodology.
- Risk assessment records.
- Risk treatment plan.
- Statement of Applicability.
- Information security objectives.
- Procedures, standards, guidelines, and work instructions.
- Internal audit programme, plans, checklists, and reports.
- Management review inputs and outputs.
- Corrective action records.
- Evidence of competence, awareness, training, and communication.
- Records demonstrating operation of controls.
- Supplier security documentation relevant to the ISMS.
- Legal, regulatory, contractual, and compliance records relevant to information security.
- Other ISMS records retained as evidence of conformity and effective operation.

This procedure applies to documented information in all formats and media, including:

- Electronic documents.
- Records stored in governance, risk and compliance systems.
- Tickets, approvals, workflow records, and logs.
- Spreadsheets and registers.
- Signed PDFs.
- Email approvals where explicitly permitted.
- Paper records, where used.

This procedure applies to all personnel involved in creating, reviewing, approving, using, maintaining, or retiring ISMS documented information, including employees, contractors, and relevant third parties.

## Prerequisites & Inputs

The following prerequisites must be in place before this procedure is performed:

| Prerequisite | Description | Responsible Role |
|---|---|---|
| Approved ISMS document repository | A designated controlled repository for storing current and approved ISMS documentation. | ISMS Document Controller |
| Defined document owners | Each controlled ISMS document must have an assigned owner accountable for content accuracy and maintenance. | Information Security Manager |
| Access control model | Role-based access to create, edit, approve, view, archive, and delete ISMS documents. | Repository Administrator |
| Document classification scheme | Classification labels must be available and aligned to the organisation’s information classification requirements. | Information Security Manager |
| Retention schedule | Retention periods for ISMS documents and records must be defined and approved. | Compliance Manager |
| Approval workflow | A defined approval process or workflow must exist for controlled ISMS documents. | ISMS Document Controller |
| Version control method | A method must exist for assigning, tracking, and preserving document versions. | ISMS Document Controller |
| Change request mechanism | A method must exist for initiating document creation, revision, withdrawal, or archival. | Document Owner |

Inputs to this procedure may include:

- New or changed ISO/IEC 27001:2022 requirements.
- Results of risk assessments or risk treatment activities.
- Internal audit findings.
- External audit findings.
- Corrective actions.
- Management review decisions.
- Changes to legal, regulatory, or contractual requirements.
- Organisational changes.
- Changes to assets, processes, technologies, suppliers, or services.
- User feedback on existing ISMS documents.
- Scheduled periodic document review.
- Identified need for new or revised control documentation.

## Step-by-Step Procedure (numbered)

1. **Identify the need for documented information**

   1.1. The Document Owner, Information Security Manager, Compliance Manager, Internal Auditor, control owner, or process owner identifies the need to create, update, withdraw, or archive documented information.

   1.2. The need may arise from one or more of the following:

   - ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Clause 7.5 requirements.
   - Evidence required to demonstrate ISMS conformity.
   - Operation of ISMS processes.
   - Implementation or operation of Annex A controls.
   - Audit findings or corrective actions.
   - Risk assessment or risk treatment activities.
   - Management review decisions.
   - Changes in organisational context, interested parties, or ISMS scope.
   - Legal, regulatory, or contractual obligations.
   - Periodic review cycle.

   1.3. The initiator records the request using the approved document change request method.

   | Field | Required Information |
   |---|---|
   | Request type | Create, revise, retire, archive, restore, or emergency update |
   | Document title | Name of the document or proposed document |
   | Business justification | Reason for the request |
   | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 relevance | Applicable clause, Annex A control, or ISMS process |
   | Requested by | Name or role of requester |
   | Requested date | Date request submitted |
   | Required completion date | Target completion date, if applicable |
   | Impacted stakeholders | Functions, teams, or third parties affected |
   | Classification | Proposed information classification |
   | Retention requirement | Proposed retention period or record type |

2. **Determine whether the document is controlled documented information**

   2.1. The ISMS Document Controller reviews the request and determines whether the item is controlled documented information under the ISMS.

   2.2. A document or record must be controlled where it:

   - Is required by ISO/IEC 27001:2022.
   - Is required by the organisation for effective ISMS operation.
   - Provides evidence of conformity.
   - Defines a mandatory or repeatable security process.
   - Supports information security risk management.
   - Supports legal, regulatory, contractual, or audit obligations.
   - Requires approval, version control, retention, or restricted access.

   2.3. If the item is not controlled documented information, the ISMS Document Controller records the decision and directs the requester to the appropriate unmanaged or operational storage location.

   2.4. If the item is controlled documented information, the procedure continues.

3. **Assign document metadata**

   3.1. The ISMS Document Controller assigns or confirms the required document metadata before drafting or revision.

   3.2. Each controlled ISMS document must include, at minimum:

   | Metadata Element | Requirement |
   |---|---|
   | Document ID | Unique identifier assigned according to the ISMS document naming convention |
   | Title | Clear and descriptive document title |
   | Version | Version number using the approved version numbering method |
   | Owner | Role accountable for maintaining the document |
   | Approver | Role authorised to approve the document |
   | Effective date | Date from which the document applies |
   | Review date or frequency | Next scheduled review or approved review interval |
   | Classification | Information classification label |
   | Framework reference | Relevant ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clause or Annex A control reference |
   | Status | Draft, in review, approved, effective, superseded, archived, or withdrawn |
   | Retention period | Applicable retention rule |
   | Repository location | Controlled storage location |
   | Access group | Authorised users or groups |

   3.3. Controlled documents must use approved organisational templates where available.

   3.4. The document title, owner, classification, and control reference must be accurate and suitable for the document purpose.

4. **Create or revise the documented information**

   4.1. The Document Owner drafts or revises the document using the approved template and style appropriate to the artifact type.

   4.2. The content must be:

   - Accurate, complete, and suitable for its intended use.
   - Aligned to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 requirements.
   - Consistent with approved ISMS policies and risk treatment decisions.
   - Written clearly enough for intended users to understand their responsibilities.
   - Free from obsolete references, unsupported claims, or conflicting requirements.
   - Classified according to the organisation’s information classification scheme.
   - Traceable to applicable ISMS requirements, controls, processes, or records.

   4.3. Where the document is a procedure, work instruction, checklist, or operational standard, the Document Owner must ensure it defines sufficient detail for consistent execution.

   4.4. Where the document is a record, form, register, or evidence artifact, the Document Owner must ensure it contains enough information to demonstrate conformity and effective ISMS operation.

   4.5. The Document Owner must avoid storing current controlled ISMS documentation in unmanaged locations, personal drives, local folders, or email inboxes.

5. **Apply version control**

   5.1. The ISMS Document Controller ensures that version control is applied before review and approval.

   5.2. The following versioning convention must be used unless otherwise approved:

   | Version Type | Format | Use |
   |---|---|---|
   | Initial draft | 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 | Draft versions before first approval |
   | First approved issue | 1.0 | First formally approved version |
   | Minor revision | 1.1, 1.2, 1.3 | Non-material updates that do not change requirements or responsibilities |
   | Major revision | 2.0, 3.0 | Material changes to scope, requirements, roles, process, controls, or obligations |
   | Emergency revision | Current version plus emergency notation in change record | Urgent change requiring accelerated approval |

   5.3. Each controlled document must include or be linked to a change history.

   | Version | Date | Description of Change | Author | Reviewer | Approver |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | 1.0 | [DATE] | Initial approved issue | [ROLE/NAME] | [ROLE/NAME] | [ROLE/NAME] |

   5.4. The ISMS Document Controller must ensure that superseded versions are removed from general use and retained only in the controlled archive.

   5.5. Obsolete documents must be clearly marked as superseded, archived, or withdrawn to prevent unintended use.

6. **Review the document**

   6.1. The Document Owner submits the draft or revised document for review.

   6.2. Reviewers must be selected based on relevance to the document content. Reviewers may include:

   - Information Security Manager.
   - Compliance Manager.
   - Risk Manager.
   - Control owner.
   - Process owner.
   - Legal representative.
   - Human Resources representative.
   - IT Operations representative.
   - Privacy or Data Protection representative.
   - Internal Audit representative.
   - Supplier or third-party management representative.

   6.3. Reviewers assess whether the document is:

   - Suitable for its intended purpose.
   - Aligned to ISO/IEC 27001:2022.
   - Consistent with ISMS scope, policies, objectives, risk assessment, and Statement of Applicability.
   - Operationally feasible.
   - Accurate and complete.
   - Appropriately classified.
   - Supported by necessary records or forms.
   - Free of conflicts with existing approved documentation.
   - Compliant with legal, regulatory, and contractual obligations.
   - Assigned an appropriate retention period.

   6.4. Reviewer comments must be recorded in the approved review workflow, repository comment function, or document change request record.

   6.5. The Document Owner resolves reviewer comments before submission for approval.

   6.6. Unresolved material comments must be escalated to the Information Security Manager.

7. **Approve the document prior to issue**

   7.1. Controlled ISMS documents must be reviewed and approved for suitability and adequacy before issue.

   7.2. The approver must have authority appropriate to the document type and impact.

   | Document Type | Minimum Approver |
   |---|---|
   | ISMS scope | Executive management or ISMS governance body |
   | Information security policy | Executive management or designated senior accountable owner |
   | ISMS procedures | Information Security Manager |
   | Risk assessment methodology | Information Security Manager and Risk Manager |
   | Risk treatment plan | Risk owner or executive management, as applicable |
   | Statement of Applicability | Information Security Manager and executive management or ISMS governance body |
   | Standards and work instructions | Relevant control owner and Information Security Manager |
   | ISMS records and forms | Document Owner or Information Security Manager |
   | Internal audit documentation | Internal Audit Lead |
   | Management review records | Chair of management review or executive sponsor |

   7.3. Approval may be evidenced through:

   - Electronic workflow approval.
   - Digital signature.
   - Repository approval status.
   - Meeting minutes recording formal approval.
   - Email approval retained as an ISMS record, where workflow approval is not available.

   7.4. Approval evidence must identify:

   - Document title and version.
   - Approver name or role.
   - Approval date.
   - Approval decision.
   - Any conditions of approval.

   7.5. Documents must not be published as approved or effective until approval evidence has been captured.

8. **Publish and distribute the approved document**

   8.1. The ISMS Document Controller publishes the approved version to the controlled ISMS repository.

   8.2. The ISMS Document Controller ensures that:

   - Only the current approved version is available for normal use.
   - Access permissions are consistent with classification and need-to-know.
   - The document is retrievable by authorised users.
   - The effective date is visible.
   - Superseded versions are removed from current access locations.
   - External distribution is controlled, where applicable.

   8.3. The Document Owner identifies affected users and stakeholders requiring notification, training, or acknowledgement.

   8.4. Distribution may be performed through:

   - Controlled repository notification.
   - ISMS communication channel.
   - Training or awareness platform.
   - Email distribution with link to the controlled document.
   - Governance or management meeting communication.
   - Supplier portal or contractual communication route, where applicable.

   8.5. Where distributed outside the organisation, the Document Owner must ensure that:

   - External distribution is authorised.
   - The classification permits external release.
   - Recipients are identified.
   - Distribution records are retained.
   - Any confidentiality, contractual, or non-disclosure requirements are met.
   - Uncontrolled copies are clearly marked unless controlled external access is provided.

9. **Control access, retrieval, and use**

   9.1. The Repository Administrator grants access to controlled documented information based on approved roles, classification, and need-to-know.

   9.2. Edit access must be restricted to authorised Document Owners, delegates, ISMS Document Controllers, and approved contributors.

   9.3. Approval rights must be restricted to authorised approvers.

   9.4. Read access must be sufficient to ensure that personnel can access information required to perform their ISMS responsibilities.

   9.5. The repository must support retrieval using document title, document ID, owner, classification, status, or control reference.

   9.6. Downloading, printing, or forwarding restricted documents must be controlled according to the applicable classification and acceptable use requirements.

   9.7. Users must refer to the controlled repository as the authoritative source. Copies downloaded, printed, or emailed are considered uncontrolled unless explicitly designated as controlled copies.

10. **Protect documented information**

   10.1. The ISMS Document Controller and Repository Administrator must ensure that documented information is protected from:

   - Unauthorised access.
   - Unauthorised modification.
   - Accidental deletion.
   - Loss of confidentiality.
   - Loss of integrity.
   - Loss of availability.
   - Improper use.
   - Obsolescence or unintended use.

   10.2. Protection measures must include, as applicable:

   | Protection Requirement | Control Measure |
   |---|---|
   | Confidentiality | Classification labels, role-based access, encryption where required |
   | Integrity | Version control, approval workflow, restricted edit permissions |
   | Availability | Central repository, backup, recovery capability, access monitoring |
   | Authenticity | Approval evidence, change history, metadata |
   | Preservation | Retention schedule, archival controls, format readability |
   | Prevention of unintended use | Superseded watermark, archive segregation, current-version-only publication |

   10.3. Repositories storing controlled ISMS documentation must be backed up or otherwise protected in accordance with approved backup and resilience requirements.

   10.4. Access to restricted ISMS documents must be reviewed periodically or upon role change, termination, or classification change.

11. **Maintain the document register**

   11.1. The ISMS Document Controller maintains a document register of controlled ISMS documented information.

   11.2. The register must include, at minimum:

   | Register Field | Description |
   |---|---|
   | Document ID | Unique identifier |
   | Document title | Name of document |
   | Artifact type | Policy, procedure, standard, record, plan, register, report, form, etc. |
   | Owner | Accountable owner |
   | Approver | Authorised approver |
   | Version | Current approved version |
   | Status | Draft, approved, effective, superseded, archived, withdrawn |
   | Effective date | Date document became effective |
   | Review frequency | Required review cycle |
   | Next review date | Scheduled review date |
   | Classification | Information classification |
   | Retention period | Required retention duration |
   | Repository location | Link or location |
   | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 reference | Clause, Annex A control, or ISMS process |
   | Last review date | Date of most recent review |
   | External distribution | Yes or no, and recipient group if applicable |

   11.3. The register must be updated when a controlled document is created, approved, revised, superseded, withdrawn, archived, restored, or disposed of.

12. **Perform periodic review**

   12.1. Each controlled ISMS document must be reviewed at the defined frequency or sooner when a triggering event occurs.

   12.2. Unless a stricter requirement applies, the following minimum review frequencies apply:

   | Document Category | Minimum Review Frequency |
   |---|---|
   | ISMS scope | Annually or upon material organisational change |
   | Information security policy | Annually |
   | Risk assessment methodology | Annually or upon material risk process change |
   | Risk assessment records | At planned risk assessment intervals or upon significant change |
   | Risk treatment plan | At least annually and after risk assessment updates |
   | Statement of Applicability | At least annually and after significant risk or control changes |
   | Procedures and standards | Annually |
   | Work instructions | Annually or upon process change |
   | Internal audit records | Per audit programme and retention schedule |
   | Management review records | Per management review schedule and retention schedule |
   | Training and awareness records | Per retention schedule |
   | Supplier security records | Per supplier review schedule and retention schedule |

   12.3. Triggering events requiring out-of-cycle review include:

   - Change to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 requirements or certification scope.
   - Significant security incident.
   - Material change to risk assessment or risk treatment.
   - Major organisational restructuring.
   - Introduction of new systems, services, suppliers, or technologies.
   - Change in legal, regulatory, or contractual obligations.
   - Internal or external audit finding.
   - Corrective action requiring document change.
   - Management review decision.
   - Obsolete, inaccurate, or conflicting content identified.

   12.4. The Document Owner records the outcome of the review as one of:

   - No change required.
   - Minor update required.
   - Major revision required.
   - Document to be withdrawn.
   - Document to be replaced by another controlled document.

   12.5. Review evidence must be retained even when no changes are made.

13. **Handle document changes**

   13.1. Changes to controlled ISMS documents must follow the review and approval steps in this procedure.

   13.2. The Document Owner must assess whether the change affects:

   - ISMS scope.
   - Information security objectives.
   - Risk assessment or risk treatment.
   - Statement of Applicability.
   - Policies or mandatory requirements.
   - Roles and responsibilities.
   - Legal, regulatory, or contractual obligations.
   - Control design or operation.
   - Training or awareness requirements.
   - Supplier or customer commitments.

   13.3. Material changes must be communicated to affected stakeholders before or on the effective date.

   13.4. Where changes require user acknowledgement or training, the Document Owner must define and track completion.

   13.5. Change records must be retained with the document or in the approved workflow system.

14. **Control externally originated documented information**

   14.1. The Document Owner identifies externally originated documented information necessary for the planning and operation of the ISMS.

   14.2. Examples include:

   - Laws, regulations, and regulatory guidance.
   - Contractual security requirements.
   - Customer security obligations.
   - Supplier security documentation.
   - Standards, codes of practice, or certification requirements.
   - External audit reports.
   - Penetration test reports from third parties.
   - Threat intelligence or advisory documents used in ISMS decisions.

   14.3. Externally originated documented information must be identified, classified, and controlled where necessary to ensure its suitability and availability.

   14.4. The Document Owner must ensure that externally originated documents are:

   - Stored in an approved location.
   - Identified as externally originated.
   - Linked to relevant ISMS processes or obligations.
   - Protected according to classification and contractual requirements.
   - Reviewed for currency where applicable.
   - Distributed only to authorised recipients.

15. **Retain records**

   15.1. ISMS records must be retained for the period defined in the retention schedule.

   15.2. Retention periods must consider:

   - ISO/IEC 27001:2022 evidence requirements.
   - Certification audit cycles.
   - Legal and regulatory obligations.
   - Contractual commitments.
   - Business requirements.
   - Litigation hold or investigation requirements.
   - Risk and assurance needs.

   15.3. Unless otherwise required by law, contract, or approved retention schedule, the following minimum retention periods apply:

   | Record Type | Minimum Retention Period |
   |---|---|
   | Current approved ISMS policies and procedures | Retain while current |
   | Superseded ISMS policies and procedures | 3 years after supersession |
   | ISMS scope versions | 3 years after supersession |
   | Risk assessment records | 3 years after supersession or completion |
   | Risk treatment plans | 3 years after supersession or completion |
   | Statement of Applicability versions | 3 years after supersession |
   | Internal audit reports and evidence | 3 years |
   | Management review records | 3 years |
   | Corrective action records | 3 years after closure |
   | Training and awareness records | 3 years or duration of employment plus 1 year, whichever is longer |
   | Access review records for ISMS repositories | 3 years |
   | Document approval records | Life of document plus 3 years |
   | Document change request records | 3 years after closure |
   | External distribution records | 3 years after distribution or withdrawal |

   15.4. Records subject to legal hold, investigation, audit dispute, regulatory inquiry, or active corrective action must not be destroyed until the hold is formally released.

16. **Archive superseded or withdrawn documents**

   16.1. When a document is superseded, withdrawn, or no longer required for current use, the ISMS Document Controller moves it to the controlled archive.

   16.2. Archived documents must be:

   - Clearly marked as superseded, withdrawn, or archived.
   - Removed from current-use locations.
   - Retained for the applicable retention period.
   - Protected from unauthorised access, alteration, or deletion.
   - Retrievable for audit, legal, regulatory, or business purposes.
   - Disposed of only after retention requirements are met.

   16.3. The document register must be updated to reflect archive status, archive date, and retention end date.

17. **Dispose of documents and records**

   17.1. At the end of the retention period, the ISMS Document Controller identifies documents and records eligible for disposal.

   17.2. Before disposal, the ISMS Document Controller must confirm with the Document Owner and Compliance Manager that:

   - Retention period has expired.
   - No legal hold applies.
   - No open audit, corrective action, investigation, dispute, or regulatory matter requires continued retention.
   - Disposal is permitted by law, contract, and organisational retention requirements.

   17.3. Disposal must be performed securely according to the document format and classification.

   | Format | Disposal Method |
   |---|---|
   | Electronic records | Secure deletion or approved repository purge process |
   | Paper records | Cross-cut shredding or approved secure destruction service |
   | Removable media | Secure wiping, cryptographic erase, or physical destruction |
   | Cloud repository records | Approved deletion process with audit trail where available |
   | Backups | Expire through approved backup retention cycle unless specific purge is required and feasible |

   17.4. Disposal evidence must be retained and must include:

   - Description of disposed records.
   - Date of disposal.
   - Disposal method.
   - Person or service performing disposal.
   - Approval for disposal.
   - Confirmation of legal hold check.

18. **Monitor compliance with this procedure**

   18.1. The Information Security Manager monitors compliance with this procedure through periodic checks, internal audits, management review inputs, and document register review.

   18.2. Compliance checks may include:

   - Sampling documents for approval evidence.
   - Verifying document metadata completeness.
   - Confirming current versions are available at points of use.
   - Confirming obsolete versions are removed from normal use.
   - Checking review dates are current.
   - Reviewing access permissions.
   - Verifying retention and archival controls.
   - Confirming external distribution records.
   - Checking document register accuracy.

   18.3. Nonconformities must be recorded and managed through the corrective action process.

## Roles & RACI

| Activity | Document Owner | ISMS Document Controller | Information Security Manager | Approver | Reviewer | Repository Administrator | Compliance Manager | Internal Audit |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Identify need for document creation or change | R | C | C | I | C | I | C | C |
| Determine whether document is controlled | C | R | A | I | I | C | C | I |
| Assign metadata and document ID | C | R | A | I | I | C | C | I |
| Draft or revise document | R | C | C | I | C | I | C | I |
| Review document content | C | C | A | I | R | I | C | C |
| Resolve review comments | R | C | A | I | C | I | C | I |
| Approve document | I | C | C | A/R | I | I | C | I |
| Publish approved document | I | R | A | I | I | C | I | I |
| Configure repository access | I | C | A | I | I | R | C | I |
| Maintain document register | C | R | A | I | I | C | C | I |
| Communicate changes | R | C | A | C | I | I | C | I |
| Archive superseded documents | C | R | A | I | I | C | C | I |
| Apply retention schedule | C | R | A | I | I | C | R | I |
| Approve disposal | C | R | A | I | I | I | R | I |
| Verify procedure compliance | I | C | A | I | I | I | C | R |
| Manage nonconformities | R | C | A | I | C | I | C | C |

RACI legend:

- **R** = Responsible for performing the activity.
- **A** = Accountable for ensuring the activity is completed and approved.
- **C** = Consulted for input.
- **I** = Informed of outcome.

Role responsibilities:

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Document Owner | Maintains the accuracy, relevance, completeness, classification, review, and lifecycle of assigned documented information. |
| ISMS Document Controller | Administers document control processes, document register, metadata, versioning, publication, archival, and controlled distribution. |
| Information Security Manager | Owns the ISMS document control process, ensures alignment with ISO/IEC 27001:2022, resolves escalations, and reports status to management. |
| Approver | Reviews and formally approves controlled documents for suitability and adequacy before issue. |
| Reviewer | Provides subject matter review to confirm accuracy, feasibility, compliance, and consistency. |
| Repository Administrator | Manages technical access, repository configuration, backup coordination, permission groups, and audit logging where applicable. |
| Compliance Manager | Advises on retention, legal, regulatory, contractual, and audit evidence requirements. |
| Internal Audit | Independently evaluates whether documented information controls are designed and operating effectively. |
| Users | Use only current approved documents from controlled repositories and report suspected obsolete, inaccurate, or inaccessible documentation. |

## Records & Outputs

The following records and outputs are produced or maintained as a result of this procedure:

| Record or Output | Description | Owner | Retention |
|---|---|---|---|
| Controlled ISMS document register | Master list of controlled ISMS documented information and metadata. | ISMS Document Controller | Current plus 3 years |
| Document change request | Request and justification for creation, revision, withdrawal, archive, or disposal. | ISMS Document Controller | 3 years after closure |
| Draft document | Working version under development or review. | Document Owner | Until approved or cancelled |
| Approved controlled document | Current authorised version available for use. | Document Owner | While current |
| Change history | Record of document changes, version updates, and rationale. | ISMS Document Controller | Life of document plus 3 years |
| Review comments and resolution record | Evidence of review and issue resolution. | Document Owner | Life of document plus 3 years |
| Approval evidence | Workflow approval, signature, meeting record, or approved email. | ISMS Document Controller | Life of document plus 3 years |
| Distribution record | Evidence of internal or external communication of approved document. | Document Owner | 3 years |
| Acknowledgement or training record | Evidence that affected users acknowledged or were trained on document changes. | Document Owner | 3 years or per training retention rules |
| Archived document | Superseded, withdrawn, or obsolete controlled document retained for evidence. | ISMS Document Controller | Per retention schedule |
| Disposal approval record | Approval and confirmation that document or record may be securely disposed. | Compliance Manager | 3 years after disposal |
| Disposal evidence | Evidence of secure destruction or deletion. | ISMS Document Controller | 3 years after disposal |
| Access review record | Evidence that access to document repositories was reviewed. | Repository Administrator | 3 years |
| Nonconformity or corrective action record | Record of failure to comply with this procedure and corrective action taken. | Information Security Manager | 3 years after closure |

Document control status definitions:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Draft | Document is being created or revised and is not approved for use. |
| In review | Document has been submitted for stakeholder review. |
| Approved | Document has been approved but may not yet be effective. |
| Effective | Document is approved and currently applicable. |
| Superseded | Document has been replaced by a newer approved version. |
| Withdrawn | Document is no longer required and has been formally withdrawn from use. |
| Archived | Document is retained for evidence or reference but not for current use. |
| Disposed | Document has been destroyed or deleted in accordance with retention requirements. |

## Exceptions & Escalation

Exceptions to this procedure are permitted only where formally justified, risk assessed, approved, and recorded.

Examples of exceptions include:

- Emergency publication of a document before completion of the standard review cycle.
- Temporary use of an alternative repository due to service outage.
- Retention beyond the standard period due to legal hold or regulatory requirement.
- Restricted distribution of normally available ISMS documentation due to confidentiality concerns.
- Use of email approval where workflow approval is unavailable.
- Delayed periodic review due to dependency on an active investigation, audit, or regulatory change.

Exception requests must include:

| Field | Required Information |
|---|---|
| Exception requester | Name and role of requester |
| Document affected | Document ID, title, and version |
| Procedure requirement affected | Specific requirement for which exception is requested |
| Justification | Business or compliance reason |
| Risk assessment | Confidentiality, integrity, availability, legal, regulatory, audit, and operational impacts |
| Compensating controls | Measures to reduce risk during exception period |
| Duration | Start date and end date |
| Approver | Information Security Manager or higher authority where required |
| Review date | Date exception will be reviewed |
| Closure evidence | Evidence that exception ended or was converted to approved practice |

Escalation requirements:

| Scenario | Escalation Path | Required Action |
|---|---|---|
| Material disagreement on document content | Document Owner → Information Security Manager | Resolve or refer to ISMS governance body |
| Approval delay affecting ISMS compliance | ISMS Document Controller → Information Security Manager → Approver | Prioritise approval or define interim control |
| Suspected use of obsolete document | User or Document Owner → ISMS Document Controller | Remove obsolete document and notify affected users |
| Unauthorised change to controlled document | ISMS Document Controller → Information Security Manager → Incident Management process if applicable | Preserve evidence, restore approved version, investigate |
| Loss or corruption of controlled documentation | Repository Administrator → Information Security Manager | Restore from backup and assess impact |
| Unauthorised disclosure of restricted documented information | Any person → Information Security Manager | Assess as potential information security incident |
| Retention or disposal conflict | ISMS Document Controller → Compliance Manager → Legal, if required | Suspend disposal until resolved |
| Repeated noncompliance with this procedure | Information Security Manager → ISMS governance body or executive management | Initiate corrective action |

Emergency changes:

- Emergency document changes may be approved through an accelerated process when delay would create unacceptable information security, legal, regulatory, operational, or audit risk.
- Emergency approval must be obtained from the Information Security Manager or delegated authority.
- The emergency change must be retrospectively reviewed and fully documented within 10 business days.
- If the emergency change is not confirmed through normal approval, it must be withdrawn or replaced by an approved version.

## Review

This procedure must be reviewed at least annually and whenever one or more of the following occurs:

- Changes to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 or certification requirements affecting documented information.
- Material change to the ISMS scope.
