- Change to the controlled document repository or approval workflow.
- Significant audit finding related to document control.
- Significant information security incident involving documentation integrity, availability, or confidentiality.
- Change to legal, regulatory, contractual, or retention requirements.
- Management review decision requiring update.
- Repeated exceptions or nonconformities related to document control.

The Information Security Manager is accountable for ensuring this procedure remains suitable, adequate, and effective. The ISMS Document Controller is responsible for coordinating the review and maintaining review evidence.

Review activities must include:

- Confirming alignment with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Clause 7.5.
- Confirming that document control responsibilities remain accurate.
- Assessing whether document metadata, approval, versioning, retention, and distribution requirements remain effective.
- Reviewing exceptions, nonconformities, and audit results.
- Confirming the document register is complete and current.
- Confirming retention periods remain appropriate.
- Identifying improvement opportunities.

Review outcomes must be recorded as one of:

- Approved with no changes.
- Approved with minor changes.
- Major revision required.
- Procedure withdrawn or replaced.

The review record must include the reviewer, review date, outcome, summary of changes or rationale for no change, and approval evidence.

ISO27-028.title: Records Control Procedure
ISO27-028.content:
| Metadata | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | [ISMS-PROC-REC-001] |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | ISMS Manager |
| Effective Date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Framework | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 |
| Control Reference | Clause 7.5.3 — Control of documented information |
| Classification | Internal |

## Purpose

This procedure defines how the organisation controls records that demonstrate conformity of the Information Security Management System (ISMS) with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and with the organisation’s own ISMS requirements.

For the purpose of this procedure, “records” are a form of documented information retained as evidence that ISMS activities have been performed, decisions have been made, controls have operated, and requirements have been met.

This procedure supports ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Clause 7.5.3 by ensuring ISMS records are:

- Available and suitable for use where and when needed.
- Adequately protected from loss of confidentiality, improper use, compromise of integrity, or loss of availability.
- Controlled for distribution, access, retrieval, use, storage, preservation, change control, retention, and disposition.
- Retained in a manner that provides reliable evidence of ISMS conformity and operational effectiveness.

## Scope

This procedure applies to all ISMS records created, received, maintained, archived, or disposed of by the organisation in support of ISO/IEC 27001:2022.

This includes records in any format, including electronic documents, tickets, logs, reports, approvals, registers, meeting minutes, emails, system exports, screenshots, signed forms, audit evidence, and records held in approved business systems.

The procedure applies to:

- ISMS governance records.
- Risk management records.
- Internal audit and management review records.
- Corrective action records.
- Security control operation records.
- Security incident records.
- Competence, awareness, and training records.
- Supplier and third-party security records.
- Legal, regulatory, contractual, and compliance records relevant to the ISMS.
- Records required by the Statement of Applicability and associated control procedures.
- Records required to demonstrate fulfilment of information security objectives.

This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, temporary workers, service providers, and other personnel who create, access, maintain, approve, store, retrieve, transfer, archive, or dispose of ISMS records.

This procedure does not define the content of individual policies, procedures, standards, or plans; it defines how records evidencing ISMS conformity are controlled.

## Prerequisites & Inputs

Before applying this procedure, the following must be established and available:

| Prerequisite / Input | Description | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| ISMS scope statement | Defines the organisational, technical, and physical boundaries of the ISMS. | ISMS Manager |
| Documented Information Control Procedure | Defines how ISMS documents and records are generally controlled. | ISMS Manager |
| Information Classification Policy | Defines classification levels and handling requirements for information assets and records. | Information Security Manager |
| Access Control Policy | Defines rules for granting, reviewing, and revoking access to repositories containing ISMS records. | IT / Information Security |
| Records Retention Schedule | Defines minimum retention periods and disposal requirements for ISMS records. | ISMS Manager / Legal |
| Approved ISMS repository | Authorised location or system used to store and retrieve controlled ISMS records. | ISMS Manager |
| Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements | Requirements affecting retention, protection, availability, or disposal of ISMS records. | Legal / Compliance |
| ISMS roles and responsibilities | Defined accountability for record creation, approval, maintenance, review, and disposal. | Top Management / ISMS Manager |
| Audit programme | Internal and external audit schedule and evidence requirements. | Internal Audit |
| Risk assessment and treatment methodology | Defines how risk records are generated and maintained. | Risk Owner / ISMS Manager |

Approved repositories may include the following, subject to access control and retention requirements:

| Repository Type | Examples | Permitted Use |
|---|---|---|
| ISMS governance repository | [Document management system], [GRC platform] | Policies, procedures, registers, approvals, meeting records |
| Ticketing/workflow system | [Service management system], [issue tracker] | Corrective actions, incidents, service requests, change evidence |
| Security tooling platforms | SIEM, vulnerability scanner, EDR, IAM system | Control operation records, alerts, monitoring outputs |
| HR or learning platform | [HRIS], [LMS] | competence, training, and awareness evidence |
| Supplier management platform | [Vendor management system] | supplier due diligence, reviews, contractual evidence |
| Internal audit repository | [Audit management system] | audit plans, checklists, findings, evidence, reports |

Records must not be maintained solely in uncontrolled personal storage locations, local drives, personal email inboxes, removable media, or unapproved collaboration spaces.

## Step-by-Step Procedure (numbered)

1. **Identify ISMS record requirements**

   1.1. The ISMS Manager shall identify the records required to demonstrate conformity with ISO/IEC 27001:2022, the organisation’s ISMS requirements, and applicable legal, regulatory, and contractual obligations.

   1.2. Record requirements shall be identified from, at minimum:

   - ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clauses requiring documented information as evidence.
   - The organisation’s Statement of Applicability.
   - Risk assessment and risk treatment processes.
   - Internal audit programme.
   - Management review requirements.
   - Corrective action process.
   - Information security objectives and performance monitoring.
   - Security operational procedures.
   - Supplier security requirements.
   - Incident management requirements.
   - Applicable legislation, regulation, contractual clauses, and customer commitments.

   1.3. Required ISMS records shall be listed in the ISMS Records Register or equivalent controlled inventory.

2. **Define record attributes in the ISMS Records Register**

   2.1. For each record type, the ISMS Manager or assigned Record Owner shall define the control attributes needed to manage the record throughout its lifecycle.

   2.2. At minimum, the following attributes shall be recorded:

   | Attribute | Required Content |
   |---|---|
   | Record name/type | Name of the record or evidence type |
   | Purpose | Why the record is required and what conformity it demonstrates |
   | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 reference | Clause, control, or ISMS requirement supported |
   | Record owner | Role accountable for completeness and accuracy |
   | Creator/source | Role, process, or system generating the record |
   | Approved repository | Authorised storage location |
   | Classification | Information classification level |
   | Access restrictions | Roles or groups authorised to access the record |
   | Format | Native system record, PDF, spreadsheet, report, ticket, log, signed form, etc. |
   | Frequency | Creation or update frequency |
   | Retention period | Minimum retention requirement |
   | Preservation requirements | Encryption, backup, immutability, export, legal hold, or integrity requirements |
   | Disposal method | Secure deletion, anonymisation, destruction, or archival transfer |
   | Review requirement | Whether periodic review is required and by whom |

   2.3. The ISMS Records Register shall be maintained as controlled documented information.

3. **Create records at the point of activity**

   3.1. Personnel responsible for ISMS activities shall create records at the time the activity is performed or as soon as reasonably practicable thereafter.

   3.2. Records shall be complete, accurate, legible, attributable, and retained in a manner that preserves their evidential value.

   3.3. Each record shall include sufficient contextual information to demonstrate what occurred, when it occurred, who performed or approved it, and what decision or outcome resulted.

   3.4. Where applicable, records shall include:

   - Date and time of activity.
   - Name, role, or unique identifier of the person or system creating the record.
   - Version, ticket number, meeting reference, system event ID, or other unique identifier.
   - Approval status and approver identity.
   - Links to related risk records, control records, audit records, incident records, or corrective actions.
   - Evidence of completion, review, or verification.

   3.5. Records shall not be backdated, falsified, altered to conceal facts, or deleted outside approved disposal processes.

4. **Classify records**

   4.1. The Record Owner shall ensure each record type is assigned an information classification in accordance with the Information Classification Policy.

   4.2. Classification shall reflect the sensitivity of the record, including whether it contains:

   - Security vulnerabilities or control weaknesses.
   - Security incident details.
   - Personal data.
   - Authentication or access control information.
   - Supplier or contractual information.
   - Audit findings.
   - Risk ratings or risk treatment decisions.
   - Confidential business or technical information.

   4.3. Records with higher classifications shall be protected using additional controls such as restricted access, encryption, secure transfer, redaction, and need-to-know handling.

5. **Store records only in approved repositories**

   5.1. ISMS records shall be stored in the approved repository defined in the ISMS Records Register.

   5.2. Where records are generated in operational systems, the original system record may serve as the authoritative record if the system provides appropriate access control, retention, backup, and retrieval capability.

   5.3. Where an operational system does not meet retention or retrieval requirements, the Record Owner shall export or copy the record to an approved ISMS repository in a controlled format.

   5.4. Records shall not be stored exclusively in:

   - Personal drives.
   - Local workstation folders.
   - Personal email accounts or inboxes.
   - Unapproved cloud storage.
   - Consumer messaging platforms.
   - Removable media unless explicitly authorised and encrypted.

6. **Apply naming, indexing, and retrieval controls**

   6.1. Records shall be named, indexed, tagged, or otherwise organised so they can be located and retrieved within a reasonable timeframe for operational use, audits, management review, incident response, or legal inquiry.

   6.2. Where records are file-based, naming conventions should include, where practical:

   - Record type.
   - Business area or system.
   - Relevant period or date.
   - Unique reference number.
   - Version or status, if applicable.

   Example format:

   | Record Type | Example Naming Convention |
   |---|---|
   | Internal audit report | `Internal-Audit-Report_[Scope]_[YYYY-MM-DD]_v[1.0]` |
   | Risk assessment | `Risk-Assessment_[Asset/Process]_[YYYY-MM-DD]_v[1.0]` |
   | Management review minutes | `Management-Review-Minutes_[YYYY-Q#]_[YYYY-MM-DD]` |
   | Corrective action evidence | `CA-[ID]_Evidence_[YYYY-MM-DD]` |
   | Access review record | `Access-Review_[System]_[YYYY-MM]` |

   6.3. Records stored in systems of record shall use system-generated identifiers where available, such as ticket IDs, audit IDs, incident IDs, change IDs, or risk IDs.

7. **Control access to records**

   7.1. Access to ISMS records shall be granted based on business need, least privilege, segregation of duties, and classification requirements.

   7.2. The Record Owner shall approve access to restricted record repositories or record types unless approval is managed through a formally authorised role-based access model.

   7.3. Access permissions shall be reviewed periodically in accordance with the Access Control Policy and at minimum when:

   - Personnel change roles.
   - Personnel leave the organisation.
   - Supplier access changes or ends.
   - Repository ownership changes.
   - A security incident affects records or repositories.
   - An audit identifies excessive or inappropriate access.

   7.4. Access to records containing highly sensitive information, such as security incidents, vulnerabilities, legal matters, or audit findings, shall be limited to authorised personnel with a demonstrable need to know.

8. **Protect records from unauthorised alteration and loss**

   8.1. Records shall be protected against unauthorised modification, deletion, corruption, loss, or unavailability.

   8.2. Protection mechanisms shall be applied based on classification, evidential value, and risk, and may include:

   - Role-based access control.
   - Multi-factor authentication for repository access.
   - Encryption at rest and in transit.
   - Backup and recovery.
   - Version history.
   - Audit logging.
   - Write-once or immutable storage where required.
   - Digital signatures or approval workflows.
   - Integrity checks.
   - Legal hold controls.
   - Change logs for amended records.

   8.3. If a record must be corrected, the correction shall preserve the original record or maintain an auditable history of the change, including who made the change, when it was made, and why it was made.

   8.4. Records shall not be overwritten where doing so would compromise evidence of conformity, traceability, or decision-making.

9. **Maintain records for the defined retention period**

   9.1. Each ISMS record type shall be retained for the period specified in the Records Retention Schedule or ISMS Records Register.

   9.2. Retention periods shall be based on:

   - ISO/IEC 27001:2022 conformity evidence needs.
   - Certification audit cycle requirements.
   - Legal and regulatory obligations.
   - Contractual and customer requirements.
   - Operational and business needs.
   - Risk and evidential value.
   - Limitation periods for disputes, claims, or investigations.

   9.3. Unless a longer legal, regulatory, contractual, or business requirement applies, core ISMS conformity records should be retained for at least one full certification cycle plus the current cycle year.

   9.4. Example minimum retention periods are provided below and shall be adjusted where required by law, contract, or organisational retention rules:

   | Record Category | Example Records | Minimum Retention |
   |---|---|---|
   | ISMS scope and governance | ISMS scope, policies, ISMS objectives, governance approvals | Current version plus 3 years |
   | Risk management | Risk assessments, risk treatment plans, risk acceptance approvals | Current version plus 3 years |
   | Statement of Applicability | Approved SoA versions and approval records | Current version plus 3 years |
   | Internal audits | Audit programme, plans, evidence, findings, reports | 3 years |
   | Management reviews | Agendas, minutes, inputs, outputs, actions | 3 years |
   | Corrective actions | Nonconformities, root cause analysis, action evidence, effectiveness reviews | 3 years after closure |
   | Security incidents | Incident records, investigation evidence, lessons learned | 3 years or legal requirement |
   | Competence and awareness | Training attendance, competence assessments, role-specific training evidence | Duration of employment plus [X] years |
   | Access reviews | User access review outputs and remediation evidence | 3 years |
   | Supplier security | Due diligence, assessments, reviews, contract security evidence | Contract term plus [X] years |
   | Monitoring and measurement | KPI/KRI results, control monitoring reports, metrics | 3 years |
   | Vulnerability and remediation | Scan results, remediation tickets, acceptance records | 3 years |
   | Business continuity / backup testing | Test records, results, improvement actions | 3 years |

10. **Retrieve records for audits, reviews, and operational needs**

   10.1. The ISMS Manager shall coordinate retrieval of ISMS records required for internal audits, certification audits, management reviews, regulatory requests, customer audits, or investigations.

   10.2. Record Owners shall provide requested records within agreed timelines and ensure that records are complete and appropriate for the purpose requested.

   10.3. Records provided to auditors or external parties shall be reviewed for classification and confidentiality before release.

   10.4. Where records contain sensitive information not required for the request, the Record Owner shall redact or provide controlled extracts, provided the evidence remains sufficient and accurate.

   10.5. External sharing of records shall follow approved information transfer, confidentiality, and contractual requirements.

11. **Review records for completeness and ongoing suitability**

   11.1. Record Owners shall periodically review assigned record sets to confirm that:

   - Required records exist.
   - Records are stored in approved repositories.
   - Records are complete and retrievable.
   - Access permissions remain appropriate.
   - Retention periods are correctly applied.
   - Records subject to legal hold are preserved.
   - Disposition actions are performed when due.

   11.2. The ISMS Manager shall perform, at minimum annually, a review of the ISMS Records Register and sample record sets to confirm continued alignment with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Clause 7.5.3.

   11.3. Issues identified during record reviews shall be recorded and tracked to closure as corrective actions or improvement actions, as appropriate.

12. **Place records on legal, regulatory, audit, or investigation hold where required**

   12.1. Records shall not be deleted, destroyed, anonymised, or altered when they are subject to legal hold, regulatory inquiry, audit request, investigation, dispute, litigation, or security incident preservation requirement.

   12.2. Legal, Compliance, Internal Audit, or the ISMS Manager may initiate a record hold.

   12.3. The Record Owner shall ensure affected repositories and personnel are notified of the hold and that automated deletion or disposition is suspended for affected records.

   12.4. Record holds shall be documented, including:

   | Hold Attribute | Description |
   |---|---|
   | Hold reference | Unique identifier for the hold |
   | Initiating authority | Legal, Compliance, Internal Audit, ISMS Manager, or other authorised role |
   | Reason for hold | Investigation, litigation, audit, regulatory request, incident, or other reason |
   | Records affected | Record types, systems, date ranges, custodians |
   | Start date | Date the hold became effective |
   | Restrictions | Required preservation actions and prohibited actions |
   | Review date | Date hold status must be reviewed |
   | Release approval | Authority required to release the hold |

13. **Dispose of records securely when retention expires**

   13.1. Records shall be disposed of only after the approved retention period has expired and no legal hold, audit hold, investigation hold, contractual requirement, or business need requires further retention.

   13.2. Disposal shall be authorised by the Record Owner and, where required, Legal, Compliance, or the ISMS Manager.

   13.3. Disposal methods shall be appropriate to the record format and classification, including:

   | Record Format | Approved Disposal Method |
   |---|---|
   | Electronic file | Secure deletion, repository retention rule, cryptographic erasure, or approved sanitisation |
   | System record | Approved purge, deletion workflow, anonymisation, or archival deletion function |
   | Backup record | Expiry through approved backup lifecycle management, unless legal hold applies |
   | Paper record | Cross-cut shredding or certified secure destruction |
   | Removable media | Secure wiping, degaussing, physical destruction, or certified disposal |
   | Cloud-hosted record | Provider-supported secure deletion in accordance with contractual and security requirements |

   13.4. Disposal of records classified as confidential or higher shall be evidenced by a destruction log, system audit log, workflow approval, or certificate of destruction.

   13.5. Disposal evidence shall itself be retained in accordance with the Records Retention Schedule.

14. **Manage obsolete, superseded, or replaced records**

   14.1. Superseded ISMS records with evidential value shall be retained in accordance with the retention schedule.

   14.2. Obsolete records shall be clearly identified or segregated to prevent unintended use as current evidence.

   14.3. Where versioned records are maintained, prior approved versions shall be preserved where needed to demonstrate historical conformity, decisions, approvals, or control operation.

   14.4. Draft or working records that are not required as evidence may be deleted when no longer needed, unless they are subject to legal hold, audit requirement, or investigation preservation.

15. **Monitor compliance with this procedure**

   15.1. The ISMS Manager shall monitor conformance with this procedure through periodic sampling, internal audits, management review inputs, corrective action tracking, and repository access reviews.

   15.2. Nonconformities may include:

   - Missing required ISMS records.
   - Records stored in unapproved locations.
   - Inadequate access controls.
   - Failure to retain records for the required period.
   - Unauthorised deletion or alteration.
   - Inability to retrieve audit evidence.
   - Records lacking attribution, approval, or completeness.
   - Retention periods inconsistent with legal or contractual requirements.

   15.3. Identified nonconformities shall be managed in accordance with the Corrective Action Procedure.

## Roles & RACI

| Activity | Top Management | ISMS Manager | Record Owner | Record Creator / Process Owner | IT / Repository Administrator | Legal / Compliance | Internal Audit |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Approve overall approach to ISMS records control | A | R | C | C | C | C | C |
| Maintain ISMS Records Register | I | A/R | R | C | C | C | C |
| Define record retention requirements | I | A/R | R | C | C | C/R | C |
| Create ISMS records | I | C | A | R | C | C | C |
| Ensure record completeness and accuracy | I | C | A/R | R | C | C | C |
| Classify records | I | C | A/R | C | C | C | C |
| Assign approved repository | I | A/R | R | C | C/R | C | C |
| Configure repository access and retention controls | I | C | A | C | R | C | I |
| Approve access to restricted records | I | C | A/R | C | C | C | I |
| Retrieve records for audits and reviews | I | A/R | R | C | C | C | R |
| Initiate legal, audit, or investigation hold | I | R | C | C | C | A/R | A/R |
| Authorise record disposal | I | A/R | A/R | C | R | C/R | I |
| Verify compliance with this procedure | I | A/R | C | C | C | C | R |
| Report significant record control failures | A | R | C | C | C | C | C |

RACI legend:

| Letter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| R | Responsible for performing the activity |
| A | Accountable for the outcome and approval |
| C | Consulted before or during the activity |
| I | Informed of the activity or outcome |

## Records & Outputs

The following records are generated or maintained as outputs of this procedure:

| Record / Output | Description | Owner | Repository | Minimum Retention |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISMS Records Register | Inventory of ISMS record types and associated control attributes | ISMS Manager | [GRC platform / ISMS repository] | Current version plus 3 years |
| Records Retention Schedule | Defined retention periods and disposal requirements | ISMS Manager / Legal | [Document management system] | Current version plus 3 years |
| Access approval records | Evidence of approval for access to restricted ISMS records | Record Owner | [IAM system / ticketing system] | 3 years |
| Repository access review evidence | Periodic review of access to ISMS repositories | IT / ISMS Manager | [IAM system / ISMS repository] | 3 years |
| Record review evidence | Evidence of periodic review of record completeness, access, and retention | ISMS Manager | [GRC platform] | 3 years |
| Record hold notices | Legal, audit, investigation, or regulatory hold instructions | Legal / Compliance / ISMS Manager | [Legal hold system / ISMS repository] | Duration of hold plus 3 years |
| Disposal approvals | Authorisation to delete, destroy, anonymise, or archive records | Record Owner | [Ticketing system / GRC platform] | 3 years |
| Destruction logs / certificates | Evidence that records were securely disposed of | Record Owner / IT | [ISMS repository] | 3 years |
| Corrective actions for record control failures | Nonconformities and remediation evidence | ISMS Manager | [GRC platform / ticketing system] | 3 years after closure |
| Audit evidence packages | Controlled evidence provided for audits or assessments | ISMS Manager | [Audit repository] | 3 years |

Minimum required metadata for retained ISMS records, where applicable:

| Metadata Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Record title or identifier | Required |
| Owner | Required |
| Creation date | Required |
| Related ISMS process or control | Required |
| Classification | Required |
| Retention category | Required |
| Approval or status | Required where approval is part of the process |
| Repository location | Required |
| Access restriction | Required for restricted or sensitive records |
| Disposal eligibility date | Required where supported by the repository |

## Exceptions & Escalation

Exceptions to this procedure are permitted only where justified, risk-assessed, time-bound, and approved.

Examples of exceptions include:

- A record must be retained in a non-standard repository due to technical constraints.
- A retention period must be extended due to contractual, legal, regulatory, or customer requirements.
- A record cannot be retrieved within the expected timeframe due to system outage or repository failure.
- An operational system cannot support required audit logging, retention, or export functionality.
- A disposal activity cannot be performed due to legal hold or unresolved investigation.
- A record must be shared externally using a non-standard transfer method.

Exception requests shall include:

| Field | Required Information |
|---|---|
| Exception reference | Unique identifier |
| Requestor | Person or role requesting the exception |
| Record type affected | Record category, system, or repository |
| Requirement affected | Procedure step, retention rule, access rule, or repository requirement |
| Business justification | Reason the exception is needed |
| Risk assessment | Confidentiality, integrity, availability, compliance, and auditability impact |
| Compensating controls | Measures to reduce risk |
| Duration | Start date and expiry date |
| Approval required | ISMS Manager and, where applicable, Legal / Compliance / Information Security |
| Review date | Date for reassessment |
| Closure criteria | Conditions required to return to normal control |

Escalation requirements:

| Scenario | Escalation Path | Required Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Required ISMS record is missing or incomplete | Record Owner to ISMS Manager | Within 2 business days of discovery |
| Record repository is unavailable during audit or regulatory request | IT to ISMS Manager and affected Record Owner | Immediately |
| Unauthorised access, alteration, or deletion is suspected | Information Security Incident Response process | Immediately |
| Retention requirement conflicts with legal or contractual obligation | ISMS Manager to Legal / Compliance | Before action is taken |
| Disposal occurred in error | Record Owner to ISMS Manager, Legal / Compliance, and Information Security | Immediately |
| External auditor or regulator disputes sufficiency of evidence | ISMS Manager to Top Management and relevant Record Owner | Within 1 business day |
| Repeated nonconformance with records control requirements | ISMS Manager to Top Management | At management review or sooner if material |

Any suspected compromise, unauthorised disclosure, unauthorised alteration, or unauthorised destruction of ISMS records shall be handled as a security event or incident in accordance with the Information Security Incident Management Procedure.

## Review

This procedure shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur that may affect ISMS records control.

Triggers for review include:

- Changes to ISO/IEC 27001 or related certification requirements.
- Changes to legal, regulatory, contractual, or customer recordkeeping requirements.
- Changes to the ISMS scope.
- Significant changes to repositories, GRC platforms, ticketing systems, identity systems, or security monitoring platforms.
- Internal or external audit findings related to documented information.
- Security incidents involving loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure, or unavailability of records.
- Changes to retention requirements.
- Repeated exceptions or nonconformities related to record control.
- Changes to organisational structure, roles, responsibilities, or outsourcing arrangements.

The ISMS Manager is responsible for coordinating the review. Legal, Compliance, Information Security, IT, Internal Audit, and relevant Record Owners shall be consulted where their areas are affected.

Review outputs shall include, where applicable:

- Updated procedure version.
- Updated ISMS Records Register.
- Updated Records Retention Schedule.
- Changes to repository controls or access models.
- Corrective actions or improvement actions.
- Communication to affected personnel.
- Updated training or awareness materials.

Review and approval history shall be maintained as controlled documented information.

| Version | Date | Reviewer / Approver | Summary of Changes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | [YYYY-MM-DD] | ISMS Manager | Initial version |

ISO27-029.title: Competence & Training Records
ISO27-029.content:
## Competence & Training Records (XLSX template)

_Editable template — add your own rows. The example row(s) below are placeholders to replace._

| Record ID | Training Title | Training Type | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Reference | Competence Requirement / Learning Objective | Audience / Role Required | Mandatory Training | Training Provider | Delivery Method | Training Date | Training Duration Hours | Attendee Name | Attendee Unique ID | Job Title / Role | Department / Team | Employment Type | Manager / Approver | Attendance Status | Completion Date | Assessment Required | Assessment Method | Score / Result | Pass Mark | Pass / Fail Status | Competence Achieved | Retraining Required | Retraining Due Date | Certificate / Evidence Reference | Record Location / Link | Trainer / Assessor Name | Trainer / Assessor Competence Evidence | Notes / Exceptions | Record Created Date | Record Last Updated Date | Record Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [EXAMPLE: CTR-2025-0001] | [EXAMPLE: Annual Information Security Awareness Training] | [EXAMPLE: Information Security Awareness] | [EXAMPLE: Cl. 7.2; A.6.3] | [EXAMPLE: Understand security responsibilities, phishing reporting, acceptable use, and incident reporting obligations] | [EXAMPLE: All Employees] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: Internal Security Team] | [EXAMPLE: E-Learning] | [EXAMPLE: 2025-02-01] | [EXAMPLE: 1] | [EXAMPLE: Jane Smith] | [EXAMPLE: EMP-00482] | [EXAMPLE: Finance Analyst] | [EXAMPLE: Finance] | [EXAMPLE: Employee] | [EXAMPLE: Alex Brown] | [EXAMPLE: Completed Online] | [EXAMPLE: 2025-02-03] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: Quiz] | [EXAMPLE: 92%] | [EXAMPLE: 80%] | [EXAMPLE: Pass] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: No] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: LMS-COMP-77821] | [EXAMPLE: https://lms.example.com/completions/77821] | [EXAMPLE: Security Awareness LMS Module] | [EXAMPLE: Approved LMS course reviewed by ISMS Manager] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: 2025-02-03] | [EXAMPLE: 2025-02-03] | [EXAMPLE: Security Awareness Lead] |
| [EXAMPLE: CTR-2025-0002] | [EXAMPLE: Secure Coding for Web Developers] | [EXAMPLE: Secure Development] | [EXAMPLE: Cl. 7.2; A.6.3] | [EXAMPLE: Apply secure coding practices and identify common web application vulnerabilities] | [EXAMPLE: Developers] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: External Training Provider Ltd] | [EXAMPLE: Virtual Live] | [EXAMPLE: 2025-03-12] | [EXAMPLE: 4] | [EXAMPLE: Ravi Patel] | [EXAMPLE: EMP-00617] | [EXAMPLE: Software Developer] | [EXAMPLE: Product Engineering] | [EXAMPLE: Employee] | [EXAMPLE: Morgan Lee] | [EXAMPLE: Attended] | [EXAMPLE: 2025-03-12] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: Practical Exercise] | [EXAMPLE: Satisfactory] | [EXAMPLE: Satisfactory] | [EXAMPLE: Pass] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: No] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: CERT-SC-2025-143] | [EXAMPLE: https://sharepoint.example.com/training/secure-coding/CERT-SC-2025-143.pdf] | [EXAMPLE: Dana White] | [EXAMPLE: Trainer CV and secure coding certification on approved trainer register] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: 2025-03-12] | [EXAMPLE: 2025-03-13] | [EXAMPLE: HR Learning Manager] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Record ID | Enter a unique identifier for this training/attendance record, e.g. CTR-YYYY-0001. |
| Training Title | Enter the official name of the training course, briefing, awareness session, induction, or competence activity delivered. |
| Training Type | Enter the category of training using allowed values: Information Security Awareness, Role-Based Security Training, Secure Development, Incident Response, Privacy/Data Protection, Physical Security, Supplier Security, Induction, Refresher, Other. |
| ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Reference | Enter the relevant clause or control reference, typically Cl. 7.2 and/or A.6.3; include any other applicable internal ISMS control reference if relevant. |
| Competence Requirement / Learning Objective | State the specific competence, awareness outcome, or skill the attendee is expected to gain, linked to their role or information security responsibilities. |
| Audience / Role Required | Enter the target audience or role group required to complete the training, e.g. All Employees, Developers, Service Desk, Privileged Users, ISMS Internal Auditors, Senior Management. |
| Mandatory Training | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether the training is mandatory for the attendee’s role. |
| Training Provider | Enter the internal team, individual, external supplier, or learning platform that provided the training. |
| Delivery Method | Enter one allowed value: Classroom, Virtual Live, E-Learning, Toolbox Talk, Workshop, On-the-Job Training, Simulation/Exercise, Other. |
| Training Date | Enter the date the training was delivered or assigned in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Training Duration Hours | Enter the duration of the training in hours as a number, e.g. 1, 1.5, 2. |
| Attendee Name | Enter the full name of the person who attended or was assigned the training. |
| Attendee Unique ID | Enter the employee ID, contractor ID, learner ID, or other unique workforce identifier. |
| Job Title / Role | Enter the attendee’s current job title or functional role at the time of training. |
| Department / Team | Enter the attendee’s department, business unit, or team. |
| Employment Type | Enter one allowed value: Employee, Contractor, Temporary Worker, Supplier, Intern, Other. |
| Manager / Approver | Enter the attendee’s line manager or responsible approver for competence and training requirements. |
| Attendance Status | Enter one allowed value: Attended, Completed Online, Assigned Not Started, In Progress, Absent, Cancelled, Exempted. |
| Completion Date | Enter the date the attendee completed the training in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank if not completed. |
| Assessment Required | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether a test, quiz, observation, exercise evaluation, or other assessment was required. |
| Assessment Method | Enter the method used to assess competence, e.g. Quiz, Practical Exercise, Manager Observation, Simulation, Interview, Attendance Only, Not Applicable. |
| Score / Result | Enter the score or outcome achieved, including units where applicable, e.g. 85%, 18/20, Satisfactory, Completed; use Not Applicable if no assessment was required. |
| Pass Mark | Enter the required pass threshold or acceptance criterion, e.g. 80%, 16/20, Satisfactory; use Not Applicable if no assessment was required. |
| Pass / Fail Status | Enter one allowed value: Pass, Fail, Not Applicable, Pending. |
| Competence Achieved | Enter Yes, No, or Pending to indicate whether the required competence has been demonstrated based on completion and assessment results. |
| Retraining Required | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether further training is required due to failure, absence, role change, expired competence, or management decision. |
| Retraining Due Date | Enter the required retraining deadline in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank if retraining is not required. |
| Certificate / Evidence Reference | Enter the certificate number, LMS completion ID, attendance sheet reference, assessment record ID, or other evidence identifier. |
| Record Location / Link | Enter the file path, SharePoint/Teams link, LMS URL, HRIS reference, or document repository location where supporting evidence is stored. |
| Trainer / Assessor Name | Enter the name of the trainer, facilitator, assessor, or system that delivered or assessed the training. |
| Trainer / Assessor Competence Evidence | Enter a brief reference confirming the trainer/assessor is competent, e.g. qualification, certification, role experience, approved trainer list reference, or Not Applicable for automated LMS content. |
| Notes / Exceptions | Enter any relevant exception, exemption reason, late completion note, accessibility adjustment, or management decision; leave blank if none. |
| Record Created Date | Enter the date this record was first created in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Record Last Updated Date | Enter the date this record was last updated in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Record Owner | Enter the role accountable for maintaining this record, e.g. HR Learning Manager, ISMS Manager, Security Awareness Lead. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the HR Learning Manager with oversight from the ISMS Manager or Security Awareness Lead. Update after each training event or LMS completion import, review at least monthly, and draw source data from the LMS, HRIS, attendance sheets, assessment results, certificates, and the ISMS competence/training matrix.

field_guidance.Score / Result: Enter the score or outcome achieved, including units where applicable, e.g. 85%, 18/20, Satisfactory, Completed; use Not Applicable if no assessment was required.
field_guidance.Pass Mark: Enter the required pass threshold or acceptance criterion, e.g. 80%, 16/20, Satisfactory; use Not Applicable if no assessment was required.
field_guidance.Pass / Fail Status: Enter one allowed value: Pass, Fail, Not Applicable, Pending.
field_guidance.Competence Achieved: Enter Yes, No, or Pending to indicate whether the required competence has been demonstrated based on completion and assessment results.
field_guidance.Retraining Required: Enter Yes or No to indicate whether further training is required due to failure, absence, role change, expired competence, or management decision.
field_guidance.Retraining Due Date: Enter the required retraining deadline in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank if retraining is not required.
field_guidance.Certificate / Evidence Reference: Enter the certificate number, LMS completion ID, attendance sheet reference, assessment record ID, or other evidence identifier.
field_guidance.Record Location / Link: Enter the file path, SharePoint/Teams link, LMS URL, HRIS reference, or document repository location where supporting evidence is stored.
field_guidance.Trainer / Assessor Name: Enter the name of the trainer, facilitator, assessor, or system that delivered or assessed the training.
field_guidance.Trainer / Assessor Competence Evidence: Enter a brief reference confirming the trainer/assessor is competent, e.g. qualification, certification, role experience, approved trainer list reference, or Not Applicable for automated LMS content.
field_guidance.Notes / Exceptions: Enter any relevant exception, exemption reason, late completion note, accessibility adjustment, or management decision; leave blank if none.
field_guidance.Record Created Date: Enter the date this record was first created in YYYY-MM-DD format.
field_guidance.Record Last Updated Date: Enter the date this record was last updated in YYYY-MM-DD format.
field_guidance.Record Owner: Enter the role accountable for maintaining this record, e.g. HR Learning Manager, ISMS Manager, Security Awareness Lead.

example_rows: [EXAMPLE: Understand security responsibilities, phishing reporting, acceptable use, and incident reporting obligations]
[EXAMPLE: Approved LMS course reviewed by ISMS Manager]
[EXAMPLE: Apply secure coding practices and identify common web application vulnerabilities]
[EXAMPLE: Trainer CV and secure coding certification on approved trainer register]
table.maintenance: Owned by the HR Learning Manager with oversight from the ISMS Manager or Security Awareness Lead. Update after each training event or LMS completion import, review at least monthly, and draw source data from the LMS, HRIS, attendance sheets, assessment results, certificates, and the ISMS competence/training matrix.

ISO27-030.title: Awareness Programme Materials
ISO27-030.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Control Reference | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Document ID] | 1.0 | [Information Security / GRC Owner] | [Effective Date] | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 | Annex A.6.3 — Information Security Awareness, Education and Training | Internal |

## Purpose

This template is used to plan, document, approve, deliver, and retain evidence of information security awareness programme materials supporting ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A.6.3.

Annex A.6.3 requires personnel and relevant interested parties to receive appropriate information security awareness, education, and training, including updates to organisational policies, topic-specific guidance, and responsibilities relevant to their roles. This template provides a consistent format for creating and evidencing awareness materials such as:

- Slide decks and training modules
- Posters, intranet content, email campaigns, and newsletters
- Phishing simulation notices, test scenarios, and learning materials
- Role-based awareness content for privileged users, managers, developers, contractors, and other relevant groups
- Refresher communications following incidents, audit findings, risk assessments, or policy changes

The completed form supports audit evidence by showing that awareness content is planned, relevant, approved, delivered, measured, and retained.

## Instructions

1. Complete this template for each awareness material, campaign, training module, poster set, phishing simulation, or awareness communication package.
2. Use one form per distinct awareness item or campaign. For example:
   - One form for the annual mandatory security awareness training deck.
   - One form for a phishing simulation campaign.
   - One form for a poster campaign on reporting suspicious emails.
3. Ensure the material aligns to applicable information security policies, acceptable use rules, incident reporting expectations, data protection requirements, and role-specific security responsibilities.
4. Identify the intended audience clearly, including whether the material applies to:
   - All personnel
   - Employees only
   - Contractors or temporary workers
   - Privileged users
   - Developers or technical teams
   - Managers
   - Third-party users with access to organisational information or systems
5. Include measurable learning or awareness objectives where practical.
6. Obtain approval before publication, delivery, or launch, especially for phishing simulations and organisation-wide communications.
7. Ensure phishing tests are ethically designed, lawful, proportionate, and approved by relevant stakeholders before execution.
8. Attach or reference the actual awareness materials, such as slide decks, posters, emails, landing pages, LMS modules, intranet articles, screenshots, or phishing templates.
9. After delivery, update the completion and effectiveness fields with evidence such as attendance, completion rates, quiz results, phishing click rates, reporting rates, feedback, and remediation actions.
10. Retain the completed form and supporting evidence in the approved records repository.

## Form Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Guidance |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Awareness Material ID | Text | Yes | Unique identifier for the material or campaign, such as `AW-2025-001`. |
| Material / Campaign Title | Text | Yes | Name of the awareness item, such as “Annual Security Awareness Training”, “Recognising Phishing Emails”, or “Secure Remote Working Poster Campaign”. |
| Material Type | Select | Yes | Select one or more: Slide Deck, LMS Module, Poster, Email Campaign, Newsletter, Intranet Article, Phishing Simulation, Workshop, Video, Quick Reference Guide, Role-Based Training, Other. |
| Description / Summary | Long text | Yes | Briefly describe the content, purpose, and expected outcome of the material. |
| ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Control Mapping | Text | Yes | Default: Annex A.6.3 — Information Security Awareness, Education and Training. Include additional relevant controls where applicable, such as A.5.10, A.5.12, A.5.14, A.5.15, A.5.16, A.5.24, A.5.26, A.8.7, A.8.12, or A.8.24. |
| Related Policy / Standard / Procedure | Text / Links | Yes | Reference applicable internal documents, such as Information Security Policy, Acceptable Use Policy, Access Control Policy, Incident Management Procedure, Data Classification Standard, Remote Working Standard, Secure Development Standard, or Privacy Policy. |
| Awareness Objective(s) | Long text | Yes | State what the audience should understand or do after receiving the material. Objectives should be specific and action-oriented. Example: “Personnel can identify common phishing indicators and report suspicious emails using [reporting mechanism].” |
| Target Audience | Multi-select / Text | Yes | Define audience groups. Examples: All Personnel, New Joiners, Contractors, Privileged Users, Developers, Service Desk, Finance Team, HR Team, Executives, Third Parties. |
| Audience Size / Population | Number / Text | No | State the estimated or actual number of recipients, learners, or test subjects. |
| Delivery Method | Select / Text | Yes | Select or describe delivery channel: LMS, classroom, virtual session, intranet, email, collaboration platform, posters in office, screensavers, phishing simulation platform, team briefing, onboarding workflow. |
| Delivery Frequency | Select | Yes | Select: One-Time, Onboarding, Annual, Quarterly, Monthly, Event-Driven, Policy-Change-Driven, Incident-Driven, Risk-Driven, Other. |
| Planned Delivery Date / Period | Date / Date range | Yes | Planned date or campaign period for delivery, publication, or simulation launch. |
| Actual Delivery Date / Period | Date / Date range | No | Complete after delivery. Record actual delivery, publication, or launch date. |
| Campaign Owner | Name / Role | Yes | Person accountable for preparation and delivery of the material. Usually Information Security, GRC, HR Learning & Development, or Communications. |
| Content Author | Name / Role | Yes | Person or team responsible for drafting the material. |
| Subject Matter Reviewer | Name / Role | Yes | Reviewer responsible for technical and policy accuracy. |
| Legal / Privacy Reviewer | Name / Role | Conditional | Required where material involves personal data, monitoring, phishing simulation, disciplinary implications, external communications, or regulated topics. |
| HR / Learning Reviewer | Name / Role | Conditional | Required for mandatory training, onboarding, learning management system content, or people-management implications. |
| Communications Reviewer | Name / Role | Conditional | Required for broad communications, posters, branded campaigns, intranet publication, or executive messaging. |
| Approval Authority | Name / Role | Yes | Person authorised to approve release, such as CISO, Information Security Manager, Head of GRC, HR Learning Lead, or designated control owner. |
| Content Version | Text | Yes | Version of the awareness material, such as `v1.0`. Update when content is materially changed. |
| Content Location / Link | URL / Repository path | Yes | Link to the approved slide deck, poster files, LMS module, email copy, phishing template, landing page, screenshots, or campaign package. |
| Classification of Material | Select | Yes | Select: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted. Most internal awareness material should be Internal unless it includes sensitive details such as phishing test design or incident specifics. |
| Sensitive Content Included | Yes/No | Yes | Indicate whether the material includes sensitive examples, internal system names, simulated attacks, incident details, personal data, or restricted operational information. |
| Accessibility and Inclusion Check Completed | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm content is reasonably accessible, legible, understandable, and appropriate for the audience. Consider language, readability, alternative text, captions, and colour contrast where applicable. |
| Localisation / Language Requirements | Text | No | Identify translations or regional adaptations required for the target audience. |
| Mandatory Completion Required | Yes/No | Yes | State whether completion is mandatory. Mandatory training should have defined due dates and escalation rules. |
| Completion Due Date | Date | Conditional | Required if mandatory completion is required. |
| Completion Tracking Method | Select / Text | Conditional | Required for mandatory or measurable campaigns. Examples: LMS report, attendance register, HR system, email analytics, phishing platform report, acknowledgement form. |
| Assessment Method | Select / Text | No | Examples: Quiz, knowledge check, phishing simulation metrics, acknowledgement, manager confirmation, attendance, practical exercise, no assessment. |
| Pass Mark / Success Criteria | Text | Conditional | Required where an assessment is used. Example: “80% quiz score” or “Phishing reporting rate greater than click rate.” |
| Reinforcement / Remediation Approach | Long text | No | Describe follow-up for non-completion, failed assessments, repeat phishing clickers, or low-awareness teams. Include coaching, reminder communications, refresher training, or manager escalation. |
| Key Messages | Long text | Yes | Summarise the primary messages. Example: “Report suspicious emails immediately; do not reuse passwords; protect confidential information; follow clear desk and screen locking requirements.” |
| Behaviour Expected from Audience | Long text | Yes | State the required actions or behaviours. Example: “Use [reporting mechanism] to report suspected phishing; classify documents before sharing; complete mandatory training by the due date.” |
| Incident Reporting Instructions Included | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm the material tells personnel how and where to report suspected information security events or weaknesses. |
| Policy Responsibilities Included | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm the material references personnel responsibilities under applicable information security policies and acceptable use requirements. |
| Role-Based Content Included | Yes/No | Yes | Indicate whether the material includes tailored content based on job function or access level. |
| Trigger for Material | Select / Text | Yes | Select or describe trigger: Annual Programme, New Joiner Onboarding, Policy Update, New Risk, Security Incident, Audit Finding, Regulatory Requirement, Seasonal Threat, Phishing Trend, Technology Change, Other. |
| Threat / Risk Topic Covered | Multi-select / Text | Yes | Examples: phishing, social engineering, malware, ransomware, password security, MFA, data handling, clean desk, remote working, mobile device security, cloud usage, secure development, supplier security, incident reporting, privacy, physical security. |
| Supporting Evidence Required | Checklist / Text | Yes | Identify evidence to retain, such as approved deck, poster PDF, email copy, LMS report, attendance register, phishing report, screenshots, quiz results, approval record, communications plan. |
| Delivery Status | Select | Yes | Select: Draft, Under Review, Approved, Scheduled, Delivered, Cancelled, Superseded. |
| Effectiveness Metrics | Long text | No | Complete after delivery. Include measurable results such as completion rate, average quiz score, phishing click rate, phishing report rate, attendance rate, acknowledgement rate, user feedback score, or incident trend impact. |
| Lessons Learned / Improvement Actions | Long text | No | Record improvements for future awareness activities, such as simplifying content, targeting high-risk groups, improving reporting instructions, or changing delivery frequency. |
| Exceptions / Deviations | Long text | No | Record any deviations from planned delivery, audience, approval, or tracking, including justification and compensating actions. |
| Next Review Date | Date | Yes | Date the content must be reviewed for accuracy and continued relevance. At minimum, review annually or after major policy, threat, legal, organisational, or technology changes. |
| Superseded By | Text / Link | No | Complete when the material is replaced by a newer version or campaign. |
| Record Owner | Name / Role | Yes | Person accountable for maintaining this completed form and associated evidence. |

### Awareness Material Planning Checklist

| Checklist Item | Yes/No/NA | Evidence / Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Material addresses information security responsibilities relevant to the target audience. |  |  |
| Material aligns with current approved information security policies and procedures. |  |  |
| Material includes clear instructions for reporting suspected information security events or weaknesses. |  |  |
| Material is appropriate to the audience’s role, access level, and risk exposure. |  |  |
| Mandatory completion requirements, due dates, and escalation paths are defined where applicable. |  |  |
| Content has been reviewed for technical accuracy. |  |  |
| Content has been reviewed for legal, privacy, or HR considerations where applicable. |  |  |
| Content has been approved before release. |  |  |
| Evidence of delivery and completion will be captured. |  |  |
| Effectiveness metrics have been defined. |  |  |
| Accessibility, readability, and language needs have been considered. |  |  |
| Review date and record owner have been assigned. |  |  |

### Example Awareness Content Register

| Material ID | Title | Type | Audience | Frequency | Owner | Status | Evidence Location |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AW-2025-001 | Annual Information Security Awareness Training | LMS Module / Slide Deck | All Personnel | Annual | Information Security | Approved | [Repository link] |
| AW-2025-002 | Report Phishing Fast | Poster / Email Campaign | All Personnel | Quarterly | Security Awareness Lead | Scheduled | [Repository link] |
| AW-2025-003 | Privileged Access Responsibilities | Role-Based Training | Administrators / Privileged Users | Annual | IAM Owner | Draft | [Repository link] |
| AW-2025-004 | Secure Coding Refresher | Workshop / Slide Deck | Developers | Semi-Annual | Application Security Lead | Delivered | [Repository link] |
| AW-2025-005 | Phishing Simulation Q2 | Phishing Simulation | Selected Personnel | Quarterly | Security Operations | Under Review | [Repository link] |

### Phishing Simulation-Specific Fields

Complete this section where the material or campaign includes a phishing test, simulation, or social engineering exercise.

| Field | Type | Required | Guidance |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Simulation ID | Text | Yes | Unique identifier for the phishing simulation, such as `PHISH-2025-Q2`. |
| Simulation Objective | Long text | Yes | Define the learning and measurement objective. Example: “Assess recognition and reporting of credential-harvesting phishing emails.” |
| Target Group Selection Method | Long text | Yes | Describe how participants are selected. Ensure selection is risk-based, fair, proportionate, and approved. |
| Number of Recipients | Number | Yes | Planned number of recipients in scope. |
| Scenario Theme | Text | Yes | Describe the scenario theme without including unnecessary sensitive detail. Example: “Fake document share notification” or “Benefits update”. |
| Risk Level of Simulation | Select | Yes | Select: Low, Medium, High. High-risk simulations require additional approval and privacy/HR review. |
| Use of Credentials / Data Capture | Select | Yes | Select: No Capture, Username Only, Simulated Entry Only, Other. Avoid collecting real passwords or unnecessary personal data. |
| Landing Page Message | Text / Link | Yes | Link to or describe the educational landing page shown after interaction. It should provide immediate, constructive learning. |
| Reporting Mechanism Tested | Text | Yes | Identify reporting route tested, such as phishing report button, service desk ticket, security mailbox, or hotline. |
| Pre-Notification Approach | Text | No | Describe whether general awareness or campaign notice is provided, without compromising test validity. |
| Success Metrics | Long text | Yes | Examples: delivery rate, open rate, click rate, credential submission rate, report rate, time to report, repeat click rate. |
| Remediation Plan | Long text | Yes | Describe follow-up training, coaching, or communications for individuals or groups needing improvement. |
| Privacy Impact Considered | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm that personal data processing, monitoring, reporting, and retention have been considered. |
| HR / Employee Relations Review Completed | Yes/No/NA | Yes | Required where individual-level results may be used for follow-up, escalation, or performance-related actions. |
| Executive / Senior Approval Obtained | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm senior approval before launch. |
| Simulation Launch Window | Date range | Yes | Planned launch window. Avoid critical business periods unless explicitly approved. |
| Actual Simulation Completion Date | Date | No | Complete after simulation. |
| Results Report Location | URL / Repository path | No | Link to final simulation report and lessons learned. |

### Delivery and Effectiveness Log

| Date | Activity | Audience / Group | Delivery Channel | Evidence Captured | Result / Metric | Follow-Up Required |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Date] | [Training delivered / poster published / phishing launched] | [Audience] | [Channel] | [Evidence] | [Metric] | [Yes/No and action] |

## Approval / Routing

The completed template and associated awareness materials must be routed for review and approval before publication, training delivery, or campaign launch.

| Stage | Reviewer / Approver | Required When | Approval Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Content Author Review | Content Author | All materials | Draft version and author confirmation |
| Information Security Review | Information Security Manager / Control Owner | All materials mapped to A.6.3 | Review comments, approval workflow, or signed approval |
| Policy / GRC Review | GRC Owner or Policy Owner | Materials referencing policies, audit requirements, or ISO/IEC 27001 obligations | Review record or approval ticket |
| Technical SME Review | Relevant SME | Technical, role-based, secure development, cloud, access control, or incident response content | Review comments or approval |
| HR / Learning & Development Review | HR / L&D Representative | Mandatory training, onboarding, personnel records, non-completion escalation, employee communications | LMS approval, HR sign-off, or workflow approval |
| Legal / Privacy Review | Legal / Privacy Representative | Phishing simulations, monitoring, personal data, regulated content, or sensitive investigations | Legal/privacy approval or DPIA reference where applicable |
| Communications / Brand Review | Communications Representative | Posters, intranet content, executive messages, broad campaigns | Communications approval |
| Senior Management Approval | CISO / Security Steering Committee / Executive Sponsor | Organisation-wide campaigns, phishing simulations, high-risk awareness activities, or campaigns with business impact | Approval minutes, workflow approval, or signed authorisation |

Approval record:

| Approval Role | Name | Decision | Date | Comments |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Content Author | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Changes Required | [Date] | [Comments] |
| Information Security Reviewer | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Changes Required | [Date] | [Comments] |
| GRC / Policy Reviewer | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Changes Required | [Date] | [Comments] |
| HR / L&D Reviewer | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Changes Required / Not Applicable | [Date] | [Comments] |
| Legal / Privacy Reviewer | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Changes Required / Not Applicable | [Date] | [Comments] |
| Communications Reviewer | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Changes Required / Not Applicable | [Date] | [Comments] |
| Final Approver | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Changes Required | [Date] | [Comments] |

## Records & Retention

Completed awareness programme material forms and associated evidence must be retained as controlled information security management system records.

Records should demonstrate that information security awareness, education, and training were planned, approved, delivered, and evaluated in accordance with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A.6.3.

| Record Type | Examples | Retention Requirement | Record Location | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Completed Awareness Programme Materials Form | This completed template, approval records, routing history | Minimum 3 years or longer if required by legal, regulatory, contractual, or audit obligations | [Records repository / GRC system] | [Record Owner] |
| Approved Awareness Content | Slide decks, LMS modules, posters, email copy, newsletters, intranet screenshots, videos, quick reference guides | Retain current version plus prior versions for minimum 3 years | [Content repository / LMS / intranet archive] | [Information Security / L&D Owner] |
| Training Delivery Evidence | Attendance registers, LMS completion reports, acknowledgements, webinar logs, onboarding completion records | Minimum 3 years | [LMS / HR system / records repository] | [HR / L&D Owner] |
| Assessment Evidence | Quiz results, pass/fail records, knowledge check summaries, completion certificates | Minimum 3 years | [LMS / records repository] | [HR / L&D Owner] |
| Phishing Simulation Evidence | Approved simulation plan, email templates, landing page screenshots, campaign metrics, results report, remediation records | Minimum 3 years, subject to privacy and employment law requirements | [Phishing platform / records repository] | [Security Operations / Awareness Owner] |
| Effectiveness and Improvement Records | Metrics dashboards, lessons learned, improvement actions, management reporting | Minimum 3 years | [GRC system / records repository] | [GRC Owner] |
| Review and Supersession Records | Review notes, version history, superseded materials, change approvals | Minimum 3 years after supersession | [Document management system] | [Document Owner] |

Retention and handling requirements:

- Store records in an approved repository with access restricted to authorised roles.
- Protect individual-level training, assessment, and phishing simulation results as confidential personnel-related information.
- Do not retain real passwords, unnecessary personal data, or excessive behavioural monitoring data.
- Ensure records are available for internal audit, external audit, management review, and certification assessment.
- Dispose of records securely after the approved retention period, subject to legal hold, investigation, regulatory, contractual, or audit requirements.
- Review awareness materials at least annually and whenever significant changes occur to threats, policies, technology, legal obligations, organisational context, or incident trends.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Review ID | Enter a unique identifier for this access review cycle or review record, e.g. AR-YYYY-Q#-SYSTEM or AR-YYYY-MM-###. |
| Review Period | Enter the period covered by the review in YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD format. |

| System / Application / Repository | Enter the exact name of the system, application, database, cloud platform, file share, code repository, or other access-controlled asset being reviewed. |

| User Full Name | Enter the full legal or HR-recorded name of the individual whose access is being reviewed. |

| Last Login Date | Enter the most recent successful login or use date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter Never if no login is recorded, or Unknown if the source does not provide it. |
| Access Granted Date | Enter the date the access was originally granted in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter Unknown if not available. |
| Previous Review Decision | Enter the outcome from the prior review for this same access, if available; allowed values: Retain, Remove, Modify, Exception, Not Previously Reviewed, Unknown. |
| Reviewer Decision | Enter the review decision using one allowed value: Retain, Remove, Modify, Suspend, Investigate, Exception Required. |
| Decision Rationale | Enter a concise explanation supporting the reviewer decision, including why access remains appropriate or why change/removal is required. |
| Remediation Required | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether any access change, removal, suspension, or investigation is required. |
| Remediation Action | If remediation is required, enter the specific action to be taken, e.g. remove group membership, downgrade role, disable account, confirm with manager; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Remediation Owner | Enter the person or team responsible for completing the remediation action, e.g. IAM Team, Service Desk, System Administrator, Application Owner. |
| Remediation Due Date | Enter the target completion date for remediation in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no remediation is required. |
| Remediation Completion Date | Enter the actual date remediation was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no remediation is required or Pending if not yet complete. |
| Remediation Ticket / Change Reference | Enter the ticket, change, request, or workflow reference used to evidence the remediation; enter N/A if no remediation is required. |
| Post-Remediation Status | Enter one allowed value: Not Required, Pending, Completed, Overdue, Failed, Risk Accepted. |
| Exception Approved | Enter Yes, No, or N/A to indicate whether an exception to normal access policy was formally approved. |
| Exception Reference | If an exception exists, enter the risk acceptance, exception, or approval reference; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Evidence Location | Enter the controlled location or link where evidence is stored, such as review export, signed approval, ticket, screenshot, IAM report, or GRC record. |
| Reviewer Sign-off Date | Enter the date the reviewer completed and signed off the review in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Approver | Enter the person providing final approval or oversight of the access review, if required by procedure; use full name and role, or N/A. |
| Approver Sign-off Date | Enter the final approval date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if not required. |
| Comments | Enter any additional relevant notes, constraints, anomalies, or follow-up information; do not include unnecessary personal data. |

### Maintenance

This template is owned by the Information Security Manager or IAM/GRC process owner, with review input from system owners and business data owners. It is updated at least annually and whenever access review procedures, systems, roles, or IAM sources change; records should be drawn from authoritative IAM directories, HR records, application entitlement exports, privileged access management tools, and service desk/change management systems.

field_guidance.Review ID: Enter a unique identifier for this access review cycle or review record, e.g. AR-YYYY-Q#-SYSTEM or AR-YYYY-MM-###.
field_guidance.Review Period: Enter the period covered by the review in YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD format.
field_guidance.Review Date: Enter the date the access review was performed in YYYY-MM-DD format.
field_guidance.System / Application / Repository: Enter the exact name of the system, application, database, cloud platform, file share, code repository, or other access-controlled asset being reviewed.
field_guidance.System Owner: Enter the accountable business or technical owner of the system, using full name and/or role title.
field_guidance.Access Reviewer: Enter the person performing the review, normally the system owner, data owner, application owner, or delegated manager; use full name and role.
field_guidance.User Full Name: Enter the full legal or HR-recorded name of the individual whose access is being reviewed.
field_guidance.User ID / Account Name: Enter the unique account identifier as shown in the source system, directory, IAM platform, or application.
field_guidance.User Email: Enter the user's corporate email address, or N/A for non-person accounts.
field_guidance.Department / Business Unit: Enter the user's current department, team, or business unit according to HR or identity records.
field_guidance.Line Manager: Enter the user's current line manager according to HR records; use full name.
field_guidance.Employment Status: Enter one allowed value: Active, Leaver, Suspended, Contractor Active, Contractor Ended, Transferred, Unknown.
field_guidance.Account Type: Enter one allowed value: Named User, Privileged Admin, Service Account, Shared Account, Break-glass, Third-party, System Account.
field_guidance.Access Role / Group / Permission: Enter the specific role, group, permission set, profile, entitlement, access level, or membership being reviewed exactly as named in the source system.
field_guidance.Privilege Level: Enter one allowed value: Standard, Elevated, Privileged, Administrative, Read-only, Service, Unknown.
field_guidance.Access Purpose / Business Justification: Enter the business reason the access is required, tied to job role, responsibility, support need, or approved service operation.
field_guidance.Access Source: Enter where the access record was obtained from, e.g. Active Directory, Entra ID, Okta, SAP, AWS IAM, GitHub, application export, database query.
field_guidance.Last Login Date: Enter the most recent successful login or use date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter Never if no login is recorded, or Unknown if the source does not provide it.
field_guidance.Access Granted Date: Enter the date the access was originally granted in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter Unknown if not available.
field_guidance.Previous Review Decision: Enter the outcome from the prior review for this same access, if available; allowed values: Retain, Remove, Modify, Exception, Not Previously Reviewed, Unknown.
field_guidance.Reviewer Decision: Enter the review decision using one allowed value: Retain, Remove, Modify, Suspend, Investigate, Exception Required.
field_guidance.Decision Rationale: Enter a concise explanation supporting the reviewer decision, including why access remains appropriate or why change/removal is required.
field_guidance.Remediation Required: Enter Yes or No to indicate whether any access change, removal, suspension, or investigation is required.
field_guidance.Remediation Action: If remediation is required, enter the specific action to be taken, e.g. remove group membership, downgrade role, disable account, confirm with manager; otherwise enter N/A.
field_guidance.Remediation Owner: Enter the person or team responsible for completing the remediation action, e.g. IAM Team, Service Desk, System Administrator, Application Owner.
field_guidance.Remediation Due Date: Enter the target completion date for remediation in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no remediation is required.
field_guidance.Remediation Completion Date: Enter the actual date remediation was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no remediation is required or Pending if not yet complete.
field_guidance.Remediation Ticket / Change Reference: Enter the ticket, change, request, or workflow reference used to evidence the remediation; enter N/A if no remediation is required.
field_guidance.Post-Remediation Status: Enter one allowed value: Not Required, Pending, Completed, Overdue, Failed, Risk Accepted.
field_guidance.Exception Approved: Enter Yes, No, or N/A to indicate whether an exception to normal access policy was formally approved.
field_guidance.Exception Reference: If an exception exists, enter the risk acceptance, exception, or approval reference; otherwise enter N/A.
field_guidance.Evidence Location: Enter the controlled location or link where evidence is stored, such as review export, signed approval, ticket, screenshot, IAM report, or GRC record.
field_guidance.Reviewer Sign-off Date: Enter the date the reviewer completed and signed off the review in YYYY-MM-DD format.
field_guidance.Approver: Enter the person providing final approval or oversight of the access review, if required by procedure; use full name and role, or N/A.
field_guidance.Approver Sign-off Date: Enter the final approval date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if not required.
field_guidance.Comments: Enter any additional relevant notes, constraints, anomalies, or follow-up information; do not include unnecessary personal data.
